de dag gis bstan pa ni de dag gis bśad pa ste, raṅ gi lta ba mchog tu ’dzin pa btaṅ nas
ṅa rgyal med par byas te, ji skad bstan pa bźin du ñan pa ni gźan gyis bstan pa ñan pa źes
bya’o.chos ma thos pa ni mu stegs can la sogs pa ’di las phyi rol ba’i bstan pa la med pa,
phuṅ po daṅ skye mched la sogs pa mdo’i sde las gsuṅs par bstan pa gaṅ yin pa, ’khor ba
thog ma med pa nas lan ’ga’ yaṅ ma thos pa de daṅ thos par gyur pas na thos pa ni chos ma
thos pa ñan pa’i rnam pa źes bya’o.mṅon par śes pa ni drug ste, de dag ni de dag ñid kyi
skabs nas ’chad do.theg pa gźan ñan thos kyi theg pa daṅ, raṅ saṅs rgyas kyi theg pa daṅ,
lha’i theg pa daṅ, mi’i theg pa dag ste, de dag ñan kyaṅ chags par mi byed pas na ’dod pa
med pa źes bya’o.pha rol tu phyin pa ni sbyin pa mi zad pa la sogs pa drug po ’di dag go.
de la pha rol tu phyin pa’i sgra ni mchog gi don te, rgyu mchog daṅ las mchog daṅ ’bras bu
mchog gi phyir pha rol tu phyin pa źes bya’o. de la rgyu mchog ni pha rol tu phyin pa de
dag ñid goṅ nas goṅ du khyad źugs pa’i ye śes kyi rgyur ’gyur ba’i phyir ro; las mchog ni
bdag daṅ gźan la phan ’dogs par byed pa’i phyir ro; ’bras bu mchog ni bla na med pa’i byaṅ
chub yin pa’i phyir ro. yaṅ na, rgyu mchog ni sñiṅ rje chen po’i rgyu las byuṅ ba’i phyir
ro.byaṅ chub sems dpa’i sde snod ni goṅ du gsuṅ rab yan lag bcu gñis smos pa’i naṅ nas śin
tu rgyas pa’i sde gaṅ yin pa’o. According to ṭ, the word bodhisattvapiṭaka refers to the
whole canon of scriptures as described supra, to the teachings of the bodhisattvas generally.
On the connection, however, of Akṣ and the individual sūtra named Bodhisattvapiṭaka,
v. introduction.bsdu ba’i dṅos po źes bya ba ni sems can dga’ bar byed pa’i dṅos po źes bya
ba’i tha tshig ste, de yaṅ sbyin pa la sogs pa bsdu ba’i dṅos po bźi ñid kyi skabs nas ’chad
do.thabs mkhas pa ni dge ba’i rtsa ba chuṅ ṅu yaṅ dpag tu med par ’gyur bar byed pa daṅ,
sems can bstan pa ’di la ma źugs pa rnams bstan pa la gzud pa daṅ, źugs pa rnams dge ba’i
rtsa ba ’phel bar bya ba daṅ, dge ba’i rtsa ba ’phel ba rnams yoṅs su smin par bya ba
daṅ, yoṅs su smin pa rnams rnam par grol bar bya ste, de ñan par byed pas na thabs la mkhas
pa ñan pa’i rnam pa źes bya’o.tshaṅs pa ni sdig pa thams cad spaṅs pa’i mya ṅan las ’das
pa la bya ste, mdo las kyaṅ: tshaṅs par gyur bsil bar gyur, ces gsuṅs pa’i phyir ro. de’i
gnas pa ni thob par byed pa’i rgyu la bya ste, de yaṅ byams pa la sogs pa tshad med pa bźi
ñid kyi skabs nas ’chad do.dran pa ni sems can gyi don bya ba la brtson pa’i byaṅ chub sems
dpa’ bya ba daṅ mi bya bar śes śiṅ dran pa’o, śes bźin ni chos thams cad sgyu ma daṅ smig
rgyu lta bur dṅos po med par śes pa’o.skye ba la mkhas pa ni phyi daṅ naṅ gi rten ciṅ
’brel bar ’byuṅ ba’i chos rnams rgyu gaṅ las ’bras bu gaṅ skye ba śes pa ste, ’di ltar phyi’i
rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba ni sa bon gyi rkyen gyis myu gu źes bya ba nas me tog gi rkyen
gyis ’bras bu źes bya ba’i bar daṅ, naṅ gi rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba yaṅ ma rig pa’i
rkyen gyis ’du byed rnams śes bya ba nas skye ba’i rkyen gyis rga śi źes bya ba’i bar du
phyi daṅ naṅ gi chos rnams rgyu daṅ rkyen las skye’i, bdag daṅ byed pa po las skye ba ma
yin par rtogs pa’o.mi skye ba la mkhas pa ni gzuṅ ba daṅ ’dzin pa las dben pa’i don dam pa
yoṅs su grub pa’i mtshan ñid ji lta ba bźin du śes pa ste, de ñan pa’o – "Skill concerning
the unoriginated is knowledge of the highest meaning (paramārtha) beyond subject and object
(grāhyagrāhakavivikta) characterized as completed (pariniṣpannalakṣaṇa) as it really is
(yathābhūtajñāna), it is listening to that."mi sdug pa daṅ, byams pa daṅ, rten ciṅ ’brel
bar ’byuṅ ba’i rnam pa źes bya ba’i tshig gsum gyis ’dod chags daṅ źe sdaṅ daṅ gti mug gsum
gyi gñen po mi sdug pa bsgom pa la sogs pa rnam pa gsum yaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ bar ston
to. de la mi sdug pa ni ’dod chags kyi gñen po ste, de bas na mdo las kyaṅ: dge sloṅ rnal
’byor bas śi nas dur khrod du bor ba’i ro źag gcig lon pa źes bya ba nas khyi daṅ bya rgod
daṅ ’phar ba la sogs pas zos pa yid la gzuṅ bar bya ste, źes gsuṅs pa’i phyir ro. byams pa
ni źe sdaṅ gi gñen po ste, de bas na mdo sde las kyaṅ: byams pa daṅ ldan pa’i sems khon
med pa, ’gran zla med pa, gnod pa med pas phyogs bcur mos te, khyab par byas te bsgrubs te
gnas so, źes gsuṅs pa’i phyir ro. rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba ni gti mug gi gñen po ste,
de bas na mdo las kyaṅ: rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba gaṅ źe na? gaṅ dus gsum gyi chos rnams
la ’du byed tsam daṅ, chos tsam daṅ, dṅos po tsam daṅ, rgyu tsam daṅ, ’bras bu tsam ste,
byed pa po med pa de ni rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba źes bya ste, gaṅ gi tshe de yid la byas
na gti mug śas6 che ba’i gaṅ zag rnams gti mug bsrabs par ’gyur ro, źes gsuṅs pa’i phyir
ro.mi rtag pa ni dus gsum gyi ’dus byas thams cad skad cig ma re rer ’jig pas gnas pa med
pa ste, de la ’di ltar ’das pa’i ’dus byas rnams ni skyes nas ’gag par snaṅ la, da ltar byuṅ
ba’i ’dus byas rnams ni skyes pa’i skad cig phan chad du gnas pa’i mthu med la, ma ’oṅs
pa’i ’dus byas rnams ni ma skyes la ’gag pa med par snaṅ ba’i phyir ro. de ltar ’dus byas
mi rtag pa’i raṅ bźin de yaṅ sdug bsṅal rnam pa gsum gyi rten byed pas na sdug bsṅal ba
źes bya ste, sdug bsṅal rnam pa gsum ni: 1) ’du byed kyi sdug bsṅal daṅ, 2) ’gyur ba’i sdug
bsṅal daṅ, 3) sdug bsṅal gyi sdug bsṅal te; de la 1) ’du byed kyi sdug bsṅal rgyu daṅ rkyen
gyis bskyed pa’i ’du byed thams cad ni mi rtag pa yin pa’i phyir ro; 2) ’gyur ba’i sdug
bsṅal ni ’byor ba’i loṅs spyod daṅ bde ba’i tshor ba yaṅ phyis med par ’gyur źiṅ ma ’oṅs
pa na rnam par smin pa’i yid du mi ’oṅ ba’i rgyu byed pa’i phyir ro. 3) sdug bsṅal gyi sdug
bsṅal ni skye ba daṅ rga ba daṅ ’chi ba daṅ ’dod pa mi rñed pa daṅ sdug bsṅal gyi tshor
ba rnams raṅ bźin gyis sdug bsṅal ba’i steṅ du nad la sogs pa sdug bsṅal gźan daṅ yaṅ ’brel
ba’i phyir ro. bdag med pa ni ’dus byas daṅ ’dus ma byas kyi chos thams cad med pa ste,
de dag kyaṅ thos pa daṅ ldan pas khoṅ du chud par byed pa’i phyir mi rtag pa’i rnam pa la
sogs pa źes bya’o.źi ba ni ñon moṅs pa thams cad daṅ sdug bsṅal thams cad źi ba’i phyir mya
ṅan las ’das pa la bya’o.stoṅ pa ñid daṅ, mtshan ma med pa daṅ, smon pa med pa źes bya
ba rnam par thar pa’i sgo gsum po de dag gi don ni sṅar bśad zin te, de dag khoṅ du chud pa
yaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ ṅo źes bya bar sbyar ro.mṅon par ’du mi byed pa daṅ dge ba mṅon par
’du byed pa tshig gñis kyis ni srog gcod pa la sogs pa mi dge ba’i las spoṅ ba daṅ, dad
pa daṅ brtson ’grus la sogs pa dge ba mṅon par ’du byed pa yaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ źes ston
to.bden pas byin gyis brlabs pa ni ’phags pa’i bden pa bźi mthoṅ ba’i mthu daṅ ldan par byed
pa ste, bden pa mthoṅ ba’i mthu daṅ ldan par yaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ bas na thos pa ni bden
pas byin gyis brlabs pa’i rnam pa źes bya’o. yaṅ na, mdo dag las byaṅ chub sems dpa’ la
sogs pas raṅ gis dam bcas pa’i bden pa’i tshig gis byin gyis brlabs na de bźin du ’gyur ba
ste, de yaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ źes bya bar sbyar ro. The concept satyavacana is explained
by J. Burlingame in JRAS 1917 pp. 429-67.chud mi gzon pa ni las daṅ las kyi ’bras bu rnam
par smin pa yod par lta ba’o.raṅ gi kha na las pa ni gźan la rag ma lus pa ste, gźan la śes
pa ni rag ma lus par bya ba yaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ ba’i phyir ro; raṅ gi sems sruṅ ba ni
bya ba ma yin pa la mi ’jug par byed pa’o.brtson ’grus ni dge ba mṅon par ’du byed pa la
sems spro ba yin la, de mi gtoṅ ba ni rtag tu byed pa daṅ gus par byed pa’o.chos ṅes par sems
pa ni phuṅ po daṅ khams daṅ skye mched la sogs pa kun nas ñon moṅs pa daṅ rnam par byaṅ
ba’i chos rnams blos gtan la ’bebs pa’o.ji ltar bśad pa’i chos rnams mñan nas rig pas bsams
te, bsgoms na ñon moṅs pa spoṅ bar ’gyur bas ñon moṅs pa’i gñen po’i rnam pa źes bya’o.
One would have expected pratipakṣa for vipakṣa; the two are, however, sometimes confused.raṅ
gi phyogs ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i phyogs te, rnam par byaṅ ba’i chos rnams daṅ, de’i
’khor du gtogs pa’i sems can rnams so. bsruṅ ba ni phyogs de dag gźan gyis mi ’phrogs śiṅ
ñon moṅs pa’i dbaṅ du mi ’gyur bar byed pa’o.pha rol gyi phyogs bdud daṅ mu stegs can la sogs
pa ste, de dag daṅ ñon moṅs pa tshar gcod pa ni de dag mthu med ciṅ ñams smod par byed
pa’o.nor bdun ni 1) dad pa daṅ, 2) tshul khrims daṅ, 3) ṅo tsha śes pa daṅ, 4) khrel yod
pa daṅ, 5) thos pa daṅ, 6) gtoṅ ba daṅ, 7) śes rab kyi nor te, thos pa la de dag ’du bar ’gyur
bas yaṅ dag par ’du ba’i rnam pa źes bya’o. de ltar ’phags pa’i nor bdun po ’phags pa’i
nor ma yin pa’i nor las śin tu khyad źugs pa de dag thos pa la yaṅ dag par ’du ba’i phyir
dbul ba thams cad gcod pa źes bya ste, thos pa ’dis dbul ba thams cad gcod ces bya ba’i
tha tshig go.mdzaṅs pa ni rig pa’i gnas lṅa khoṅ du chud pa’i gaṅ zag ste, thos pa ni ñes
pa thams cad spoṅ ba’i gñen po yin pa daṅ, yon tan mchog rnams thob pa’i rgyu yin pa’i phyir
mdzaṅs pa de dag gis bsṅags pa’i rnam pa źes bya’o. The five vidyāsthāna are śabda-, hetu-,
adhyātma-, cikitsā-, and śilpakarmasthānavidyā, for ref. v. Edg s. v.mkhas pa ni legs
par bsams pa sems pa daṅ, legs par smra ba brjod pa daṅ, legs par bya ba’i las byed pa daṅ,
legs par smras pa daṅ ñes par smras pa’i don khoṅ du chud par nus pa ste, de lta bu dag
thos pa la mos par byed pas mkhas pa la mṅon par dga’ ba’i rnam pa źes bya’o. ’phags pa
ñan thos daṅ, raṅ saṅs rgyas daṅ, de bźin gsegs pa bdag gis kyaṅ thos pa de lta bu thugs su
chud pa’am, thos pa la ’phags pa rnams dgyes pas na thos pa ni ’phags pas kun śes pa’i rnam
pa źes bya’o.’phags pa ma yin pa ni so so’i skye bo ste, thos pa’i śes rab de dag kyaṅ
dam pa’i chos la mos śiṅ dad par byed nus pa’i phyir ’phags pa ma yin pa dad par byed pa’i
rnam pa źes bya’o.thos pa’i śes rab las ’phags pa’i bden pa bźi mthoṅ ba ’byuṅ ba’i phyir
bden pa mthoṅ ba’i rnam pa źes bya’o.zag pa daṅ bcas pa’i phuṅ po’i skyon skye ba daṅ, rga
ba la sogs pa rnam par spaṅs pa’i thabs kyaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ bas na ’di skad ces bya’o.
thos pa’i śes rab kyis ’khor ba’i chos rnams kyi skyon khoṅ du chud par byed pas na ’dus
byas kyi skyon la yoṅs su ’jal ba’i rnam pa źes bya’o.don la rton pa la sogs pa rton pa
bźi po yaṅ thos pa las ’byuṅ źes bya bar sbyar te, de dag gi don ni rton pa bźi’i skabs nas
’chad do.thos pa daṅ ldan na sdig pa mi dge ba’i chos rnams mi byed pas sdig pa thams cad
mi bya ba’i rnam pa źes bya’o.bdag daṅ gźan la phan pa ni bdag daṅ gźan mi dge ba’i gnas
nas bton te, dge ba la ’jog pa’am śes pa’i mthar phyin par byed pa ste, de yaṅ thos pa las
byuṅ źes sbyar ro.thos pa ñid dge ba’i raṅ bźin yin pas legs par byas pa’i las kyi rnam
pa źes bya’o; de ltar legs par byas pas na mi ’gyod pa’i rnam pa ste, dge ba byas pa ni phyis:
’di lta bu ’gyur ro, sñam du sems la gduṅ ba med pa’i phyir ro. Reading these two items
as one ākāra as in T1 p. 196a2-3 and as the Sanskrit version, and thus making up the right
number 84 ākāras altogether, not as in all Tibetan versions, where the two are separate
as two ākāras.khyad par du ’gro ba ni yon tan khyad par can ma thob pa las thob par bya’am;
yaṅ na, mos pa spyod pa’i sa yan chad goṅ nas goṅ du sa rnams gnon pa la bya ste, de yaṅ
thos pa las ’byuṅ bar sbyar ro.saṅs rgyas kyi chos thams cad ni stobs daṅ mi ’jigs pa la
sogs pa ste, mdor na saṅs rgyas kyi chos de dag thams cad kyaṅ thos pa la brten nas ’thob
par ’gyur gyi, de las thabs gźan med pas na saṅs rgyas kyi chos thams cad ’thob pa’i rnam
pa źes bya’o.

śes rab kyi ’jug pa bstan pa’i dbaṅ du byas nas btsun pa śa ra dva ti’i bu, de la byaṅ chub
sems dpa’ rnams kyi tshul bźin yid la byed pa la ’jug pa ni sum cu rtsa gñis te źes bya ba
la sogs pas gsuṅs so. V. also ṭ. fol. 89a1-2.ṭ. fol. 97a7-b4: de la tshul ni ’phags pa’i
lam daṅ mya ṅan las ’das pa la bya’o. de daṅ mthun par sems śiṅ bsgom pa ni tshul bźin yid
la byed pa źes bya ste. tshul bźin yid la byed pa des de kho na ñid kyi don la ’jug ciṅ,
tshul bźin yid la byed pa la ’jug pa źes bya’o. de ltar don la ’jug pa de yaṅ bsam pa’i śes
rab kyis gtan la phab pa’i chos de la bsgom pa’i śes rab kyis goms par byas nas don rtogs
par ’gyur te. de bas na ’di ni bsam pa daṅ bsgom pa’i śes rab yin par rig par bya’o. yaṅ
na, tshul ’di ’phags pa’i lam daṅ mya ṅan las ’das pa’am, mṅon sum daṅ rjes su dpag pa la
sogs pa’i rigs pa’am, ma nor bar ston pa’i mkhan po daṅ slob dpon gyi man ṅag la bya ste,
de daṅ mi ’gal bar yid la byed pa ni tshul bźin yid la byed pa źes bya’o. tshul bźin yid
la byed pa de la ’jug pas na tshul bźin yid la byed pa la ’jug pa ste. ’jug pa ni tshul bźin
yid la byed pa la gnas pa’am, tshul bźin yid la byed pa de dag gis raṅ bźin daṅ rab tu
dbye ba rtogs pa’o – "There reasonable (yukta) means the holy way (āryamārga) and extinction
(nirvāṇa). (1) Reflecting on (cint-) and cultivating (bhāvaya-) in accordance with that
is thorough mental effort (yoniśomanasikāra). By that thorough mental effort one penetrates
the reality of things as they are, so it is called entrance through thorough mental effort
(tena yoniśomanasikāreṇa tattvārthaṃ praviśati yoniśomanasikārapraveśa iti). Thus that
entrance into the meaning [or thing pointed at by a word, cf. infra] (arthapraveśa) entails
that the meaning is understood (artham adhigamyate) after having cultivated (bhāvayitvā)
with the insight of cultivation (bhāvanā) the moments of existence discerned (viniścita)
by the insight of reflection (cintā). So this is to be known as being the insight concerned
with reflection and cultivation (cintābhāvanāprajñā).Or (atha vā), (2) reasonable (yukta)
is the holy path and extinction, but also logical arguments based on sense-perception,
inference, etc. (pratyakṣānumānādinyāya), and the instructions of teachers and preceptors
who are not imparting wrong instructions (abhrāntadeśikācāryopādhyāyopadeśa); and mental effort
not in opposition to that is thorough mental effort (tadaviruddhamanasikāro manasikāra
iti). One enters that mental effort, so it is called entrance into thorough mental effort
(taṃ yoniśomanasikāraṃ praviśati yoniśomanasikāra iti).Entrance (praveśa) is (2) to stay
within thorough mental effort, or (1) to understand essence (svabhāva) and distinctions
(prabheda) through those thorough mental efforts."This section then is interpreted as cintāmayī
and bhāvanāmayī prajñā while section a) on śrutākāra is of course śrutamayī prajñā "insight
consisting of learning (or the teachings one has heard)". Cf. ṭ. fol. 89a3: de yaṅ
thos pa las śes rab kyi bye brag phyed par gyur te...; and Bhāvanākrama I paragraph 9-12,
p. 19821-22: tasmāc cintāmayyā prajñayā yuktyāgamābhyāṃ pratyavekṣya bhūtam eva vastusvarūpaṃ
bhāvanīyam, vastūnāṃ svarūpaṃ ca paramārthato ’nutpāda evāgamato yuktitaś ca niścitam
etc.[The word artha primarily means "aim", "what is aimed at", possibly from the root ṛ-
"to go, move, reach, obtain", see MMW s. v., then "thing" or "object" aimed at by a word,
the "meaning" aimed at by a word. yoniśas is taken as equivalent to yukta and yukti and also
to yoni, cf. the beginning of the next paragraph c) with notes].

źi gnas kyi gnas źes bya ba la źi gnas ñid gnas yin pas źi gnas kyi gnas te, źi gnas de la ’jug
pa ni źi gnas kyi raṅ bźin rtogs par byed pa’am, tiṅ ṅe ’dzin de la gnas par byed pa’o
– "Peaceful meditation is a state, thus it is said "the state of peaceful meditation" (śamatha
eva sthānam śamathasthānam iti) (karmadhāraya-compound). Entering that peaceful meditation
means "one understands the essence of peaceful meditation" or "one stays in that concentration"
(tasmiñ śamathe praveśa iti śamathasvabhāvam adhigacchati vā tasmin samādhau
tiṣṭhati vā)."lhag mthoṅ gis ’dus byas daṅ ’dus ma byas kyi chos rnams kyi raṅ daṅ spyi’i
mtshan ñid rab tu rnam par ’byed pas na lhag mthoṅ rnam par dpyod pa źes bya la, de ltar rnam
par dpyad pa las de kho na ñid kyi don rtogs par ’gyur bas ’jug pa źes kyaṅ bya’o – "By
expanded vision one discerns the special and general characteristics of the conditioned
and unconditioned moments of existence, thus it is called discernment of expanded vision (vipaśyanayā
saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svasāmanyalakṣaṇāni pravicinotīti vipaśyanāvyavacāraḥ);
and by such discernment the reality of things as they are is understood, thus it is
called entrance (evaṃvyavacārāt tattvārtho ’dhigamyate ceti praveśaḥ)."źi gnas daṅ lhag
mthoṅ de ñid kyaṅ sems las su ruṅ ba la ’jug pa bśad de, dmigs par bya ba’i don la ci dgar
gnas su btub pa ni źi gnas daṅ lhag mthoṅ yin pa’i phyir ro.lus dben pa daṅ sems dben pa
la ’jug pa gñis kyis ni źi gnas daṅ lhag mthoṅ bsgom pa la sbyor ba bstan te, spoṅ ba daṅ
mthun pa’i gnas lam brag phug daṅ nags tshal la sogs pa la gnas na chags par ’gyur ba’i yul
’gro ba bzaṅ mo la sogs pa med pa daṅ, ’dod pa la ’dun pa la sogs pa rtog pa med pa na źi
gnas daṅ lhag mthoṅ la ’jug par ’gyur ba’i phyir ro.rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba ni phyi
daṅ naṅ gi bye brag gis rnam pa gñis te, sṅar bśad par zad do, de la ’jug pa ni de dag gi
mtshan ñid rtogs par byed ces bya ba’i tha tshig go.bden pa’i rjes su mthun pa ni ’phags pa’i
bden pa bźi tshul bźin du yid la byed pa’o, yaṅ na khams gsum la yid byuṅ ba daṅ, ñon
moṅs pa’i tshogs rnams daṅ bral bar dga’ ba daṅ, mya ṅan las ’das pa la gcig tu phyogs pa
daṅ, ’phags pa’i lam sgrub par mos pa ni bden pa bźi rtogs pa’i rgyu yin pas bden pa’i rjes
su mthun pa źes bya’o. yaṅ na bden pa bźi ni mthoṅ ba’i lam gyis rtogs par bya ba yin pas
de daṅ mthun pa ni ṅes par ’byed pa’i cha bźi yin no; bden pa’i rjes su ’jug pa’i chos des
’jug pas na bden pa’i rjes su mthun par ’jug pa źes kyaṅ bya ste, chos des de kho na’i
don rtogs par byed ces bya ba’i tha tshig go. yaṅ na bden pa’i rjes su mthun pa’i rtogs par
bya ba’i phyir ’jug ces bya bar yaṅ bśad do.chad pa med pa daṅ rtag pa med pa tshig gñis
ni rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba’i don phyin ci ma log par rtogs pa bstan te, phyi daṅ naṅ
gi rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba rgyu daṅ rkyen la brten nas skad cig ma’i tshul gyis skye ba
rgyun mi ’chad pa daṅ, de dag ñid kyaṅ mi rtag pa yin par rtogs na chad pa med pa daṅ rtag
pa med pa la ’jug pa źes bya’o. de ñid kyi don gsal bar bstan pa’i phyir rgyu daṅ rkyen
la ’jug pa źes gsuṅs so, ma rig pa daṅ sa bon lta bu ni rgyu yin la, sa daṅ chu la sogs pa
ni rkyen yin par śes pa’o.bdag la sogs pa mu stegs can gyis bdag tu btags pa’i miṅ gi rnam
graṅs ni sṅar bśad par zad de, de dag med par rtogs par byed pas na bdag med pa nas gaṅ
zag gi bar du med pa la ’jug pa źes bya’o, cf. fol. 25a5-b3.’oṅ ba daṅ, ’gro ba daṅ, gnas
med ces bya ba ni skye ba daṅ ’gag pa daṅ ’jug pa med pa ste, de ltar rtogs pa la ’jug pa
źes bya’o.mi ’pho źiṅ rgyu daṅ ’bras bu chud mi za ba la ’jug pa ni ’di nas pha rol tu chos
rdul tsam yaṅ ’phos pa med pa la, las dge ba daṅ mi dge ba’i ’bras bu yaṅ chud mi za bar
śes pa’o.stoṅ pa ñid daṅ, mtshan ma med pa daṅ, smon pa med pa ’dris par byed pa la ’jug
pa źes bya ba la sogs pa ’di man chad kyis mi gnas pa’i mya ṅan las ’das pa’i lam śes rab
daṅ sñiṅ rjes zin par ston te, ’khor ba na gnas kyaṅ śes rab kyis ’khor ba’i dṅos po thams
cad stoṅ pa ñid la sogs par khoṅ du chud pas ’khor ba’i skyon gyis kyaṅ ma gos la, de ltar
khoṅ du chud kyaṅ sñiṅ rjes sems can gyi don du ’khor bar ’jug pas na stoṅ pa ñid daṅ mtshan
ma med pa daṅ smon pa med pa mṅon sum du mi byed pa la ’jug par yaṅ byed ces bya bar
sbyar te. ’og ma dag la yaṅ lam gñis kyis zin par de bźin du sbyar ro – "... This and the
following teaches the way to extinction not founded anywhere (apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇamārga) including
both insight (prajñā) and compassion (karuṇā). (The bodhisattva) is not sullied by
any of the imperfections of existence (saṃsāradoṣair nopalipyate) even though he stays in
existence, because he with insight (prajñā) has penetrated the emptiness and so on of all
things in existence. But even so, by compassion (karuṇā) for the sake of all beings he enters
existence (saṃsāra), so it is said "entrance into not realizing....". This applies also
for the following pairs of items."On the connection between the concepts of parijaya and
asākṣātkaraṇa cf. Āloka p. 6817: tatphalāsākṣadkaraṇād dhyānaparijayaṃ karoti, and the
introduction supra.bsam gtan bźi daṅ, nam mkha’ mdzod daṅ, dpa’ bar ’gro ba la sogs pa’i tiṅ
ṅe ’dzin daṅ mthar gyis gnas pa’i sñoms par ’jug pa rnams śes rab kyis bskyed pa’i tshul
la ’jug ste, dbaṅ byed kyaṅ sñiṅ rje’i dbaṅ gis ’dod pa’i khams kyi sems can rnams la lta
ba’i phyir bsam gtan la sogs pa de dag gi dbaṅ gis mi skye ba la ’jug go.mṅon par śes pa
ñid ye śes yin pas mṅon par śes pa’i ye śes yin pa’am, yaṅ na bsam gtan mi zad pa’i skabs
su bśad pa ltar mṅon par śes pa daṅ ye śes źes phye ste, śes rab kyis de lta bu dag bskyed
pa la ’jug kyaṅ, sñiṅ rjes zag pa zad pa mṅon sum du byed pa ma yin pa la ’jug go.śes rab
kyis kyaṅ kun tu brtags pa’i chos rnams raṅ bźin med ciṅ sems tsam du śes pa ni naṅ du rtog
pa la ’jug pa yin la, de ltar śes kyaṅ sñiṅ rje’i dbaṅ gis mya ṅan las ’das pa ṅes par
gyur par mi ’jug go.śes rab kyis ’dus byas kyi skyon mi rtag pa la sogs pa la yoṅs su ’jal
yaṅ, sñiṅ rjes ’dus ma byas kyi chos mya ṅan las ’das pa mṅon sum du mi byed par ’jug go.śes
rab kyis sems can thams cad la bdag med par so sor rtogs te, don bya ba’i gnas raṅ bźin
med par śes kyaṅ, sñiṅ rje chen pos mi gtoṅ ste, sems can gyi don yaṅ byed do. de la rnam
pa bdun gyis na sñiṅ rje las sñiṅ rje chen po khyad par du ’phags te, 1) raṅ bźin ni źe
mi sdaṅ ba daṅ gti mi mug pa’i raṅ bźin yin pa’i phyir ro; 2) rnam pa ni sdug bsṅal gcig
daṅ gñis nas sdug bsṅal brgya stoṅ maṅ po’i bar la rtog pa’i phyir ro; 3) dmigs pa ni ’jig
rten gyi khams thams cad la dmigs pa’i phyir ro; 4) sa ni bsam gtan bźi pa’i sar gtogs pa’i
phyir ro; 5) rgyud ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i rgyud la ’byuṅ ba’i phyir ro; 6) ’dod chags
daṅ bral ba thob pa ni ’dod pa’i khams thams cad kyi ’dod chags daṅ bral ba thob pa’i phyir
ro; 7) sñiṅ rje’i skye mched mi mñam pa ni sems can thams cad la skyob par byed pa’i phyir
ro.skye ba thams cad ni ’gro ba rgyud lṅa’i skye ba rnams te, so so’i skye bo dag ltar
skye ba de dag tu ñon moṅs pa’i dbaṅ du gyur nas yaṅ daṅ yaṅ du skye bas ’jigs par lta ba
ni śes rab ste, de ltar rtogs kyaṅ sñiṅ rje chen po’i smon lam gyi dbaṅ gis rtag tu bsams
bźin du śes pas srid pa thams cad kyaṅ yoṅs su ’dzin to.śes rab kyis khams gsum gyi chos rnams
la yid byuṅ źiṅ ’dod chags daṅ bral bar ’jug kyaṅ, sñiṅ rjes ’dod chags daṅ bral ba’i
chos mya ṅan las ’das pa yaṅ mṅon sum du mi byed do.’dod pa ñid dga’ ba yin la, de dag so
so’i skye bos bsten par bya ba yin pas yon tan yaṅ yin te, śes rab kyis de dag raṅ bźin med
par rtogs pas ’dod pa’i yon tan lṅa po gaṅ la yaṅ chags pa daṅ sdaṅ ba med de, yal bar
’dor ba la ’jug pa yin yaṅ, chos rnams kyi don rtogs nas yid sim par ’gyur ba’i chos kyi dga’
ba yaṅ mi gtoṅ ba la ’jug go.śes rab daṅ sñiṅ rje’i lam mdor bsdus te bstan pa’i phyir
spros pa daṅ rnam par rtog pa thams cad spoṅ ba la ’jug pa daṅ, thabs mkhas pa’i spros pa
daṅ rnam par rtog pa mi spoṅ bar ’jug pa źes gsuṅs te, śes rab kyis lus daṅ ṅag gi las kyi
spros pa daṅ sems kyi rnam par rtog pa thams cad spoṅ yaṅ, dga’ ldan nas ’bab pa daṅ yum
gyi lhums su gśegs pa la sogs pa sku’i phrin las daṅ chos ston pa’i gsuṅ gi phrin las kyi
thabs mkhas pa’i spros pa daṅ thugs kyi chos rnams kyi mtshan ñid rab tu ’byed pa’i rnam
par rtog pa yaṅ mi spoṅ źes sbyar ro.

śes rab kyi ’jug pa tshul bźin źes bya ba de’i don yaṅ bstan ciṅ, ṅes pa’i tshig gi dbaṅ du
byas nas btsun pa śa ra dva ti’i bu, gźan yaṅ tshul bźin źes bya ba, de ni rigs pa’i tshig
go źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅs so. (107a)yoni means "uterus" "the female generative organ",
then "place of birth", "origin", and adverbially "fundamentally", "thoroughly". The translation
"thorough" is kept to connect it with yoniśomanasikāra, "thorough mental activity",
notwithstanding the play on the other meanings.Cf. Buddhasaṃgītisūtra as quoted in Bhāvanākrama
I p. 19914-16: katamā yoniśaḥ pṛcchā? katamā yoniḥ? āha: anutpādo yoniḥ, tasya pṛcchā
yoniśaḥ pṛcchā. Tib. (ibid. p. 2469-12): tshul bźin ’dri ba ni gaṅ lags? tshul bźin ni
gaṅ lags? bka’ stsal pa: skye ba med pa ni tshul bźin no, de ’dri ba ni tshul bźin ’dri
ba’o.slu bar mi byed pa ni rigs pa ste, rigs pa bźi daṅ ldan pa’i śes pa la tshul bźin bya’o.
rigs pa bźi ni 1) ltos pa’i rigs pa daṅ, 2) bya ba byed pa’i rigs pa daṅ, 3) ’thad par
bsgrub pa’i rigs pa daṅ, 4) chos ñid kyi rigs pa’o. [de la 1) ltos pa’i rigs pa ni: rgyu
gaṅ daṅ rkyen gaṅ dag la ltos te chos gaṅ skye ba’o; 2) bya ba byed pa’i rigs pa ni: chos
skyes pa rnams raṅ gi bya ba byed pa ste, ’di lta ste dper na mig gis gzugs rnams la lta bar
byed pa daṅ, rna bas sgra rnams ñan pa byed la sogs pa lta bu’o; 3) ’thad par bsgrub pa’i
rigs pa ni: chos rnams mi rtag pa’am, rten ciṅ ’brel bar ’byuṅ ba’am, sdug bsṅal ba’am,
stoṅ pa’am, bdag med pa’o, źes tshad ma gsum po yid ches pa’i luṅ daṅ mṅon sum daṅ rjes su
dpag pa dag gis ñe bar rtog par byed ciṅ mi rtag pa la sogs par sgrub par byed pa’o; 4)
chos ñid kyi rigs pa ni: ci’i phyir ’jig rten gnas pa de lta bur gyur pa yin, ci’i phyir sa’i
mtshan ñid sra ba yin źes bya ba nas chos thams cad la yaṅ sbyar te ci’i phyir de lta
bu yin źe na? de ni chos ñid yin te, chos de dag gi raṅ bźin de yin źiṅ, de dag gi ṅo bo ñid
de lta bu yin pas, chos ñid de gaṅ kho na yin pa de ñid ’dir rigs pa yin no.] rigs pa de
lta bu dag tshul bźin yid la byed pas śes śiṅ rtogs par byed pas na, tshul bźin źes bya
ba de ni rigs pa’i tshig ces bya ste. ’og ma rnams la yaṅ tshul de bźin du sbyar ro – "It
does not cheat, thus it is reasoning (yukti), thorough should be taken in the meaning ’knowledge
furnished with four kinds of reasoning’ (caturyuktiyuktajñāne yonir iti). The four
kinds of reasoning are 1) reasoning concerned with dependence on (apekṣāyukti), 2) reasoning
concerned with cause and effect (kāryakāraṇayukti), 3) reasoning by presenting proof (upapattisādhanayukti),
and 4) reasoning concerned with the true nature of things (dharmatāyukti).
[There, 1) reasoning concerned with dependence on [is concerned with] the causes and
conditions by which moments of existence arise; 2) reasoning concerned with cause and effect
[is concerned with] the appropriate effects that arisen moments of existence cause, as
when the eye sees form and the ear hears sound; 3) reasoning by presenting proof investigates
the moments of existence as impermanent, originated in dependence, as suffering, empty,
and selfless by the three standards of knowledge, viz. canonical scripture, sense-perception
and inference, and it establishes impermanence, etc.; and 4) reasoning concerned with
the true nature of things [is concerned with questions like] "Why has the state of the
world become like this?", "Why does the element earth have the essential character of hardness?",
etc., with regard to all things [it asks the question] "Why is it like that?" [and
answers like] "This is the nature (prakṛti) of those moments of existence, such is their
essence (svabhāva), this is the true nature of things (dharmatā)". That reasoning is concerned
with that very true nature of things.] That reasoning knows and understands by thorough
mental effort, thus one says ’Thorough is a word for reasoning’. The following should be
understood accordingly."The part in brackets is a quotation from Śbh with some changes –
mainly the substitution of dharma for skandha – and abbreviations: 1. (fol. 7A33, S p. 14112-13,
D fol. 57b3-4) tatrotpattyapekṣā yair hetubhir yaiḥ pratyayaiḥ skandhānāṃ prādurbhāvo
bhavati / 2. (7A34-5, S p. 1423-6, D fol. 57b6-7) kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ katamā / yeṣām utpannānāṃ
skandhānāṃ svena hetunā svena pratyayena tasmiṃs tasmin svakāryakaraṇe viniyogas tad
yathā / cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni / śrotre(5)ṇa sabdāḥ śrotavyāḥ / 3) (fol. 7A35-6, 14212-1431,
D fol. 58a1-4) upapattisādhanayuktiḥ [(5) katamā /] anityāḥ skandhāḥ pratītyasamutpannā
duḥkhāḥ śūnyā anātmāna iti tribhiḥ pramāṇair upaparīkṣate [yad uta] āptāgamena pratyakṣeṇānumānena
ca / [ebhis tribhiḥ pramāṇairupapattiyuktaiḥ satāṃ hṛdayagrāhakair vyavasthāpanā]
sādhanā kriyate [/ yad uta skandha-]anityatāyā vā .... 4) ( fol. 7A37-7B31, S p.
1434-13, D fol. 58a4-7) dharmatāyuktiḥ katamā / kena kāraṇena .... tathābhūto lokasanniveśaḥ
kena kāraṇena kharalakṣaṇā pṛthivī ..(7B3).. prakṛtir eṣāṃ dharmāṇām iyaṃ svabhāva eṣām
īdṛśaḥ / dharmataiṣā / yaiva cāsau dharmatā / saivātra yuktir [yoga upāyaḥ /]Msa. p. 1685-11
treats the four ways of reasoning by relating them to the three vehicles, but also to
thorough mental effort (yoniśomanasikāra), which indeed is also the the basis of the treatment
in ṭ. Differing somewhat from ṭ and Śbh, the fourth reasoning is concerned with the unthinkable
(acintya) nature of things. yuktiprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ caturvidhaṃ / apekṣāyuktiḥ
/ kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ / upapattisādhanayuktiḥ / dharmatāyuktiś ca / yānaprajñaptivyavasthānaṃ
trividhaṃ / śrāvakayānaṃ / pratyekabuddhayānaṃ / mahāyānaṃ ca / tatrāpekṣāyuktis triṣv
api yāneṣu yoniśomanaskāraḥ / tam apekṣya tena pratyayena lokottarāyāḥ samyagdṛṣṭer utpādāt
/ kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ samyagdṛṣṭiḥ saphalā / upapattisādhanayuktiḥ / pratyakṣādibhiḥ pramāṇaiḥ
parīkṣā / dharmatāyuktir acintyaṃ sthānaṃ / siddhā hi dharmatā na punaś cintyā / kasmāt
/ yoniśomanaskārāt samyagdṛṣṭir bhavati / tato vā kleśaprahāṇaṃ phalam ity evam ādi /Saṃdhinirmocana
X, 7,4,7 treats the four in great detail. Cf. also Mavbh III, 12; Bbh p. 37
and 29317-18; Śbh p. 3698ff.Notes to the Sanskrit text: 1) S yair hetupratyayaiḥ for yair
hetubhir yaiḥ pratyayaiḥ 2) ṭ probably read tatrāpekṣāyuktir yān hetūn yān pratyayān apekṣya
ye ’pi dharmā prādurbhavanti 3) As tib. bya ba byed pa’i rigs pa gaṅ źe na / ...gaṅ yin
pa rnams MS ...yuktir yād and no daṇḍa 4) MS tasmims 5) MS śabdā 6) ṭ probably abbreviated
as kāryakāraṇayuktir utpannānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svakāryakaraṇas tad yathā / cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni
/ śrotreṇa sabdāḥ śrotavyāḥ / 7) Bracketed part not in ṭ 8) ṭ has dharmāḥ for skandhāḥ
MS, S has iti, which probably is a misreading for the visarga and has no equivalent
in tib. 9) MS om. visarga 10) MS yad uta tāptāgamena 11) W ...saṃni... 12) ṭ abbreviates
* ity ādi yāvat kena kāraṇena tathābhūtāḥ sarvadharmāḥ 13) W idaṃ 14) As tib. and ṭ de dag
gi MS,S,W eṣa 15) W om. daṇḍa 16) W ...ṣā(ṃ); daṇḍa as in tib. and ṭ, MS,S,W om. 17) As
tib. and ṭ gaṅ kho na yin pa S,W caiva MS ambiguous.tshul ni chos rnams kyi raṅ bźin phyin
ci ma log pa’am, yaṅ na tshul bźin yid la byed pa sum cu rtsa gñis kyi skabs su (ṭ. 97b1,
v. supra) tshul gyi sgra bśad pa de la bya’o.sgo ni tshul bźin te, bsam gtan daṅ, mṅon par
śes pa daṅ, stobs daṅ mi ’jigs pa la sogs pa yon tan dpag tu med pa rnams sgrub pa’i sgo
yin pa’i phyir ro, yaṅ na de’i sgo nas chos yaṅs śiṅ rgya che ba rtogs par byed pa’i phyir
ro.kha ni rten la bya ste, tshul bźin la brten nas chos phra źiṅ zab pa rnams rtogs par
byed pa’i phyir ro.rgyu daṅ rkyen źes bya ba ni tshul bźin te, saṅs rgyas kyi chos rnams kyi
rgyu daṅ rkyen yin pa’i phyir ro.mi ’gog pa źes bya ba la tshul bźin daṅ mi mthun pa’i
rgyu daṅ rkyen rnams kyis de med par ’gyur ba ni ’gog pa źes bya na, tshul bźin yid la byed
pa las byuṅ ba’i śes rab dkar po’i chos kyi mthu daṅ ldan pas raṅ daṅ mi mthun pa’i rkyen
gyis med par mi ’gyur bas mi ’gog pa’i tshig ces bya’o.mi ’gal ba ni chos rnams kyi raṅ
bźin ji ltar gnas pa las mi ’gal bar rtogs pa’i phyir ro.tshul bźin gyi dṅos po thams cad
bdag med par rtogs te, gaṅ la yaṅ chags pa daṅ sdaṅ ba med par btaṅ sñoms kyi tshig ces bya’o.The
last two mentiond items refer to not being dependent upon ālayavijñāna: kun gźi rnam
par śes pa la mi gnas pas na mi rten pa’i tshig ces bya’o. mi gnas pa ni rten smos ma thag
pa de gñis la mi gnas pa’i phyir ro. yaṅ na gaṅ zag gi dṅos por chags pa med pas na rten
pa med pa’o, chos kyi dṅos por chags pa med pas na mi rten pa’o, kun gźi rnam par śes pa’i
gnas la gnas pa med pas na mi gnas pa źes bya’o. The last paragraph seems to have read
three items in the sūtra, the two and, in addition, rten pa med pa – *aniśraya (?) ST has
mi rten pa for DLNQ rten pa med pa, and the respective editions may have lost one of the
two items. The text read by ṭ may originally have had aniśrayapadam etad, anāśrayapadam etad,
anāśritapadam etat, and the three have been interpreted respectively as freedom from grasping
for substance in a) the pudgala and b) the dharmas, and from being dependent on the
ālayavijñāna.ma g-yos pa ni raṅ bźin gźan du mi ’gyur ba ste, tshul bźin de ṅo bo ñid kyis
dag pas nams kyaṅ raṅ bźin gźan du mi ’gyur ba la bya’o; rnam par ma g-yos pa źes bya ba
la mi mthun pa’i phyogs kyi dbaṅ du gyur pa ni rnam par g-yos pa ste, tshul bźin des mi
mthun pa’i phyogs spaṅs pas mi rtag pa la rtag par ’dzin pa la sogs pa mi mthun pa’i phyogs
kyi chos rnams kyi dbaṅ du mi ’gyur ba’i phyir rnam par ma g-yos pa źes bya’o, yaṅ na ’dod
chags la sogs pa kun nas ñon moṅs pa daṅ phyin ci log bźi’i rluṅ gis bskyod par mi nus
pas na ma g-yos pa źes bya la, phuṅ po daṅ khams daṅ skye mched la mṅon par chags pa’i rluṅ
gis bskyod par mi nus pas na rnam par ma g-yos pa źes bya’o.kun brtags pa’i ṅo bo la yod
par mi ’dzin pas na sgro btags pa med pa’o. ".... not apprehending the imagined essence (parikalpitasvabhāva)
as existent".rtag pa daṅ chad pa la sogs pa’i mthar ma lhuṅ ba na mñam
pa ñid do, gzugs daṅ sgra la sogs pa’i mtshan ma rnam pa sna tshogs su ’byed pa ni mñam
pa ste, chos thams cad brjod du med pa’i raṅ bźin du tshul bźin gyis khoṅ du chud pa la de
lta bur ’byed pa med pas mi mñam pa med pa’o.ji ltar bsgrubs pa bźin du ’bras bu ’thob ste,
mi slu bas na bden pa’i tshig go, ’phags pa rnams kyi spyod yul yin pa’am, tshad ma gsum
daṅ mi ’gal bas yaṅ dag pa’i tshig go.’jig rten gyi chos brgyad kyis mi ’gyur ba’am, yaṅ
na chos rnams kyi raṅ bźin don dam pa skye ba daṅ ’jig pa daṅ bral ba rtogs par byed pa’i
tshul bźin yaṅ mi ’gyur ba’i tshig ces bya’o.phyir bya ba ni gñen po’i chos kyis sbyaṅ źiṅ
gtaṅ dgos pa ste, tshul bźin de ñid kun nas ñon moṅs pa’i chos gźan sbyoṅ ba’i gñen po yin
te, de la gźan gaṅ gis kyaṅ sbyaṅ źiṅ gtaṅ mi dgos pas na phyir bya ba med pa’i tshig go.
Cf. Dbh p. 7115.’jig rten pa’i lam daṅ, ’jig rten las ’das pa’i lam daṅ, de gñis ka’i goṅ
ma theg pa chen po’i lam gyis spaṅs par bya ba’i skyon spaṅs pas źi ba daṅ rab tu źi ba
daṅ ñe bar źi ba’i tshig go. mi mthun pa’i phyogs daṅ gñen po’i chos rnam pa sna tshogs su
rtog pa’i spros pa med pas spros pa med pa’i tshig ste; ji ltar mi rtog ce na? ’degs pa
med pa daṅ gźag pa med pa źes smos te, kun nas ñon moṅs pa’i chos glo bur ba bdegs śiṅ bsal
du yaṅ med la, rnam par byaṅ ba’i chos sems kyi raṅ bźin ’od gsal ba gsar du bsnan ciṅ gźag
tu yaṅ med par tshul bźin gyis rtogs pa’i phyir ro.phuṅ po lṅa daṅ, khams bco brgyad daṅ,
skye mched bcu gñis la sogs pa ji sñed yod pa daṅ, de dag ñid kyaṅ mi rtag pa daṅ, sdug
bsṅal ba la sogs pa ji lta ba bźin du yod pa ma lus pa daṅ, phyin ci ma log par tshul bźin
gyis rtogs pas na ma tshaṅ ba med pa’i tshig go; bdag la sogs pa dṅos po med pa’i rnams
yod par sgro btags nas śes pa’i yul du ’jal ba ni lhag pa ste, tshul bźin de ltar mi ’jal
bas lhag pa med pa’o.... of saṃsāra? Cf. Śikṣ p. 354-5: kalyāṇamitrā .... niṣkāsayitāraḥ
saṃsārapurāt. bsal źiṅ bsñigs pa ni phyir dbyuṅ ba ste, tshul bźin śes pa thams cad kyi sñiṅ
po yin pas de ltar byar med pa’i phyir dbyuṅ du med pa’o.tshul bźin daṅ mi mthun pa mi
rtag pa la rtag par ’dzin pa la sogs pa ni gñen po ste, de dag ’dis spaṅs pas na gñen po med
pa’o.theg pa mchog gi lam du źugs pa’i tshul bźin gyis gaṅ zag daṅ chos la bdag med pa
khoṅ du chud de, ñan thos daṅ raṅ saṅs rgyas la sogs pa mchog rnams las kyaṅ dam par gyur
pas na dam pa’i tshig go.de kho na’i tshig ces bya ba ni bstan pa’o. lhag ma bźi ni bśad pa
ste: rtag du de bźin du gnas śiṅ rnam par mi ’jig pas de bźin ñid daṅ ma nor ba daṅ phyin
ci log tu gyur pa med pas ma nor ba de bźin ñid daṅ gźan du ’gyur ba med pas gźan ma yin
pa’i de bźin ñid daṅ chos rnams kyi raṅ bźin yin pas ji lta ba bźin źes bya ste, chos rnams
kyi yoṅs su grub pa’i mtshan ñid de lta bur śes par byed pa’i tshul bźin yid la byed pa
la yaṅ de skad ces bya’o – "This is said in connection with thorough mental effort (yoniśomanasikāra)
that knows the absolute character (pariniṣpannalakṣaṇa) of moments of existence."ṭ.
fol. 101a5: yaṅ na de kho na la sogs pa ni chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi rnam graṅs kyi tshig
yin te – "Or, ’the real (tattva)’ and the following words are synonyms of total reality (dharmadhātuparyāyapada)".To
elucidate this a quotation from the Ratnameghasūtra on the topic
then follows, ṭ. fol. 101a5-b4: de bas na dkon mchog sprin gyi mdo las byaṅ chub sems dpa’
sgrib pa thams cad rnam par sel bas gsol pa: bcom ldan ’das, de kho na źes bgyi ba ci
lags? bcom ldan ’das kyis bka’ stsal pa: rigs kyi bu, ’di lta ste, de kho na źes bya ba ni
yaṅ dag pa’i don gyi tshig bla dags so. gsol pa: bcom ldan ’das, yaṅ dag pa źes bgyi ba ci
lags? bcom ldan ’das kyis bka’ stsal pa: gaṅ de bźin ñid daṅ ma nor ba de bźin ñid daṅ gźan
ma yin pa de bźin ñid do. gsol pa: bcom ldan ’das, de bźin ñid źes bgyi ba ji lta bu lags?
bcom ldan ’das kyis bka’ stsal pa: rigs kyi bu, chos ’di dag ni so so raṅ gis rig pa
ste, de dag la yi ges gdags par mi nus so. ci’i phyir źe na? chos de dag ni yi ge thams cad
las śin tu ’das pa, brjod pa thams cad las śin tu ’das pa, tshig gi spyod yul thams cad
las śin tu ’das pa, tshig gi lam thams cad las śin tu ’das pa, spros pa thams cad daṅ bral
ba, phye ba daṅ btsums pa thams cad daṅ rtog ge thams cad daṅ bral ba, rtog ge thams cad
kyis brtag pa’i spyod yul ma yin pa, mtshan ma med pas mtshan ma’i spyod yul thams cad las
yoṅs su ’das pa, byis pa’i spyod yul las śin tu ’das pa, bdud thams cad kyi spyod yul las
śin tu ’das pa, ñon moṅs pa’i spyod yul thams cad las śin tu ’das pa, rnam par śes pa’i spyod
yul las śin tu ’das pa, mi gnas pa, gnas ma yin pa, źi ba ’phags pa’i ye śes kyi spyod
yul, de dag ñid kyis so sor raṅ gis rig par bya ba, dri ma med pa, daṅ ba, dag pa, gya nom
pa rtag pa, brtan pa, rgyun du gnas pa, ’jig par mi ’gyur ba’i chos de, de bźin gśegs pa
rnams byuṅ yaṅ ruṅ, ma byuṅ yaṅ ruṅ, chos kyi dbyiṅs ni gnas pa’o, źes gsuṅs pa’i phyir
ro.byaṅ chub ṅes par thob pa ni chud mi za ba ste, tshul bźin gyis byaṅ chub thob par byed
pas chud mi za ba’i tshig go.yaṅ dag pa ñid de kho na ñid phyin ci ma log pa’i mthar thug
pas yaṅ dag pa’i mtha’i tshig go.sṅon gyi mtha’ daṅ, phyi ma’i mtha’ daṅ, da ltar byuṅ ba
dus gsum bdag ñid thams cad du mi dmigs pas dus gsum yaṅ dag par rjes su mthoṅ ba ni dus
gsum mñam pa’i tshig ces bya’o. de ji ltar mñam źe na? dus yoṅs su ma chad pa źes smos te,
’dus byas kyi chos kyi phuṅ po la sogs pa skye ba daṅ, gnas pa daṅ ’jig pa’i sgo nas dus
gsum du gdags par zad kyi, yoṅs su grub pa’i mtshan ñid la ni de lta bu dbye ba med pa’i phyir
ro – ".... since this kind of classification is not existent in what has the absolute
character (pariniṣpannalakṣaṇa)".gzugs la rnam par śes pa mi gnas pa la sogs pas dus gsum
gyi chos ’dus byas rnams la ma chags pa’am, de dag la miṅ daṅ mtshan ma’i bdag ñid du mṅon
par źen pa med pa ni tshul bźin yin par ston te, ji ltar so so’i skye bo dag kun brtags
pa’i gzugs la rnam par śes pas rnam pa sna tshogs su rtog ciṅ de’i bdag ñid du mṅon par źen
pa de ltar mi byed pas gzugs la rnam par śes pa mi gnas pa źes bya ste, tshor ba la sogs
pa lhag ma rnams la yaṅ de daṅ ’dra bar bśad do.de ni don la rton pa’i tshig ces bya ba la
sogs pas tshul bźin de tshig ’bru daṅ, gaṅ zag daṅ, rnam par śes pa daṅ, bkri ba’i don gyi
mdo sde la mi rton gyi, so sor rton pa bźi la brten ces bya ba’i tha tshig go.

See ṭ. fol. 88b4, b5: śes rab kyi rgyu, and cf. ṭ. fol. 103a4-7, infra. rnam pa gcig tu na tshul
bźin źes bya ba de ni rigs pa’i tshig go źes bya ba la ṅes pa’i tshig smos pa thams cad
tshul bźin yid la byed pa daṅ mi sbyar bar chos rnams kyi de bźin ñid yoṅs su grub pa’i
ṅes pa’i tshig gi rnam graṅs yin par sbyar źiṅ bśad de, de bas na mjug thogs su tshul bźin
źes bya ba ni chos thams cad do źes gsuṅs pa’i phyir te; gaṅ zag la bdag med pa daṅ chos
la bdag med pa ni tshul bźin źes bya ba ste, de chos thams cad la ma khyab pa med pa’i phyir
tshul bźin źes bya ba ni chos thams cad do źes bśad do. ’bras bu bstan pa’i dbaṅ du byas
nas: ci’i phyir źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅs te, ci’i phyir źes bya ba ni chos thams cad
la ci’i phyir tshul bźin źes bya ba’i gtan tshigs ’dri ba’o – "And further, the etymology
(nirukti) saying: ’Thorough is a word for reasoning’ (in the preceding paragraph: yonir iti
yuktipadam etat) does not apply for thorough mental effort (yoniśomanasikāra) concerned
with everything, so then one goes on referring to the etymology concerned with things as
they really are, to the perfected state of things (tathatāpariniṣpannanirukti). Thus follows
’Thorough is [concerned with] all moments of existence’: The fact of selflessness of the
person (pudgalanairātmya) and selflessness of all things (dharmanairātmya) is thorough [or
fundamental], and because this fact applies for all moments of existence (sarvadharmāvyāpyabhāvatvāt),
it is said ’Thorough is [concerned with] all moments of existence’. To demonstrate
the fruit (phala) of this it is said ’Why’ etc." Cf. ṭ. fol. 88b1-2.The "etymology"
is made in treating yoniśas and yuktitas as the same word; cf. the two preceding paragraphs
b) and c), especially notes in the beginning of these paragraphs.

ji ltar bdag la bdag med pa, de bźin du źes bya ba la sogs pas ni tshul bźin mthoṅ ba daṅ sbyor
ba bstan pa’i sgo nas chos thams cad la tshul bźin źes bya ba ston te, bdag ces bya ba
ni raṅ gi ñe bar len pa’i phuṅ po ste, de la gaṅ zag daṅ chos kyi raṅ bźin bdag med pa bźin
du phuṅ po daṅ khams daṅ skye mched la sogs pa chos thams cad kyaṅ tshad ma gsum mam, śes
rab rnam pa gsum gyi rigs pas mthoṅ ba’am, ji ltar sems can la bdag med pa bźin du phuṅ
po daṅ khams daṅ skye mched la sogs pa chos thams cad kyaṅ bdag med par mthoṅ na tshul bźin
mthoṅ ba źes bya bas chos thams cad tshul bźin źes bya bar grub bo.

’khor ba’i khams kyi tshul bźin ni ’khor ba’i raṅ bźin te, ji ltar mya ṅan las ’das pa’i dbyiṅs
kyi tshul bźin yoṅs su dag pa bźin ’khor ba’i raṅ bźin yaṅ yoṅs su dag par mthoṅ na źes
bya ba’i tha tshig go. Cf. Kpv 52: yoniśodharmaprayogaḥ, and Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā p. 129:
āśayena śrutvā dhīra yoniśaḥ prayujyate/.kun nas ñon moṅs pa’i raṅ bźin ni ’dod chags la
sogs pa ste, lus daṅ sems la gnod pa sna tshogs skyed par byed pa’i phyir ro, rnam par byaṅ
ba ni byaṅ chub kyi phyogs daṅ, pha rol du phyin pa ste, ñon moṅs pa rnams ’joms pa’i gñen
po yin pa’i phyir ro, mi mthun pa’i phyogs daṅ gñen po de gñi ga yaṅ brjod du med pa’i
raṅ bźin du mtshuṅs śiṅ mi mthun pa’i phyogs daṅ gñen po źes brjod pa ltar don dam par bye
brag med par mthoṅ ba, de ni tshul bźin rab tu sbyor ba źes bya’o.de ltar gñi ga yaṅ brjod
du med par ’dra bas rnam par byaṅ ba’i chos la yon tan can du rigs par yaṅ mi sems, kun
nas ñon moṅs pa’i chos la skyon can du mi rigs par yaṅ mi sems pa, de ni tshul bźin rab tu
sbyor ba źes bya’o.

btsun pa śa ra dva ti’i bu, mdor na źes bya ba la sogs pas ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’ de ltar tshul
bźin sbyor ba de dag thams cad gaṅ la dmigs śiṅ gaṅ la brten nas sbyor ba’i gnas ston
te, tshul bźin sbyor ba ji sñed pa źes bya ba ni tshul bźin gyi ’jug pa graṅs ji sñed yod
pa’am, ji sñed byed pa źes bya ba’i don to. de dag thams cad kyi gnas ni sems can no źes bya
ba ni tshul bźin de dag gi rten daṅ dmigs par bya ba’i yul sems can yin te, ’di ltar byaṅ
chub sems dpa’ sems can la thugs brtse bas de dag yoṅs su gzuṅ ba’i phyir tshul bźin yid
la byed pa de dag la sbyor ba mdzad pa’am, yaṅ na ji ltar sems can la bdag med pa de bźin
du chos thams cad rigs pas mthoṅ źes bya ba la sogs pa’i tshul gyis sems can gyi yul la
tshul bźin gyi sbyor ba mdzad do źes bya ba’i tha tshig go. de ltar thugs rje chen po’i dbaṅ
gis sems can la dmigs nas dmigs pa daṅ bcas pas: chos kyi dbyiṅs dkrugs par mi ’gyur ram?
sñam pa la de sems can gyi gnas kyaṅ mi spoṅ la chos kyi gnas kyaṅ ’khrugs par mi byed
do źes gsuṅs te, byaṅ chub sems dpa’ de sems can gyi gnas ’khor bar skye ba yaṅ mi gtoṅ la,
chos kyi gnas stobs daṅ mi ’jigs pa la sogs pa yon tan gyi chos rnams kyi ’byuṅ gnas kyi
chos kyi dbyiṅs rnam par dag pa daṅ rnam par mi rtog pa’i ye śes ’khrugs par mi byed de,
sems can kyi don du ’khor bar gnas kyaṅ de gñis las ñams par mi ’gyur źes bya ba’i tha tshig
go.Cf. also Aṣṭādaśa (71), p. 824ff: tad bodhisattvo mahāsattva prakṛtiśūnyatāpāramitāsu
caran rūpaṃ na vikopayati. śūnyaṃ vā nāśūnyam iti. ... na rūpaṃ śūnyatāṃ vikopayati ...
na śūnyatā bodhiṃ vikopayati. tat kasya hetoḥ? na hy eṣāṃ svabhāvo ’sti ya evaṃ vikopayed.

śes rab kyi rnam pa la sogs pa goṅ du bśad pa rnams bsdus te bstan pa daṅ, goṅ du bśad pa’i
chos rnams kyi ’bras bu śes rab yin par bstan pa’i phyir btsun pa śa ra dva ti’i bu, de ltar
de’i chos kyi rnam pa daṅ, thos pa’i rnam pa daṅ, tshul bźin la ’jug pa’i sbyor ba rgyu
mthun pa, de ni śes rab ces bya’o źes smras te; de’i źes bya ba ni sems bskyed pa daṅ bsam
pa mi zad pa la sogs pa nas śes rab mi zad pa’i bar la gnas pa’i byaṅ chub sems dpa’ ’di’i
źes bya ba’i don to; chos kyi rnam pa ni phuṅ po daṅ khams daṅ skye mched la sogs pa’o,
yaṅ na, chos kyi rnam pa ni sems bskyed pa daṅ, bsam pa daṅ, sbyor ba daṅ, lhag pa’i bsam
pa daṅ, sbyin pa daṅ, tshul khrims daṅ, bzod pa daṅ, brtson ’grus daṅ, bsam gtan la sogs
pa goṅ du bśad pa’i chos rnams so; thos pa’i rnam pa ni goṅ du thos pa’i rnam pa brgyad cu
rtsa bźi smos pa’o; tshul bźin la ’jug pa’i sbyor ba ni goṅ du tshul bźin la ’jug pa sum
cu rtsa gñis smos pa’o; chos de rnams ñid rgyu bas na chos kyi rnam pa daṅ, thos pa’i rnam
pa daṅ, tshul bźin la ’jug pa’i sbyor ba’i rgyu źes bya ste, rgyu de daṅ mthun pa’i ’bras
bu ni rgyu mthun pa ste, dṅos su śes rab mi zad pa’o; don du na rgyu mthun pa źes bya ba
ni rgyu ci ’dra bar mthun par ’gyur ba’i ’bras bu la bya ste, chos kyi rnam pa daṅ, thos pa’i
rnam pa daṅ, tshul bźin la ’jug pa’i sbyor ba’i rgyu de dag las ’bras bu śes rab mi zad
pa ’byuṅ bar ’os kyi, gźan ni ma yin pa’i phyir ro.

śes rab kyi raṅ bźin bstan pa’i dbaṅ du byas nas de la śes rab ni ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi
gnas te źes bya ba la sogs pas gsuṅs so. Cf. 88b4, b5-6: śes rab de śes rab kyi mi mthun pa’i
phyogs daṅ ma ’dres pa.’grogs pa bcu drug daṅ lhan cig mi gnas źes bya bas ni śes rab
kyaṅ skabs ’dir rnam par mi rtog pa’i ye śes dmigs pa daṅ, spros pa thams cad las ’das pa,
mtshan ma thams cad ma ’dres pa’i raṅ bźin la bya bar ’dod de, de bas na dmigs pa daṅ, mtshan
ma’i skyon rnams daṅ ma ’dres pa’i phyir ’grogs pa bcu drug daṅ lhan cig mi gnas so źes
bśad do.The expression ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas is somewhat problematic, and the
Tibetan text is possibly corrupt. Dbh p. 5226-27: na ca saṃskṛtasaṃvāsena saṃvasati, and Aṣṭa
p. 79326.: na ca tena vānyena vā nimittena sārdhaṃ saṃvasati (cf. also Aṣṭādaśa (55) p.
211-2; Suvkr p. 524-7; Aṣṭa p. 76020) seem to be expressions very close to Akṣ, but both
’grogs pa ~ saṃvāsa and lhan cig ~ sārdham cannot be in the same sentence. Thus it seems
that either the expression from Dbh or the one from Aṣṭa has to be chosen. From item no. 8
the ’grogs pa has been left out, and suggests the Aṣṭa variant of the expression, while in
the case of no. 1 to no. 7 the Dbh variant is the basis for the reconstruction. There are
no variants in the available Tibetan material. The §£¶Ì of T1 (p. 196b19ff) and the §£ªP(¶X)¶P,
with variants, of T2 (p. 5964ff) also give no clue to the original Sanskrit. The introduction
is based on T1 p. 196b19,: ṃ–¬ƒºz™Ã¶≥§Q§ª™k§£©Û§§¶Ì which seems to have read dharma,
the probability of this reconstruction being strengthened by T2 (p. 5964) which has
ṛ∆ for ™k, also a common equivalent for dharma: ¶≥§Q§ªṛ∆§£ªPºz¶X.

de la ma rig pa’i ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas so źes bya ba la sogs pas ’khor ba’i rgyu srid
pa’i yan lag bcu gñis rnams daṅ lhan cig mi gnas par bstan te: de la ma rig pa ni yaṅ
dag pa’i mtha’ khoṅ du ma chud pa’o; ma rig pa de ñid ’grogs pa yin pas na ma rig pa’i ’grogs
pa ste, ma rig pa’i dbaṅ du gyur pa’am, ma rig pa daṅ ’dres par gyur pa’o. mi gnas so
źes bya ba ni de daṅ ma ’dres pa’am, ma ’bags pa źes bya ba’i don to. gal te rnam par mi rtog
pa’i ye śes de ma rig pa daṅ ’dres na ni gźan gyi dbaṅ gi mtshan ñid bźin du ’khor bar
lhuṅ ba’i skyon du ’gyur ro. de bźin du źes bya ba ni de daṅ ’dra ba źes bya ba’i don to.
’du byed rnams daṅ lhan cig mi gnas so źes bya ba nas yan lag lhag ma rnams la yaṅ de daṅ
’dra bar sbyar ro. de la ’du byed ni rnam pa gsum ste, bsod nams ma yin par ñe bar ’gro ba’i
’du byed daṅ, bsod nams su ñe bar ’gro ba’i ’du byed daṅ, mi g-yo bar ñe bar ’gro ba’i
’du byed do. rnam par śes pa ni sa bon thams cad kyi rten rnam par smin pa’i raṅ bźin kun
gźi rnam par śes pa’o. miṅ ni tshor ba daṅ ’du śes daṅ ’du byed daṅ rnam par śes pa rnams
so. gzugs ni bstan du yod la thogs pa daṅ bcas pa’am, bstan du med la thogs pa daṅ bcas pa
daṅ, bstan du yaṅ med la thogs pa yaṅ med pa ste, de gñis gcig tu bsdus na miṅ daṅ gzugs
źes bya’o. skye mched drug ni mig gi skye mched nas yid kyi skye mched kyi bar du’o. reg
pa ni yul daṅ dbaṅ po daṅ rnam par śes pa rnams rgyu daṅ ’bras bu’i mtshan ñīd du dus mñam
du tshogs pa’o. tshor ba ni bde ba daṅ sdug bsṅal ba daṅ bde ba yaṅ ma yin sdug bsṅal ba
yaṅ ma yin pa’i tshor ba rnams so. sred pa ni yul daṅ loṅs spyod la rgyun du spyod kyaṅ tshva
chu ’thuṅ ba daṅ ’dra bar ṅoms pa daṅ tshim pa med pa’o. len pa ni ’dod pa len pa daṅ,
tshul khrims daṅ brtul źugs len pa daṅ, lta ba len pa daṅ, bdag tu smra ba len pa daṅ. srid
pa ni ’dod pa’i srid pa daṅ, gzugs kyi srid pa daṅ, gzugs med pa’i srid pa’o. skye ba ni
las kyi bag chags rnam pa sna tshogs bags pa’i khyad par las ñiṅ mtshams sbyor ba de daṅ
de dag tu phuṅ po daṅ khams daṅ skye mched la sogs pa mṅon par grub pa’o. rga ba ni mer mer
po daṅ, nur nur po daṅ, mkhraṅ gyur pa daṅ, rkaṅ lag ’gyus pa nas gźon nu daṅ laṅ tsho
daṅ dar la bab pa’i stobs daṅ mthu daṅ gzi brjid daṅ mdaṅs la sogs pa rab tu gźan du gyur
te ñams pa’o. śi ba ni tshe daṅ drod daṅ rnam par śes pa med par gyur pa’o.

ma rig pa ’gog pa’i ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas so źes bya ba la sogs pas ma rig pa ’gags
pa la sogs pa ’khor ba las ldog pa’i rgyu rnam par byaṅ ba’i chos rnams daṅ yaṅ ma ’dres
pa bstan te, ma rig pa ’gags pa ni ma rig pa spaṅ ba’am, ma rig pa med par gyur nas de daṅ
mi mthun pa’i rig pa skyes pa la bya’o.

’jig tshogs la lta ba’i ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa źes bya ba la sogs pas log pa’i lta
ba rnams daṅ ma ’dres pa bstan te, de la ’jig tshogs źes bya ba ni gzugs la sogs pa phuṅ
po lṅa ’jig pa’i raṅ bźin can rnams phuṅ po daṅ tshogs su gyur pa la bya ste, de la bdag
yod par lta ba ni ’jig tshogs la lta ba’o. ’jig tshogs la lta ba de ñid rtsa ba yin pas na
’jig tshogs la lta ba’i rtsa ba ste, lta bar gyur pa thams cad kyi rgyu yin pa’i phyir ro
– tatrātmadṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ, saiva satkāyadṛṣṭir mūlam iti satkāyadṛṣṭimūlam, sarvadṛṣṭigatahetutvāt.lta
ba de’i rtsa ba las byuṅ ba ni lta bar gyur pa drug cu rtsa gñis po’i bar
dag ste, lta bar gyur pa drug cu rtsa gñis ni rtag par lta ba daṅ, mtha’ daṅ mtha’ med
par smra ba la sogs pa tshaṅs pa’i dra ba daṅ lṅa gsum pa la sogs pa las gsuṅs pa bźin du
rig par bya’o. bar dag ces smos pas ni bdag tu lta ba’i ri’i rtse mo ñi śu po gzugs la bdag
tu lta ba daṅ, bdag gzugs daṅ ldan pa daṅ, gzugs bdag gi yin pa daṅ, gzugs la bdag gnas
par lta ba daṅ, de bźin du tshor ba la sogs pa phuṅ po lhag ma bźi la yaṅ mthun mthun du sbyar
te, de dag la sogs pa lta bur gyur pa thams cad daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa źes bya ba’i
tha tshig go.Cf. Mvy 4684-4704: viṃśatiśikharasamudgataḥ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaḥ ...; Brahmajālasūtra;
lṅa gsum pa?; Aṣṭādaśa (57) p. 4426: satkāyadṛṣṭau dvāṣaṣṭidṛṣṭigatāny antargatāni
bhavanti.

mthon dman ni ’bras bu yin la, ’jig rten gyi chos ni rgyu yin te, ’di ltar rñed pa la sogs pas
ni mtho bar sems pa ’byuṅ la, ma rñed pa la sogs pa las mi dma’ bar sems pa ’byuṅ ba’i
phyir te, ’jig rten gyi chos brgyad po de dag gis sems kheṅs pa daṅ źum par mi ’gyur bas na
mthon dman gyi ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa nas ’jig rten gyi chos brgyad kyi bar gyi
’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas źes gsuṅs so. de la rñed pa daṅ ma rñed pa ni chos gos daṅ
lhuṅ bzed la sogs pa’o, sñan pa daṅ mi sñan pa ni yon tan daṅ skyon rnams so, smad pa daṅ
bstod pa ni skyon smos pa daṅ yon tan tshigs su bcad pas brjod pa’o, bde ba daṅ sdug bsṅal
ni lus daṅ sems la phan ’dogs pa daṅ gnod pa bskyed pa’o.

The different mental impurities (upakleśa) are explained in detail: khro ba daṅ khon du ’dzin
źes bya ba nas ñe ba’i ñon moṅs pa thams cad kyi bar gyi ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas
źes bya ba ñe ba’i ñon moṅs pa daṅ ma ’dres par bstan te: ṅa rgyal yaṅ sems ñe bar ñon moṅs
par byed pa’i sgo nas ñe ba’i ñon moṅs pa źes gdags so; cf. Kośa p. 3121-5: tatra ye yāvat
kleśā upakleśā api te, cittopakleśanāt.The following are abbreviated quotations from Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇavaibhāṣya
fol. 222a4ff and/or Triṃśikābhāṣya p. 303ff, on the basis of
which the present reconstructions of the ṭ text are made, but cf. the introduction. Abhidharmasamuccaya
p. 813ff, tib. 50b2ff treats the same concepts, but does not have the same text.de
la khro ba ni ’phral du gnod par byed pa la gnas te, sems kyi kun nas mnar sems pa’o
– tatra krodho vartamānam apakāram āgamya cetasa āghātaḥ. [For the equivalents āgam- and
gnas cf. Dbh index s.v.]. Triṃśikābhāṣya p. 303, tib. fol. 159a4-5; Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa
fol. 14a4, Dantinne p. 139; cf. Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇavaibhāṣya fol. 222a4.khon du ’dzin pa
ni khros pa’i ’og tu ’dis bdag la gnod pa ’di byas so źes śar gñer ba’i mdud par ’dzin pa
mi gtoṅ ba’o – upanāhaḥ krodhād ūrdhvaṃ mamānenedam apakṛtam iti vairānubandhasyānutsargaḥ.
Triṃś p. 306-8, tib. fol. 159a6-b1 = Pskvai fol. 222b1-2.’chab pa ni ’dun pa daṅ źe sdaṅ
daṅ ’jigs pa la sogs pa bsal te, phan par ’dod pa’i gleṅ ba pos: khyod ’di lta bu byed
pa’o, źes bsñad pa na kha na ma tho ba mkhyud pa’o – mrakṣaś chandadveṣabhayādīn nirākṛtya
taddhitaiṣiṇā codakena tat tvam evaṃkārīty anuyuktasyāvadyapracchādanā. Triṃś p. 3010-12,
tib. fol. 159b1-3 = Pskvai fol. 222b2-4.yoṅs su gduṅ ba ni tshig brlaṅ pos gźan gyi sems
gduṅ bar bskyed pa’o – paridāhaś caṇḍena vacasā parapradāśitā. Triṃś p. 3015ff, tib. fol.
159b3ff = Pskvai fol. 222b3ff. The words paridāha (ṭ) and pradāsa (-śa) are given the same
meaning, cf. Edg s. v. pradāsa; Triṃś and Pskvai have tshig brlaṅ po.phrag dog ni pha rol
po’i rñed pa daṅ, bkur sti daṅ, rigs daṅ, tshul khrims daṅ, thos pa la sogs pa’i yon tan
mthoṅ nas źe sdaṅ gi char gtogs pa’i sems khoṅ nas ’khrug pa’o – īrṣyā lābhasatkārakulaśīlaśrutādīn
guṇān parasyopalabhya dveṣāṃśiko cetaso vyāroṣaḥ. Triṃś p. 3020ff, tib. fol. 159b6ff
~ Pskvai fol. 222b7f.ser sna ni rñed pa daṅ bkur sti la źen nas ’dod chags kyi sems kyis
phyi daṅ naṅ gi dṅos po mi gtoṅ ba’o – mātsaryaṃ lābhasatkārādhyavasitasya rāgacetasā
bāhyādhyātmavastvaparityāgaḥ. Triṃś p. 3024ff, tib. fol. 160a1ff = Pskvai fol. 223a1ff.sgyu
ni rñed pa daṅ bkur sti la lhag par chags pas gźan la bslu ba’i bsama pas tshul khrims la
sogs pa’i don gźan du gnas la gźan du ston pa’o – māyā lābhasatkārādhyavasitasya paravañcanābhiprāyeṇānyavasthitasya
śīlāder arthasyānyathā prakāśanā. Triṃś p. 3029ff, tib. fol.
160a3ff = Pskvai fol. 223a3ff.g-yo ni bdag gi ñes pa bcab pa’i thabs bzuṅ ste, gźan nas gźan
du sgyur źiṅ gtam rluṅ la bskur pa daṅ, gsal bar mi byed pa’o – śāṭhyaṃ svadoṣapracchādanopāyasaṃgṛhītaṃ,
anyenānyat pratisaran vikṣipati, aparisphuṭaṃ vā pratipadyate. Triṃś p.
313ff, tib. fol. 160a3ff = Pskvai fol. 223a5ff.ṅo tsha med pa ni las de bdag gi cha ma yin
par śes kyaṅ kha na ma tho bas mi ’dzems pa’o – āhrīkyaṃ tasmin karmaṇy ātmānam ayogyaṃ
manyamānasyāpy avadyenālajjā. Triṃś p. 3117f, tib. fol. 160b5f = Pskvai fol. 224a1ff.khrel
med pa ni gźan la kha na ma tho bas mi ’dzems pa’o – anapatrāpyaṃ parato ’vadyenālajjā. Triṃś
p. 3118f, tib. fol. 160b6f treated also in Pskvai fol. 224a2, but in even shorter form,
just noting it is the opposite of the former upakleśa. The section on upakleśa ends after
this item in both Triṃś and Pskvai.ṭ fol. 105a5-b6:kheṅs pa ni ’dod chags śas che ba’i
dbaṅ gis lus kyi ’gyur ba rkaṅ lag brkyaṅ ba daṅ, mgo ’phaṅ bstod pa daṅ, smin ma bsdus pa
daṅ, so gtsigs pa la sogs pa ’gyiṅ bar snaṅ ba ste, mkhan po daṅ slob dpon daṅ bla ma la
sogs pa la thal mo sbyar ba daṅ, ’dud pa la sogs pa’i las mi byed pa’o – unnati, not identified
as quotation.rtsod pa ni de dag gi rgyu las lus daṅ ṅag gi las rdeg pa daṅ, ’chiṅ ba
daṅ, skyon smos pa daṅ, mtshaṅ ’dru ba la sogs pa byed pa’o – vivāda, not identified as quotation.rgyags
pa ni bdag gi rigs daṅ, nad med pa daṅ, gzugs daṅ laṅ tsho la sogs pa raṅ
gi phun sum tshogs pa la dga’ ba’i bye brag daṅ ldan pa’i sred pas sems raṅ dbaṅ med par byed
pa’o – madaḥ svakulārogyarūpayauvanasvasaṃpattiharṣaviśeṣā tṛṣṇā cittam asvatantrīkriyate.
Triṃś p. 319ff, tib. fol. 160b1ff ~ Pskvai fol. 224a1-4. This paragraph is quoted from
Pskvai, as this work includes a short sentence on sred pa (fol. 224a4: dga’ ba’i bye brag
daṅ ldan pa’i sred pa’i rnam pa), which Triṃś does not have.bag med pa ni ’dod chags daṅ
źe sdaṅ daṅ gti mug gi dbaṅ gis dge ba mi sgom źiṅ mi dge ba byed pa’o – pramādo lobhadveṣamohavaśāt
kuśalaṃ na bhāvayaty akuśalaṃ karoti; similar to Psk fol. 14b2 (Dantinne p. 140
§17) but quotes, rather, and abbreviates Triṃśikābhāṣya p. 323-5. Triṃś 324-5 ~ Pskvai fol.
224b1-2, but this piece is not in ṭ.The following passages on the seven kinds of conceit
are quoted with minor differences from Triṃśikābhāṣya p. 2828ff; the text given is the
reconstruction of the text in ṭ. sapta mānāḥ are treated otherwise in Kośa p. 28423ff; Abhidharmasamuccaya
rec. p. 457-13, tib. fol. 79b4-80a1, tr. p. 72 = Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa fol.
13a7-b4 (Dantinne p. 137); Ybh p. 505-6;Mvy 1946-1952.ṅa rgyal ni rigs daṅ śes rgya daṅ
nor la sogs pas dma’ ba bas de dag gis bdag che’o sñam du sems kheṅs pa’am, rigs la sogs
pa mtshuṅs pa ñid la de dag daṅ bdag mtshuṅs so sñam du sems kheṅs pa’o – hīnāt kulavijñānavittādibhiḥ
śreyān āsmi tair iti cittasyonnatir, sadṛśena vā kulādibhir eva sadṛśo ’smīti
cittasyonnatir mānaḥ. From Triṃś p. 294-6, tib. fol. 158a5-6 = Pskvai fol. 217a7-b2.lhag
pa’i ṅa rgyal ni rigs daṅ śes rgya la sogs pas mtshuṅs pa bas gtoṅ ba daṅ tshul khrims daṅ
ñams rtsal la sogs pas bdag che’o sñam pa’am, rigs daṅ nor la sogs pas che ba la bdag daṅ
mtshuṅs so sñam du sems kheṅs pa’o – kulavijñānādibhiḥ sadṛśāt tyāgaśīlapauruṣādibhir śreyān
asmi, śreyasā vā kulavittādibhir sadṛśo ’smīti cittasyonnatir atimānaḥ. From Triṃś p.
296-8, tib. fol. 158a6-7 = Pskvai fol. 217b1-2.ṅa rgyal las kyaṅ ṅa rgyal ni rigs la sogs
pa che ba bas kyaṅ bdag che’o sñam du sems kheṅs pa’o – śreyasaḥ kulādibhir aham eva śreyān
iti cittasyonnatir mānātimānaḥ. From Triṃś p. 299-10, tib. fol. 158a7 = Pskvai fol. 217b2-3.ṅa’o
sñam pa’i ṅa rgyal ni ñe bar len pa’i phuṅ po la bdag daṅ bdag gi daṅ bral ba de
dag la bdag daṅ bdag gir mṅon par źen nas sems kheṅs pa’o – teṣūpādānaskandheṣv ātmātmīyarahiteṣv
ātmātmīyābhiniveśaś cittasyonnatir asmimānaḥ. From Triṃś p. 2910-11, tib. fol. 158a7-b1
~ Pskvai fol. 217b3-6, which expands Triṃś.cuṅ zad sñam pa’i ṅa rgyal ni rigs daṅ śes
rgya daṅ nor la sogs pas khyad ches ’phags pa la bdag cuṅ zad cig gis chuṅ ṅo sñam du sems
kheṅs pa’o – bahvantaraviśiṣṭāt kulavijñānavittādibhir alpāntarahīno ’smīti cittasyonnatir
ūnamānaḥ. From Triṃś p. 2913-14, tib. fol. 158b2-3 ~ Pskvai, which expands Triṃś in fol.
218a1-4.mṅon pa’i ṅa rgyal ni yon tan khyad par can ’bras bu daṅ bsam gtan la sogs pa ma
thob pa thob bo sñam du sems kheṅs pa’o – aprāpteṣu viśeṣaguṇeṣu phaladhyānādiṣu prāptā
[mayeti] cittasyonnatir abhimānaḥ. From Triṃś p. 2911-12, tib. fol. 158b1-2 ~ Pskvai, which
expands Triṃś in fol. 217b6-218a1.log pa’i ṅa rgyal ni yon tan ma yin pa daṅ ldan pa la
bdag yon tan daṅ ldan no sñam du sems kheṅs pa’o – aguṇavato guṇavān asmīti cittasyonnatir
mithyāmānaḥ. From Triṃś p. 2914-15, tib. fol. 158b3 ~ Pskvai, which expands Triṃś in fol.
218a4-6.ñe ba’i ñon moṅs pa thams cad kyi źes bya bas ni goṅ du miṅ gis smos pa’i ñe ba’i
ñon moṅs pa rnams daṅ mi ’grogs par ma zad kyi, gźan yaṅ ñe ba’i ñon moṅs pa rnam par g-yeṅ
ba daṅ, śes bźin med pa daṅ, ’gyod pa daṅ, gñid la sogs pa daṅ yaṅ mi ’grogs so źes bya
ba’i tha tshig go.

’dod chags daṅ, źe sdaṅ daṅ, gti mug gi kun nas ldaṅ ba źes bya ba la sogs pa ñon moṅs pa rnams
daṅ lhan (114a) cig mi gnas par bstan te,ṭ. fol. 105b7-106a2 seems quoted from Triṃśikābhāṣya
p. 2813ff:’dod chags ni srid pa daṅ srid pa’i loṅs spyod la chags śiṅ smon pa’o –
rāgo bhavabhogayor adhyavasānaṃ prārthanā. Triṃś p. 2813-14, tib. fol. 157b2 = Pskvai fol.
214a2;źe sdaṅ ni sems can rnams la kun nas mnar sems pa ste, gaṅ gi dbaṅ gis sems can rnams
la gsod pa daṅ ’chiṅ ba la sogs pa byed pa’o – dveṣaḥ sattveṣv āghāto yadvaśāt sattvānāṃ
vadhabandhanādikarmakaḥ. Quotes from Triṃś p. 2816-23, tib. fol. 157b2-7 = Pskvai fol. 216b7-217a4;gti
mug gis ṅan soṅ daṅ, mtho ris daṅ, mya ṅan las ’das pa daṅ, de dag thob par
byed pa’i rgyu daṅ, de dag gi rgyu daṅ ’bras bu ’brel pa phyin ci ma log par mi śes pa’o
– moho ’pāyeṣu svarge nirvāṇe tatpratiṣṭhāpakeṣu hetuṣu teṣāṃ cāviparīte hetuphalasaṃbandhe
’jñānam. Triṃś p. 2823-24, tib. fol. 157b7.Cf. Abhidharmasamuccaya p. 71-5, tib. fol. 49a6-7
is not the same.ṭ. fol. 106a2-7: kun nas ldaṅ ba ni de dag skye ba’i rgyu daṅ rkyen phrad
nas mṅon du ’byuṅ ba ste, de yaṅ yul ñe bar gyur la, tshul bźin ma yin pa yid la byed
pa daṅ ldan źes gsuṅs pa’i phyir ro. ñon moṅs pa de dag kyaṅ mthoṅ ba’i lam gyis spaṅ bar
dka’ ba daṅ sla ba’i bye brag gis phra mo daṅ sbom po źes bya ba la, bsgom pa’i lam gyis
spaṅ bar sla ba daṅ, dka’ ba daṅ, śin tu dka’ ba’i bye brag gis chuṅ ṅu daṅ, ’briṅ daṅ, chen
po źes bya ste, bsgom pa’i lam chen po’i chen po la sogs pa dgus spaṅs pa’i ñon moṅs pa
rnams la bya’o; yaṅ na ’jig rten las ’das pa’i lam gyis spaṅ bar bya ba ni bag chags daṅ
bcas te, spaṅ bar bya ba yin pas spaṅ dka’ ba’i phyir phra mo źes bya la, ’jig rten pa’i lam
gyis spaṅ bar bya ba ni spaṅ sla bas sbom po źes bya’o; yaṅ na gaṅ zag ñon moṅs pa’i śas
chuṅ ba rnams kyis ni phra mo yin la, gaṅ zag ñon moṅs pa śas che ba rnams kyis ni sbom
po źes bya’o; yaṅ na gzugs daṅ gzugs med pa’i khams su gtogs pa’i ñon moṅs pa rnams ni kha
naṅ du bltas pa yin pas phra mo źes bya la, ’dod pa’i khams kyi ñon moṅs pa rnams kyis ni
’dod pa’i yon tan lṅa la chags te, kha phyir bltas pa yin pas sbom po źes bya’o. ñon moṅs
pa’i kun nas ldaṅ ba thams cad kyi bar źes bya ba ni ñon moṅs pa de dag gsum daṅ yaṅ mi ’grogs
par yaṅ ma zad kyi, gźan yaṅ the tshom daṅ, mdud pa daṅ, ’chiṅ ba la sogs pa daṅ mi
’grogs par ston to.Notes to the Sanskrit: 1) Triṃś, Pskvai pratighaḥ 2) Triṃś, Pskvai yenāviṣṭaḥ
3) Triṃś vadhabandhanādikam anarthaṃ cintayati, but Triṃś tib. has gsod pa daṅ ’chiṅ
ba la sogs pa’i gnod pa bya bar sems so which suggests vadhabandhanādikaraṇaṃ (-kāryaṃ?)
cintayati, -karmaka is by analogy with the use of this word in Triṃś p. 2818 et passim. 4)
As ṭ mtho ris for Triṃś sugatau tib. bde ’gro 5) Triṃś ins. yad

gti mug gi mun pa daṅ, rab rib kyi liṅ tog daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pas ñams par ’gyur ba’i chos
rnams daṅ lhan cig mi gnas par bstan te, goṅ du ñon moṅs pa’i naṅ du yaṅ gti mug smos mod
kyi, mdo las: rmoṅs pa med pa la gźan mi ’byuṅ ṅo, źes gsuṅs te, ñon moṅs pa thams cad
’byuṅ ba’i gźi gti mug yin pas ’dir logs śig tu yaṅ smos so. gti mug ñid mun pa yin pas na
gti mug gi mun pa ste, dper na mun pas dṅos (Q 130a) po rnams mi mthoṅ źiṅ log par mthoṅ
ba, de bźin du gti mug gis kyaṅ sdug bsṅal la bde bar mthoṅ bas na gti mug gi mun pa źes bya’o;
rab rib ñid liṅ tog yin pas na rab rib kyi liṅ tog ste, liṅ tog daṅ ’dra bar tshe rabs
gźan gyi ñes dmigs yod, yaṅ dag pa yaṅ mi mthoṅ ba’i phyir ro; gaṅ gi phyir sgrib par gyur
pa, de’i phyir chod pa źes bya ste, rtsig pas chod pa’i pha rol na dṅos po yod pa ma mthoṅ
ba bźin du tshe ’di’i ñes dmigs yod, yaṅ dag pa yaṅ śin tu mi mthoṅ ba’i phyir ro. yaṅ
na tshe rabs gźan gyi las daṅ ñon moṅs pa’i mtshan ñid mi śes pa ni gti mug pa’o, las daṅ
ñon moṅs pa de’i ’bras bu sdug bsṅal gyi bdag ñid gnod pa du ma’i raṅ bźin can gyi mtshan
ñid mi śes pa ni mun pa’o; tshe ’di’i las daṅ ñon moṅs pa rnams mi śes pa ni rab rib bo,
ñon moṅs pa de’i rgyus tshe ’di la gnod pa sna tshogs ’byuṅ ba daṅ phuṅ po ñid kyaṅ sdug
bsṅal sna tshogs kyi raṅ bźin can du mi śes pa ni liṅ tog go; las gaṅ byas pas tshe rabs gźan
du ’bras bu gaṅ thob par mi śes pa ni sgrib pa’o, ’bras bu de dag kyaṅ tshe ’di nas ma
’phos pa daṅ raṅ bźin med par mi śes pa ni chod pa’o. ñams par ’gyur ba’i cha daṅ mthun pa’i
chos kun nas ldaṅ ba thams cad kyi bar gyi ’grogs pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas źes bya ba ni
ñams par ’gyur ba’i chos de rnams daṅ lhan cig mi gnas par yaṅ ma zad kyi, gźan yaṅ ñon
moṅs pa’i phyogs su gtogs pa’i chos yon tan daṅ sa rim pa goṅ ma la sogs pa ’thob pa las kyaṅ
ñams par ’gyur, (Q 130b) ma thob pa yaṅ thob par mi ’gyur ba rnams daṅ lhan cig mi ’grogs
so źes bya ba’i don to.

’dod pa daṅ ’thab mo’i rñog pa daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pas bdud kyi phyogs su gtogs pa’i skyon
rnams daṅ, bdud daṅ bdud kyi las rnams spaṅs pa bstan te, ’dod pa ni gzugs la sogs pa ’dod
pa lṅa’i yon tan la bya’o, ’thab mo’i don ni sṅar smras pa bźin te, ’dod pa daṅ ’thab mo
de dag ñid rñog pa daṅ ’dra bas na rñog pa źes bya’o.The commentary on māra and mārakarma
is based upon quotations from Śbh:ṭ. fol. 107a2-b4: bdud bźi la gzugs la sogs pas ñe bar
len pa’i phuṅ po lṅa ni phuṅ po’i bdud do. khams gsum spyod pa’i ñon moṅs pa thams cad ni
ñon moṅs pa’i bdud do. sems can de daṅ de dag sems can gyi ris mthun pa de daṅ de dag nas
śi ’phos pa ni ’chi bdag gi bdud do. gaṅ dag dge ba’i phyogs la rab tu źugs nas phuṅ po daṅ,
ñon moṅs pa daṅ, ’chi bdag gi bdud las ’da’ bar ’dod pa’i khams su skyes pa’i lha’i bu
dbaṅ phyug chen po rñed pa bar chad bya ba’i phyir ñe bar lhags pa rnams ni lha’i bu’i bdud
do.Śbh fol. 11B15-6, S p. 3444-454, D fol. 126a3-5, not in W: paṃcopādānaskandhāḥ skandhamāraḥ
/ traidhātukāvacārāḥ kleśāḥ kle(6)śamāraḥ / teṣāṃ teṣāṃ satvānāṃ tasmāt tasmāt sattvanikāyāt
yan maraṇaṃ kālakriyā maraṇamāraḥ / yo ’sya kuśalapakṣaprayuktasya skandhakleśamṛtyusamatikramāya
kāmadhātūpapanno devaputra aiśvaryaprāpto ’ntarāyam upasaṃharati vyākṣepakaraṇe
/ ayam ucyate devaputramāraḥ / Śbh goes into further details on devaputramāra fol.
11B16ff, S p. 3454-21, D fol.126a5ff.ṭ. fol. 107a4-5: bdud kyi las thams cad kyi bar daṅ
lhan cig mi gnas so źes bya ba ni gaṅ ’dod pa lṅa’i yon tan la chags pa daṅ, srog gcod pa
la sogs pa sdig pa mi dge ba’i las rnams daṅ, gźan yaṅ de kho na rtogs pa’i bar du gcod pa
rtog pa daṅ rnam par rtog pa la sogs pa bdud kyi glags rñed par ’gyur ba’i las thams cad
bdud kyi las su śes par bya’o ; not in Śbh: – "’It (prajñā) does not stay with any of the
actions of the Evil One’ it is said in the text; actions of the Evil One are attachment to
the five kinds of desired sense objects (pañcakāmaguṇa), the sinful (pāpaka) and bad actions
(akuśalakarma) like killing (prāṇātipāta), etc., but further it is the thought-constructions
and fictions (kalpavikalpa) which hinder the understanding of the things themselves
(tattvāvabodha), it is all the actions where the Evil One finds weak points to attack (avatāra)".ṭ.
fol. 107a5-6: de yaṅ mdor bstan na gaṅ a la la źig thar bar ’gyur bas mṅon par
bsdus (Q 130b8, N 115b) pa mya ṅan las ’das pa daṅ rjes su mthun pa’i dge ba’i chos la dad
pa yaṅ dag par skyes pa na ’dod pa la chags pa’i dbaṅ du gyur nas ldog pa ni bdud kyi las
so – Śbh fol. 11B19-11A23, S p. 34522-34620, D fol. 126b2-127a2: tatra mārakarmāṇi / yasya
kasyacit kuśaladharmacchandaḥ samutpanno naiṣkramyopasaṃhitaḥ / kāmagredham adhipatiṃ kṛtvāpavarttate
/ veditavyaṃ mārakarmai(11A2)tad iti /ṭ. fol. 107a6-7: dbaṅ po’i sgo bsdams
te gnas pa na gaṅ chags par ’gyur ba’i gzugs daṅ, sgra daṅ, dri daṅ, ro daṅ, reg bya daṅ,
chos rnams la mtshan mar ’dzin ciṅ mṅon rtogs su ’dzin pa ni bdud kyi las so – indriyair
guptadvārasya viharataḥ / yasya raṃjanīyeṣu rūpeṣu śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmeṣu nimittagrāhitāyām
abhisamayagrāhitāyāṃ cittaṃ praskandati / veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /ṭ. fol.
107a7-b1: de bźin du zas kyi tshod rig par gnas pa na ro’i khyad par la sems chags pa daṅ,
nam gyi cha stod daṅ cha smad la mi ñal bar rjes su sbyor ba na gñid kyi bde ba daṅ, ñal
ba’i bde ba daṅ, glos ’bebs pa’i bde ba la chags śiṅ sems ’jug pa ni bdud kyi las su rigs
par bya’o – evaṃ bhojaneṣu mātrajñasya viharataḥ praṇīteṣu raseṣu [chandarāgam] anunayena
cittaṃ praskandati / [bhaktavaiṣamye evaṃ] pūrvvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyo(2)gam anuyuktasya
viharataḥ / nidrāsukhe śayanasukhe pārśvasukhe cittaṃ praskandhati / veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad
iti /ṭ. fol. 107b1-3: śes bźin daṅ bcas par gnas pa ni byis pa’am ’gro ba bzaṅ
mo kha dog mchog daṅ ldan pa’i rnams mthoṅ nas tshul bźin ma yin pa yid la byed ciṅ der sems
’jug pa daṅ, ’jig rten gyi ’phral gyi bya ba maṅ po la sems ’jug pa daṅ, ’du ’dzi maṅ po’i
naṅ du ’drea źiṅ sdig pa’i grogs po mi dge ba’i las byed pa rnams mthoṅ nas sems la mos
pa skye ba ni bdud kyi las so – tathā saṃprajānadvihāriṇo viharataḥ / abhikramapratikramādiṣu
śiśum udāravarṇṇaṃ raṃjanīyaṃ mātṛgrāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā ayoniśo nimittagrāheṇa cittaṃ praskandati
/ lokacitrāṇi vā dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ praskandati / bahvarthatāyāṃ bahu(3)kṛtyatāyāṃ cittaṃ
prakandati / tad yathā gṛhasthapravrajitaiḥ saṃsargarāmatāyāṃ pāpamitraiḥ saha ekasya vāsitāyāṃ
dṛṣṭyanumataye cittaṃ praskandati / veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti //ṭ. fol. 107b3: de
bźin du saṅs rgyas daṅ, chos daṅ, dge ’dun daṅ, sdug bsṅal daṅ, kun ’byuṅ daṅ, ’gog pa daṅ,
lam daṅ, tshe ’di daṅ, tshe rabs pha rol rnams la the tshom daṅ yid gñis skye ba ni bdud
kyi las so – tathā buddhe dharme saṃghe duḥkhe samudaye nirodhe mārge / ihaloke paraloke
kāṃkṣāvimataya utpadyante / veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /ṭ. fol. 107b3-4: gaṅ gi tshe rñed
pa daṅ bkur sti la sems chags pa daṅ, ser sna daṅ, ’dod chen daṅ, chog mi śes pa daṅ,
khro ba daṅ, khon du ’dzin pa daṅ, tshul ’chos pa daṅ, kha gsag la sems ’jug na bdud kyi las
su rig par bya’o – Śbh fol. 11A22-4, S p. 3473-6, D fol. 127a4-5: yadā lābhasatkāre cittaṃ
pra(5)skandati / mātsarye mahecchatāyāṃ asaṃtuṣṭau / krodhopanāhakuhanālapanādiṣu [śramaṇālaṃkāravipakṣeṣu
dharmeṣu] cittaṃ praskandati / veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti /After the
statement in ṭ. fol. 107b4-5: gźan yaṅ rgyas par bśad na, de la sogs pa bdud kyi las tshad
med par yod de, ’jam dpal rnam par ’phrul ba las kyaṅ: "Further, if speaking extensively,
these and the other works of the Evil One are immeasurable (apramāṇa) ...", ṭ. then fol.
107b5-109a5 quotes a long passage from Mañjuśrīvikurvāṇaparivarta on the topic of Works
of the Evil One, which enumerates twenty kinds: lha’i bu ji tsam du las rnams ’byuṅ ba de
tsam du bdud kyi las so. ji tsam du smon pa daṅ, ji tsam du log par ’dzin pa daṅ, ji tsam
du mchog tu ’dzin pa, de tsam du bdud kyi las so. ji tsam du ’dod pa daṅ, ji tsam du ’du śes
pa daṅ, ji tsam du rlom sems pa daṅ, ji tsam du yoṅs su rtog pa, de tsam du bdud kyi las
so. lha’i bu, gźan yaṅ byaṅ chub kyi sems la mṅon par źen pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so, sbyin
pa’i sems la mṅon par źen pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so, tshul khrims daṅ bzod pa daṅ brtson ’grus
daṅ bsam gtan daṅ śes rab kyi sems la mṅon par źen pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. sbyin pa’i rlom
sems su byed pa, daṅ tshul khrims mchog tu ’dzin pa daṅ, bzod pa ’dzin pa daṅ, brtson ’grus
len pa daṅ, bsam gtan la mtshan ma daṅ, śes rab rgyu ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so. dgon pa
la dga’ źiṅ mos pa’i sems daṅ, btaṅ sñoms su ltuṅ ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so. ’dod pa ñuṅ ba daṅ,
chog śes pa daṅ, sbyaṅs pa’i yon tan daṅ, yo byad bsñuṅs pa rlom sems su byed pa yaṅ bdud
kyi las so. bdag ni stoṅ pa ñid la gnas pa, bdag ni mtshan ma med pa la gnas pa, bdag
ni smon pa med pa la gnas pa, bdag ni spros pa med pa la gnas pa, bdag ni de bźin gśegs pa’i
bka’ sgrub ciṅ gnas pa’o, sñam du rlom sems su byed ciṅ rnam par rtog pa yaṅ bdud kyi las
so. lha’i bu, rtog pa daṅ, rnam par rtog pa daṅ, yoṅs su rtog pa daṅ, mthoṅ ba daṅ, thos
pa daṅ, bye brag phyed pa daṅ, rnam par śes pa’i gnas ji tsam pa, de tsam du bdud kyi las
so. lha’i bus smras pa: ’jam dpal, bdud kyi las ga las byuṅ? ’jam dpal gyis smras pa: lha’i
bu, bdud kyi las ni brtson ’grus las byuṅ ṅo. de ci’i phyir źe na? lha’i bu, brtson pa
la bdud glags tshol gyi, mi brtson pa la bdud kyis ci źig bya bar ’gyur , de ñid bdud kyi
las yin no. lha’i bus smras pa: ’jam dpal, byaṅ chub sems dpa’ ji ltar na brtson pa yin,
ji ltar na mi brtson pa yin? ’jam dpal gyis smras pa: lha’i bu, ji tsam du gñis la sbyor ba,
de tsam du brtson pa ma yin no. de ci’i phyir źe na? ’jig rten gnas pa ni gñis la sbyor
ba daṅ ldan no. lha’i bu, brtson pa źes bya ba ’di ni sbyor ba yaṅ dag pa’i tshig bla dags
so. sbyor ba yaṅ dag pa źes bya ba ’di ni sbyor ba med pa’i tshig bla dags so. sbyor ba
med pa źes bya ba ’di ni spros pa med pa’i tshig bla dags so. spros pa med pa źes bya ba ’di
ni sbyor ba yaṅ dag pa’i tshig bla dvags so. lha’i bu, gaṅ na mig la mi sbyor ba daṅ, gzugs
la mi sbyor ba ’di ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i sbyor ba yaṅ dag pa źes bya, gaṅ na rna ba
la mi sbyor ba daṅ, sgra la mi sbyor ba daṅ, sna la mi sbyor ba daṅ, dri la mi sbyor ba daṅ,
lce la mi sbyor ba daṅ, ro la mi sbyor ba daṅ, lus la mi sbyor ba daṅ, reg bya la mi sbyor
ba daṅ, yid la mi sbyor ba daṅ, chos la mi sbyor ba ’di ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i sbyor
ba yaṅ dag pa źes bya’o. yaṅ de bźin du lha’i bu, ñi śu po ’di dag ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’
rnams kyi bdud kyi las yaṅ dag phul yin no. ñi śu gaṅ źe na? ’di lta ste: 1) rnal ’byor spyod
pa rnam par grol ba ’dod ciṅ ’khor bas skrag pa rnams la bsñen pa daṅ, bsten pa daṅ,
bsñen bkur byed pa ni bdud kyi las so. 2) stoṅ pa ñid la so sor rtog ciṅ sems can yal bar
’dor ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 3) ’dus ma byas la so sor rtog ciṅ ’dus byas kyi dge ba’i rtsa
bas yoṅs su skyo ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 4) bsam gtan bskyed ciṅ bsam gtan las rnam par
mi ldog pa tshol ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 5) chos ston kyaṅ chos ñan pa rnams la sñiṅ rje chen
po mi skyed pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 6) yon tan daṅ ldan pa daṅ sbyin gnas tshol bźin du
tshul khrims ’chal pa rnams la khro ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 7) ñan thos daṅ raṅ saṅs rgyas
kyi gtam ston ciṅ theg pa chen po’i gtam ’chab pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 8) zab mo’i gtam
’chab ciṅ gtam sna tshogs ston pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 9) byaṅ chub sems dpa’i lam śes kyaṅ
pha rol tu phyin pa’i lam yoṅs su mi tshol ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 10) rab tu brtson pa’i
bsṅags pa thob kyaṅ sems can mi brtson pa rnams mṅon par mi sbyor ba yaṅ bdud kyi las so.
11) dge ba’i rtsa ba stsogs kyaṅ byaṅ chub kyi sems mṅon du mi byed pa yaṅ bdud kyi las
so. 12) lhag mthoṅ gi rnal ’byor daṅ ldan par gnas kyaṅ sems can rnams lhag mthoṅ dag par
’dzin du mi ’jug pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 13) ñon moṅs pa ma lus par zad pa tshol źiṅ ’khor
ba’i rgyun gyi ñon moṅs pa rnams la smod pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 14) śes rab kyis rnam par
dpyod ciṅ sñiṅ rje chen po la dmigs pa mi ’dzin pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 15) thabs daṅ mi
ldan par dge ba spyod pa thams cad kyaṅ bdud kyi las so. 16) byaṅ chub sems dpa’i sde snod
mi tshol gyi ’jig rten rgyaṅ phan pa’i gsaṅ tshig ’dzin pa yaṅ bdud kyi las so. 17) maṅ
du thos kyaṅ gźan gyi śes kyis dogs te, chos la slob dpon gyi dpe mkhyud byed pa yaṅ bdud
kyi las so. 18) ’jig rten pa’i dgos pa’i źal ta byed ciṅ maṅ du thos pa mi tshol ba yaṅ bdud
kyi las so. 19) byaṅ chub sems dpa’ chos smra ba theg pa chen po la yaṅ dag par źugs pa
skal pa mñam pa rnams la mi bsten, mi bsñen, bsñen bkur mi byed kyi, ñan thos daṅ raṅ saṅs
rgyas kyi theg pa la yaṅ dag par źugs pa skal pa mi mñām pa la dga’ ba yaṅ bdud kyi las
so. 20) gaṅ gi tshe brgya byin nam, tshaṅs pa’am, ’jig rten skyoṅ ba’am, rgyal po’am, tshoṅ
dpon nam, khyim bdag gi loṅs spyod daṅ, nor daṅ, rin po che daṅ, dbaṅ phyug gi che ba ñid
du gyur pa, de’i tshe chos kyi che ba ñid daṅ ldan pa rnams la mi bsten, mi bsñen, bsñen
bkur mi byed pa, ’di dag ni, lha’i bu, byaṅ chub sems dpa’ rnams kyi bdud kyi las yaṅ dag
phul ñi śu’o źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅs te . The quotation also has special relevance to
the concept of yuganaddha as described in Akṣ.For further information one is refered to
Śata and other sūtras: śes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa stoṅ phrag brgya ba la sogs pa mdo
de daṅ de dag gi naṅ nas gsuṅs pa’i bdud kyi las rnams la yaṅ bya bar rig par bya’o.The Lokottaraparivarta
quoted in Śikṣ. p. 1511ff mentions ten kinds of mārakarma. Śbh gives a bibliography
on p. 343 n. 2.Notes to the Sanskrit text: 1) S om. kleśamāraḥ 2) S satv... MS,
S ins. daṇḍa 3) As D and ṭ .. nas MS, S ...āḥ for ...āt 4) S ya(yādya)n 5) S yopyakuśala...
6) MS, S ...aḥ / 7) MS ..prāptaḥ / an... S niścayaprāptaḥ an... 8) MS, S ins. daṇḍa. Both
D (fol. 126a4 bar chad bya ba [daṅ rnam par g-yeṅ bar bya ba]’i phyir .... ñe bar logs
so) and ṭ seem to have read antarāya - upasaṃkramati for ’ntarāyam upasaṃharati 9) As D dge
ba’i chos la ’dun pa MS kuśalo dharma.. S karmaṇo dharmacch... 10) S kṛtvā pravarttante
11) S sahagatvarasampraṣṭavyadharmeṣu 12) As D, ṭ mṅon rtogs su ’dzin pa MS, S anuvyaṃjanagrāhitāyāṃ
13) D mi mthun pa dag la seems to read pratikūleṣu, but ṭ khyad par la suits praṇīteṣu
14) Bracketed part not in ṭ 15) D reads veditavyaṃ mārakarmaitad iti / for bhaktavaîṣamye
D should be preferred in accordance with the structure of the text, but ṭ om. both,
which may imply that the reading of MS is a very old one. 16) S ...rva... for ...rvva...

S saha ekavyavasitāyāṃ MS ins. daṇḍa after ...tāyāṃ. ekasya has no counterpart in D

bdag daṅ, sems can daṅ, srog daṅ, gso ba źes bya ba la sogs pas bdag tu ’dzin pa la mṅon par
chags pa daṅ ma ’dres pa bstan te, bdag la sogs pa thams cad kyaṅ bdag tu ’dod pa’i rnam
graṅs te, de dag kyaṅ bdag can rtag par smra ba daṅ, gźuṅ gcig mod kyi, grub pa’i mtha’ tha
dad pa las mtshan ñid mi mthun pa tsam gyis phye ste, miṅ so sor btags nas gźag pa’o. ’dzin
pa la mṅon par źen ces bya ba’i sgra bdag daṅ sems can la sogs pa’i tshig re re daṅ yaṅ
sbyar te, bdag tu ’dzin pa la mṅon par źen ces bya ba daṅ, sems can du ’dzin pa la mṅon
par źen ces bya ba la sogs par sbyar ro. bdag la sogs pa ’di dag gi khyad par ni sṅar bśad
par zad do. ’dzin pa la mṅon par źen pa thams cad kyi bar daṅ lhan cig mi gnas so źes bya
ba’i bdag tu ’dzin pa goṅ du smos pa rnams daṅ lhan cig mi gnas par yaṅ ma zad kyi, gźan
yaṅ bdag tu ’dzin pa dbaṅ phyug daṅ, gtso bo daṅ, dus la sogs pa yod par sems pa rnams daṅ
lhan cig mi gnas so źes bya ba’i don to.

las kyi sgrib pa daṅ chos kyi sgrib pa daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pas bag chags kyi mtshams sbyor
ba sgrib pa rnams daṅ ma ’dres pa bstan te, las kyi sgrib pa ni tshe ’di ñid la mtshams
med pa lṅa’i las byas pas las des tshe de la bden pa mthoṅ ba la bar du gcod pa ni las kyi
sgrib pa’o. chos la ser sna byed ciṅ mos pa bzlog pa la sogs pa chos thos pa’i bar du gcod
pa’i las rnams byas pas tshe rabs de daṅ de dag tu dge ba’i bśes gñen la sogs pa daṅ mi
ldan źiṅ chos thos par mi ’gyur ba ni chos kyi sgrib pa źes bya’o. ’dod chags la sogs pa ñon
moṅs pa śas che bas ’phags pa’i lam bsgrub par mi nus pa ni ñon moṅs pa’i sgrib pa’o. ’jig
tshogs daṅ mthar ’dzin par lta ba la sogs pa lta ba lṅa rnams ni lta ba’i sgrib pa źes
bya’o. sems can dmyal ba daṅ dud ’gro’i skye gnas la sogs pa ṅan soṅ gsum gyi ’gro ba dag
tu skyes nas bden pa mthoṅ bar mi ’gyur ba ni ’gro ba’i sgrib pa źes bya’o. tshe sṅa ma la
sdig pa mi dge ba’i las byas pa’i rnam par smin pas lha daṅ mir skyes kyaṅ rnam par smin
pa des bsgribs pas bden pa mi mthoṅ ba ni rnam par smin pa’i sgrib pa źes bya’o. ji tsam
du śes par bya ba la bar du gcod pa phuṅ po daṅ, khams daṅ skye mched la sogs pa la mṅon par
chags pa’i bag chags ñon moṅs pa can ma yin pa’i ma rig pa ni śes pa’i sgrib pa’o. bag
chags de dag gi mtshams sbyor bas na, bag chags daṅ mtshams sbyor ba ste, de’i dbaṅ gis gcig
nas gcig tu tshe len par byed pas so.

rtog pa daṅ rnam par rtog pa daṅ yoṅs su rtog pa źes bya ba la sogs pas mdud daṅ sgro btags
pa rnams daṅ ma ’dres pa bstan te, rtog pa daṅ rnam par rtog pa daṅ yoṅs su rtog pa gsum ni
mdud pa źes bya ste, byaṅ chub sems dpa’i ’chiṅ ba ni rnam par rtog pa sna tshogs yin pa’i
phyir ro. mtshan ma daṅ dmigs pa la sogs te, lhag ma rnams ni sgro btags pa źes bya ste,
mtshan ma la sogs pa’i rnam par chos rnams bskyed pa’i phyir ro.de la mig daṅ rna ba la
