sogs pa naṅ gi dṅos po rnams la yod pa’am med par ’dzin pa ni rtog pa’o, gzugs daṅ sgra la
sogs pa phyi’i yul rnams la yod pa daṅ med par ’dzin pa ni rnam par rtog pa’o, phyi daṅ naṅ
gi dṅos po gñi ga la yod pa daṅ med par ’dzin pa ni yoṅs su rtog pa’o. yaṅ na, ñan thos
kyi theg pa la mṅon par chags śiṅ rtog pa ni rtog pa źes bya’o, raṅ saṅs rgyas kyi theg pa
la mṅon par chags pa ni rnam par rtog pa’o, theg pa bla na med pa la mṅon par chags pa ni
yoṅs su rtog pa’o. yaṅ na, rtog ge ba rnams ni dṅos po la tshad ma rnam pa gsum gyis ’jal
te, mṅon sum daṅ, rjes su dpag daṅ, luṅ gi tshad ma’o; de la mṅon sum gyi tshad mas dṅos
po la ’jal ba ni rtog pa’o, rjes su dpag pa’i tshad mas dṅos po ’jal ba ni rnam par rtog
pa’o, luṅ gi tshad mas dṅos po ’jal ba ni yoṅs su rtog pa’o.sṅon po daṅ ser po daṅ mya ṅan
las ’das pa daṅ ’khor ba źes bya ba dag ni mtshan ma’o, gzugs daṅ sgra daṅ dri daṅ ro la
sogs pa yul rnams ni dmigs pa’o, mthoṅ ba ni mig gis so, thos pa ni rna bas so, bye brag phyed
pa ni yid kyis so, rnam par rig pa ni rnam par śes pa lhag ma rnams kyis so. yaṅ na,
mthoṅ ba la sogs pas ni sṅar bśad pa bźin no.mdud daṅ sgro btags pa thams cad kyi bar daṅ
lhan cig mi gnas źes bya ba ni mdud daṅ sgro btags pa goṅ ma rnams daṅ lhan cig mi gnas par
yaṅ ma zad kyi, gźan yaṅ byaṅ chub sems dpa’i ’chiṅ bar ’gyur ba daṅ dṅos po la sgro ’dogs
pa gźan dag daṅ yaṅ lhan cig mi gnas par ston to.The commentary is unfortunately not very
enlightening from an epistemological point of view.

No. 12 is omitted by T1 p. 196c4, the number of items then mentioned rightly becoming 16, not
17, which is one too many according to the text. ṭ. has only a very short commentary, a
fact which also indicates the late insertion of this item: bdag daṅ rtag ces bya ba la sogs
pas ni phyin ci ma log daṅ ma ’dres par bstan to.

sems can gyi sems kyi spyod pa brgyad khri bźi stoṅ daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa źes bya ba la sogs
pa mi mthun pa’i phyogs daṅ gñen po daṅ ma ’dres pa bstan te; sems can gyi sems kyi spyod
pa brgyad khri bźi stoṅ ni mi mthun pa’i phyogs so, chos kyi phuṅ po brgyad khri bźi stoṅ
ni gñen po’i phyogs te, lhag ma rnams la yaṅ de bźin du sbyar ro. de la sems can ’dod chags
la spyod pa ñi khri chig stoṅ daṅ, źe sdaṅ la spyod pa ñi khri chig stoṅ daṅ, gti mug
la spyod pa ñi khri chig stoṅ daṅ, cha mñam pa la spyod pa ñi khri chig stoṅ ste, de ltar
brgyad khri bźi stoṅ ṅo. de la ’dod chags kyi gñen po chos kyi phuṅ po ñi khri chig stoṅ,
źe sdaṅ gi gñen po chos kyi phuṅ po ñi khri chig stoṅ, gti mug gi gñen po chos kyi phuṅ po
ñi khri chig stoṅ, cha mñam pa’i gñen po chos kyi phuṅ po ñi khri chig stoṅ ste, de ltar
na chos kyi phuṅ po brgyad khri bźi stoṅ ṅo.

de la ñe bar blaṅs pa’i dṅos po gter daṅ ’bru la sogs pa mi gtoṅ ba ni ser sna’o, de las bzlog
na gtoṅ ba’o; srog gcod pa daṅ, ma byin par len pa daṅ, ’dod pas log par g-yem pa la sogs
pa mi dge ba’i las la źugs pa ni ’chal pa’i tshul khrims can yin la, srog gcod pa la sogs
pa las phyir log pa ni tshul khrims so; sems can rnams la rdeg pa daṅ ’chiṅ ba la sogs
pas ’tshe bar sems pa ni gnod sems so, rdeg pa daṅ ’chiṅ ba la sogs pas sems can la mi ’tshe
źiṅ gnod par byas kyaṅ slar gnod par mi byed pa ni bzod pa’o; dge ba’i phyogs la sems mi
spro źiṅ mi ’jug pa ni le lo ste, de las bzlog na brtson ’grus so, phyi’i yul rnams la sems
’phros pa ni rnam par g-yeṅ ba’o, dmigs pa’i dṅos po la sems rtse gcig pa ni bsam gtan
no, chos kyi mtshan ñid la phyin ci log tu chags śiṅ ’dzin pa ni ’chal pa’i śes rab bo, chos
kyi mtshan ñid la phyin ci ma log par ’byed par byed ni śes rab bo.

ṅes pa daṅ ma ṅes pa źes bya ba la sogs pa rigs rnam pa lṅa ste: ñan thos kyi rigs can daṅ,
raṅ saṅs rgyas kyi rigs can daṅ, theg pa chen po’i rigs can daṅ, rigs ma ṅes pa daṅ, rigs
med pa’o. de la rigs med pa’i gaṅ zag rnams ni ṅes pa ste, de dag tu thams cad du ’khor bar
gnas par gdon mi za ba’i phyir ro. theg pa gsum du ṅes pa’i rigs can ni ma ṅes pa ste, dge
ba’i bśes gñen gyi rkyen gyis mya ṅan las ’das par yaṅ ’gyur bas na, khams gsum du gnas
par ṅes pa med pa’i phyir ro. yaṅ na rigs can rnam pa gsum ni ṅes pa ste, raṅ raṅ gi theg
pa la brten nas ’bras bu thob par gdon mi za ba’i phyir ro. ma ṅes pa’i rigs can ni ma ṅes
pa ste, dge ba’i bśes gñen gyi rkyen gyis theg pa gar btsud par ’jug ciṅ, dge ba’i bśes
gñen daṅ ma phrad na mya ṅan las ’das par ’gyur bar chad pa med pa’i phyir ro.yaṅ dag pa’i
lta ba la źugs pa’i gaṅ zag rnams ni yaṅ dag pa źes bya ste, las daṅ las kyi ’bras bu daṅ,
dkon mchog daṅ bden pa la sogs pa yod par lta bas so. log par lta ba la źen pa’i gaṅ zag
ni log pa źes bya ste, las daṅ las kyi ’bras bu daṅ, bden pa daṅ dkon mchog la sogs pa med
par ’dod pa’i phyir ro. yaṅ na, bcom ldan ’das kyis tshogs rnam pa gsum gsuṅs te, yaṅ dag
pa ñid du ṅes pa’i tshogs daṅ, log pa ñid du ṅes pa’i tshogs daṅ, ma ṅes pa’i tshogs so.
de la yaṅ dag pa ñid du ṅes pa’i tshogs ni gaṅ ’phags pa rnams te, ’dod chags ma lus par
spaṅs pa daṅ, źe sdaṅ ma lus par spaṅs pa daṅ, gti mug ma lus par spaṅs pa ste, de dag ni
ñon moṅs pa zad par ṅes pas na, yaṅ dag par ṅes pa źes bya’o; de la log par ṅes pa ni mtshams
med pa byed pa’i gaṅ zag rnams te, de dag ni ṅan soṅ gsum du skye bar ṅes pa’i phyir log
par ṅes pa źes bya’o; ṅes pa las gźan pa rnams ni ma ṅes pa źes bya ste, rkyen la ltos
nas gal te na ñon moṅs pa spoṅ bar byed la, gal te mtshams med pa’i las kyaṅ byed pa’i phyir
ro.chos de dag ñid ’bras bu yid du ’oṅ ba daṅ yid du mi ’oṅ ba skyed pa’i bye brag gis
rnam pa gñis su gźag ste, dge ba daṅ mi dge ba’o. de la ’bras bu yid du ’oṅ ba ni lha daṅ
mi la sogs pa bde ’gro rnams so; de skyed pa ni dge ba źes bya ste, srog mi gcod pa daṅ, ma
byin par mi len pa la sogs pa dge ba bcu’i las kyi lam rnams so. ’bras bu yid du mi ’oṅ
ba ni sems can dmyal ba daṅ dud ’gro la sogs pa’o; de skyed par byed pa ni mi dge ba źes bya
ste, srog gcod pa la sogs pa mi dge ba bcu’i las kyi lam rnams so.chos de kyaṅ dag gleṅ
du mi ruṅ ba daṅ gleṅ du ruṅ ba’i sgo nas gñis su gźag ste, kha na ma tho ba daṅ bcas pa
daṅ kha na ma tho ba med pa’o. de la dam pa rnams kyi gleṅ źiṅ bsñad du mi ruṅ ba ni kha na
ma tho ba daṅ bcas pa źes bya ste, srog gcod pa la sogs pa mi dge ba’i las ñid do; dam pa
rnams kyi naṅ du gleṅ źiṅ bsñad du ruṅ ba ni kha na ma tho ba med pa ste, srog gcod pa las
phyir log pa la sogs pa dge ba bcu’i las kyi lam daṅ, dad pa daṅ, tshul khrims la sogs
pa’o.chos de dag kyaṅ khams gsum du ’byuṅ bar byed pa daṅ mi byed pa’i bye brag gis rnam pa
gñis su gźag ste, zag pa daṅ bcas pa daṅ zag pa med pa’o. de la khams gsum du ’byuṅ bar
byed pa’i chos rnams ni zag pa daṅ bcas pa źes bya ste, khams gsum du skye ba’i rgyu byed
pa’o; de la zag pa ni ’dod chags la sogs pa’i ñon moṅs pa la bya ste, de daṅ bcas pas zag
pa daṅ bcas pa’o. khams gsum du ’byuṅ bar mi byed pa’i chos de dag ni zag pa med pa ste, ’phags
pa’i lam la sogs pa’o.chos de dag ñid rgyu rkyen gyis bskyed pa daṅ ma bskyed pa’i bye
brag gis rnam pa gñis su gźag ste, ’dus byas daṅ ’dus ma byas so. de la gaṅ rgyu daṅ rkyen
gyis bskyed pa rnams ni ’dus byas źes bya’o; gaṅ rgyu daṅ rkyen gyis ma bskyed pa ni ’dus
ma byas źes bya ste, de bźin ñid daṅ mya ṅan las ’das pa la sogs pa’o.chos de dag ñid
’jig rten gyis ’dris par byas pa daṅ ma byas pa’i bye brag gis rnam pa gñis su gźag ste, ’jig
rten pa daṅ ’jig rten las ’das pa’o. de la ’jig rten pa rnams kyis ’dris par byas pa ni
’jig rten pa ste, ñe bar len pa’i phuṅ po lṅa la sogs pa ’khor bar gtogs pa’i chos thams
cad do. ’jig rten pa rnams kyis ’dris par ma byas pa ni ’jig rten las ’das pa źes bya ste,
gaṅ zag daṅ chos la bdag med pa’i de bźin ñid rnam par dag pa daṅ, rnam par mi rtog pa’i
ye śes daṅ, dag pa’i ’jig rten pa’i ye śes la sogs pa’o.chos de dag ñid dam pa daṅ dam pa
ma yin pa’i sgo nas rnam pa gñis su gźag ste, bzaṅ po daṅ ṅan pa’o. de la gaṅ dam pa rnams
ni bzaṅ po źes bya ste, ñon moṅs pa’i phyogs su gyur pa spaṅs pas na ’jig rten las ’das
pa’i chos rnams la bya’o. de la chos gaṅ dam pa ma yin pa rnams ni ṅan pa źes bya ste, ’jig
rten par gtogs pa’i chos rnams so.chos de dag ñid nag po’i phyogs daṅ dkar po’i phyogs kyi
bye brag gis rnam pa gñis su gźag ste, kun nas ñon moṅs pa daṅ rnam par byaṅ ba’o. de la
nag po’i phyogs ni kun nas ñon moṅs pa źes bya ste, ’dod chags la sogs pa’o; dkar po’i phyogs
ni rnam par byaṅ ba ste, byaṅ chub kyi phyogs daṅ sa daṅ pha rol tu phyin pa la sogs
pa’o.chos de dag ñid sdug bsṅal gyi gźi daṅ bde ba’i gźi’i bye brag gis rnam pa gñis su gźag
ste, ’khor ba daṅ mya ṅan las ’das pa’o. de la chos gaṅ sdug bsṅal gyi gźir gyur pa rnams
ni ’khor ba źes bya ste, ’di ltar ’khor ba źes bya ba ni sdug bsṅal gsum daṅ brgyad la
sogs pa sdug bsṅal dpag tu med pa’i rten du gyur pa’i phyir ro. bde ba’i gźir gyur pa ni
mya ṅan las ’das pa ste, mya ṅan las ’das pa ni ’jig rten daṅ ’jig rten las ’das pa’i bde
ba thams cad daṅ ldan pa’i phyir ro.

theg pa tha dad pa daṅ, sems can tha dad pa daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pas tha dad pa thams cad
daṅ ma ’dres pa bstan te, de la ñan thos kyi theg pa źe’am, raṅ saṅs rgyas kyi theg pa źe’am,
theg pa chen po źes bya ba la sogs pa ni theg pa tha dad pa’o; lha źe’am, mi źe’am, bud
med ces bya ba la sogs pa ni sems can tha dad pa’o; dga’ ba can gyi saṅs rgyas kyi źiṅ źe’am,
padmo can gyi saṅs rgyas kyi źiṅ źes bya ba la sogs pa ni źiṅ tha dad pa’o; ’od dpag
med ce’am, mi ’khrugs pa źe’am, śākya thub pa źes bya ba la sogs pa ni saṅs rgyas tha dad
pa’o; sa bcu źe’am, sdoṅ po brgyan pa źe’am, laṅ kar gśegs pa źes bya ba ni chos tha dad
pa’o; ’di ni ñan thos kyi dge ’dun, ’di ni raṅ saṅs rgyas kyi dge ’dun, ’di ni byaṅ chub sems
dpa’i dge ’dun źe’am, ’di ni sems daṅ po bskyed pa’i byaṅ chub sems dpa’, ’di ni mos pas
spyod pa’i byaṅ chub sems dpa’, ’di ni mthoṅ ba’i lam la źugs pa’i byaṅ chub sems dpa’
źes bya ba la sogs pa ni dge ’dun tha dad pa’o.

mi śes pa daṅ śes pa daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pas mtshan ma yid la byed pa rnams daṅ ma ’dres
pa bstan te; de la mi śes pa ni ma rig pa ste, rtag pa daṅ, gtsaṅ ba daṅ, bdag daṅ, bde bar
’dzin pa’o; śes pa ni rig pa ste, mi rtag pa daṅ, bdag med pa daṅ, mi gtsaṅ ba daṅ, sdug
bsṅal bar ’dzin pa’o; rnam pa sna tshogs su śes pa ni rnam par śes pa ste, gzugs su śes pa
daṅ, sgrar śes pa nas chos su śes pa’i bar du yin pas mig la sogs pa’i rnam par śes pa rnams
so; brjod du yod ciṅ bsam du yod pa rnams ni kun rdzob bo; de las bzlog pa ni don dam
pa ste, brjod pa daṅ bsam pas thog tu mi phebs pa’o; mtshan ma yid la byed pa thams cad kyi
bar daṅ lhan cig mi gnas źes bya ba ni mtshan ma yid la byed pa goṅ du bśad pa de rnams
daṅ lhan cig mi gnas par ma zad kyi, gźan yaṅ yod pa daṅ med pa źes bya ba daṅ, rtag pa daṅ
mi rtag pa la sogs pa’i mtshan ma rnams yid la byed pa daṅ yaṅ lhan cig mi gnas so źes
bya ba’i don to.

śes rab ni rgyu ba med pa, lus med pa źes bya ba la sogs pas goṅ du smos pa lta bu’i tshul gyis
mtshan ma thams cad spaṅs pa’i raṅ bźin cis kyaṅ ma gos par rnam par mi rtog pa’i raṅ
bźin ñid bstan te, goṅ du smos pa’i śes rab ni źes bya ba’i tha tshig go. gaṅ rgyu ba med
pa’i źes bya ba la gzuṅ ba daṅ ’dzin pa’i mtshan mar ’du śes pa ni rgyu ba’o; śes rab des
gzuṅ ba daṅ ’dzin par ’du śes thams cad spaṅs pas gzuṅ ba daṅ ’dzin pa’i mtshan mar ’du śes
pa’i rgyu med pas na rgyu ba med pa źes bya’o; chos gźan gyi gźi daṅ rten kyaṅ ma yin la,
gźan la yaṅ mi rten pas na lus med pa’o; kun rdzob tu śes rab kyi mtshan ñid chos rab tu
rnam par ’byed pa lta bu yaṅ ma yin źiṅ, de lta bur yaṅ mi gnas pas na mtshan ñid med pa’o;
śes rab kyi yul rnam pa brgyad po ’og nas bśad la sogs pa gaṅ la yaṅ mtshan mar mi ’dzin
pas na mtshan ma med pa’o.śes rab kyi raṅ bźin rgyas par bśad nas bsdus te bstan pa’i phyir
de ni mtshan ma daṅ yid la byed pa thams cad daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pa smos te, mtshan
ma thams cad spaṅs pa rnam par mi rtog pa’i raṅ bźin gyi śes rab de ni źes bya ba’i don to,
lhan cig mi gnas pa’i sgra thams cad daṅ yaṅ sbyar te, mtshan ma yid la byed pa thams cad
daṅ lhan cig mi gnas, sems daṅ lhan cig mi gnas, yid daṅ lhan cig mi gnas źes bya ba’i
don to; de la zag pa daṅ bcas pa daṅ zag pa med pa’i mtshan ñid du yid la byed pa thams cad
daṅ ma ’dres pas na mtshan ma yid la byed pa thams cad daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa źes bya’o.dge
ba daṅ mi dge ba’i bag chags rnam pa sna tshogs bsags pa rnam par smin pa’i ’bras bu
len par byed pa’i kun gźi rnam par śes pa daṅ ma ’dres pas na sems daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa
źes bya’o; ṅa daṅ ṅa’i źes rlom sems pa bdag rgyal ba daṅ bdag la chags pa la sogs pa ñon
moṅs pa bźi daṅ lhan cig pa’i ñon moṅs pa’i yid daṅ ma ’bags pas na yid daṅ lhan cig mi gnas
pa źes bya’o; gzugs la sogs pa’i yul rnams la dmigs par byed pa, kun gźi rnam par śes
pa la brten pa’i mig la sogs pa ’jug pa’i rnam par śes pa daṅ ma ’dres pas na rnam par śes
pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa źes bya’o. citta (1), manas (2) and vijñāna (3) are thus defined
according to Yogācāra doctrine as ālayavijñāna (1); kliṣṭamanas, the mind full of vices,
of conceit concerned with me and mine (ahaṃ mameti mānaḥ) (2); and the six vijñāna resulting
from sense-perception (3).gnas ni mig gi rnam par śes pa’i rten mig gi dbaṅ po nas yid
kyi rnam par śes pa’i rten yid kyi dbaṅ po’i bar du dbaṅ po rnams so. dbaṅ po de rnams la
mi brten pas na gnas daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa’o.miṅ ni gzugs daṅ sgra daṅ dri daṅ ro źes
bya ba daṅ, mig daṅ rna ba źes bya ba daṅ, ’khor ba daṅ mya ṅan las ’das pa źes bya ba daṅ,
lha sbyin daṅ mchod sbyin la sogs pa tha sñad du btags pa ste, de dag daṅ ma ’bags pas na
miṅ daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa’o. gzugs daṅ sgra la sogs pa dmigs pa’i yul rnams ni mtshan
ma źes bya ste, de dag daṅ ma ’dres pas na mtshan ma daṅ lhan cig mi gnas pa’o.chos can daṅ
chos ñid daṅ, kun rdzob daṅ don dam pa daṅ, zag pa daṅ bcas pa daṅ zag pa med pa daṅ, ’dus
byas daṅ ’dus ma byas rnams, de bźin ñid daṅ gźan par ’dod pa ni gcig pa daṅ tha dad pa
ste, de lta bu’i spros pa daṅ ma ’dres pas na gcig pa daṅ tha dad pa daṅ lhan cig mi gnas
pa źes bya’o – "Characterized by moments of existence (dharmin) and the real nature of things
(dharmatā), concealed truth (saṃvṛtisatya) and the highest truth (paramārtha), sullied
(sāsrava) and unsullied (anāsrava), conditioned (saṃskṛta) and unconditioned (asaṃskṛta),
things thus as they really are (tathatā) and wishing them to be otherwise (anyakāmatā) is
oneness and plurality. Since (insight) is not polluted by such discursive thinking (prapañca)
it is said ’it does not stay with oneness or plurality’."

de ltar śes rab kyi raṅ bźin bśad nas, de’i yul bstan pa’i phyir de la śes rab kyi yul gaṅ źe
na źes bya ba la sogs pa smos so.de la źes bya ba’i don ni gźan las dgar ba’am mgo draṅ
bar lta’o. śes rab kyi yul gaṅ źe na źes bya ba ni dris pa ste, śes rab kyis dmigs par bya
ba’am, śes rab kyis khoṅ du chud par bya ba’i dṅos po gaṅ źe na źes bya ba’i don to.

dris pa la lan gdab pa’i phyir ’di lta ste: chos brgyad la mkhas pa’o źes bya ba smos te, ’di
lta ste źes bya ba ni tshig mgo draṅ ba daṅ tshig gi rgyan du bya ba’o; chos brgyad khoṅ
du chud ciṅ rtogs pa ni chos brgyad la mkhas pa ste, de bas na chos brgyad ni śes rab kyi
yul lo, de’aṅ bstan pa daṅ bśad pa lta bur rig par bya’o. de la bstan pa las brtsams na chos
brgyad la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na? ’di lta ste: phuṅ po la mkhas pa daṅ, khams la mkhas pa
daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pa smos so, bśad pa las brtsams nas gsuṅs pa de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’i
phuṅ po la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na źes bya ba la sogs pa’o. yaṅ na graṅs daṅ, miṅ daṅ, dpe
daṅ, rab tu dbye ba bstan pa’i phyir de la śes rab kyi yul gaṅ źe na źes bya ba la sogs pa
smos so, ’di lta ste: chos brgyad la mkhas pa’o źes bya bas ni graṅs bstan te, chos brgyad
la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na? ’di lta ste: phuṅ po la mkhas pa źes bya ba la sogs pas miṅ bstan
to.Cf. Bbh. p. 3311-13: prajñāyāṃ yogaṃ karoti skandhakauśalyaṃ vā karoti dhātukauśalyam
āyatanakauśalyaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalyam ...; Śbh p. 194,2-4 et seq., e. g. p. 2481 and
note 1; Pratyekabuddhabhūmi p. 3317-19, 24-26, 341-2.

de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’i phuṅ po la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na? ’di phuṅ po rnams kyi dper bya ba
bstan pa ste, dbu ba rdos pa bstan pa daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pas dpe bstan to; de ci’i phyir
źe na? gzugs ni dbu ba rdos pa lta bu ste źes bya ba la sogs pas ni rab tu dbye ba bstan
to. de la źes bya ba ni dgar ba’i tshig ste, mkhas pa rnam pa brgyad pos bkar te, phuṅ po
la mkhas pa de bstan par ’dod pa’o. de la phuṅ po’i don ni gaṅ cuṅ zad gzugs ’das pa daṅ,
ma ’oṅs pa daṅ, da ltar gyi daṅ, naṅ gi daṅ, phyi’i daṅ, rags pa daṅ, phra ba daṅ, ṅan pa
daṅ, bzaṅ po daṅ, ñe ba daṅ, riṅ ba de dag thams cad gcig tu bsdus nas bstan pa ni phuṅ
po źes bya’o, phuṅ po de la mkhas pa ni phuṅ po la mkhas pa ste, phuṅ po’i mtshan ñid daṅ
raṅ bźin gaṅ yin pa rtogs pa’o. ji ltar phuṅ po’i mtshan ñid rtogs par ’gyur źe na? de bstan
pa’i phyir gsuṅs pa gaṅ phuṅ po rnams kyi dper bya ba bstan pa ste, dbu ba rdos pa bstan
pa daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pa’o. ’di źes bya ni dpe rnams la sñegs so. phuṅ po’i raṅ bźin
gaṅ yin pa de daṅ mthun pa’i dper gźag pa ni phuṅ po rnams kyi dper bya ba bstan pa źes bya
ste, dpe yaṅ dbu ba rdos pa bstan pa la sogs pa rnam pa bcu’o. dpe rnam pa bcu po de rnams
kyaṅ don rnam pa bcu’i dbaṅ du byas nas gsuṅs par rig par bya ste, 1) bdag rtag pa med
pa’i don daṅ, 2) bdag med ciṅ gtsaṅ ba’i don spaṅs pa’i don daṅ, 3) bdag med ciṅ mnog chuṅ
ba’i don daṅ, 4) sñiṅ po med pa’i don daṅ, 5) mi brtan pa’i don daṅ, 6) don med pa dag kyaṅ
spyod yul du gyur źiṅ yid du ’oṅ ba daṅ yid du mi ’oṅ ba’i kun tu loṅs spyod pa med pa’i
don daṅ, 7) dṅos po med kyaṅ tha sñad daṅ smra ba sna tshogs byed pa’i don daṅ, 8) don
med kyaṅ rnam par śes pa sna tshogs su ’jug pa’i don daṅ, 9) don med par yaṅ dag pa ’dzin
pa rnams kyi tiṅ ṅe ’dzin gyi spyod yul du gyur pa’i don daṅ, 10) don med kyaṅ byaṅ chub sems
dpa’ rnams bsam pa phyin ci ma log pas sems can thams cad kyi bya ba bsgrub pa’i phyir
skye ba len pa’i don to. The ten similes are treated in Mppś pp. 357-87, where also much
comparative material is given by Lamotte.

dper gźag pa de dag gi don bstan pa’i phyir de ci’i phyir źe na źes bya ba la sogs pa smos so,
de ci’i phyir źe na źes bya ba ni dpe bcu po de dag ji ltar na phuṅ po’i dper ’gyur źe’am,
phuṅ po rnams ci’i phyir dpe de daṅ ’dra bar bstan ces bya ba’i don to.

phuṅ po rnams dpe daṅ mtshan ñid ’dra bar bstan pa’i phyir gzugs ni dbu ba rdos pa lta bu ste
źes bya ba la sogs pa smos so. ’dir phuṅ po’i sgra ma smos su zin kyaṅ phuṅ po ñid bśad
pa gleṅ ba’i skabs yin pas gzugs kyaṅ phuṅ po źes bya bar draṅs te, gzugs la sogs pa’i yul
lṅa daṅ, mig la sogs pa’i dbaṅ po lṅa la sogs pa ni gzugs kyi phuṅ po źes bya’o. gzugs kyi
phuṅ po de ni dbu ba rdos pa daṅ ’dra ste, ci’i phyir źe na? bdag rtag pa med pa’i phyir
ro, don de ñid bstan pa’i phyir dbu ba rdos pa ni bdag ma yin, sems can ma yin źes bya ba
la sogs pa smos te, ’di lta ste, skyes bu la la źig gis chu bo chen po la śel lta bu kha
dog daṅ dbyibs su ldan pa’i dbu ba rdos pa maṅ po rgyu ba maṅ po mthoṅ ba daṅ, de dag la sñiṅ
po daṅ raṅ bźin yod du re nas lag pa gñis kyis ’dzin ciṅ, blaṅ bar brgal na med par gyur
pa daṅ: kye ma ’di go dbu ba rdos pa ste, gsog gsob ṅo bo ñid med do, sñam mo – "... In
this way: In the great sea some people see the foam tossed about with form and colour like
crystals (yathāsphaṭikavarṇasaṃsthāna). Thinking that it has substance (sāra) and essence
(svabhāva) they grasp for it with the hands, but it flies away and comes to nought: ‘Oh,
this is only foam, it is worthless (tucchaka), vain (riktaka) without essence (niḥsvabhāva),’
they say."de bas na dbu ba rdos pa ni bdag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pas na gaṅ zag gi bar gyi
raṅ bźin ma yin par śes so, dbu ba rdos pa’i raṅ bźin gaṅ yin pa, gzugs kyi raṅ bźin yaṅ
de yin te źes bya ba ni dbu ba rdos pa’i raṅ bźin bdag med ciṅ dṅos po med pa gsog daṅ gsob
tu gyur pa gaṅ yin pa gzugs kyi phuṅ po’i raṅ bźin yaṅ de yin te, gzugs kyi phuṅ po la
ye śes kyi mig daṅ ldan pas bltas śiṅ brtags te, źib mor gźigs na bdag daṅ raṅ bźin med ciṅ
gsog gsob stoṅ pa’i mtshan ñid du gnas pa’i phyir ro.

tshor ba ni chu’i chu bur lta bu źes bya ba la bde ba daṅ, sdug bsṅal daṅ, bde ba yaṅ ma yin
sdug bsṅal ba yaṅ ma yin par rnam pa gsum myoṅ ba ni tshor ba ste, ’dir yaṅ phuṅ po źes bya
bar sbyar ro; tshor ba’i phuṅ po ni chu’i chu bur daṅ ’dra ste. de ci’i phyir źe na? bdag
med ciṅ gtsaṅ ba spaṅs pa’i phyir ro.’di ltar sems can la la źig gis chu’i naṅ du char
bab ste, chu’i chu bur śel gyi nor bu daṅ ’dra bar rnam pa sna tshogs su ’byuṅ ba mthoṅ ba
daṅ, de dag rdzas su ruṅ źiṅ rgyan du ruṅ de re nas lag pa gñis kyis ’dzin ciṅ blaṅ bar bśams
na med par gyur ciṅ, ma bzuṅ ba’i rnams kyaṅ skyes ma thag tu ’gag ste. rdzas su ruṅ
bar ma mthoṅ nas: kye ma ’di go chu’i chu bur te, bdag med pa raṅ bźin med par gsog gsob yin
par śes so. de bźin du bde ba daṅ sdug bsṅal la sogs pa’i tshor ba’i phuṅ po la ye śes
kyi mig daṅ lag pas bltas śiṅ yod pa daṅ med pa la sogs pa rnam par dpyod na chu’i chu bur
daṅ ’dra bar bdag daṅ raṅ bźin med ciṅ gsog daṅ gsob yin pa daṅ, thams cad kyaṅ sdug bsṅal
gyi mtshan ñid ’gyur ba daṅ skyes ma thag tu ’jig pa’i raṅ bźin yin par mthoṅ ṅo – "When
rain falls into the water, some people see the bubbles as if different kinds of crystal-gems
(sphaṭikamaṇi) were originating. Thinking they are substances (dravya) and fit for ornaments
they grasp for them with their hands to arrange them, they come to nought, even the
ones which are not grasped for burst as soon as they originate. Seeing that they are not
substances they learn: ‘Oh, these are bubbles, without self (anātma), without essence (niḥsvabhāva),
worthless and vain.’ Thus also the part of personality of feeling, pleasant and
unpleasant, etc., is without self and without essence, worthless and vain just like bubbles;
grasped with the eyes and hands of wisdom, examined if existent or non-existent, one sees
that they are all characterized by suffering (duḥkhalakṣaṇa), having the essence of perishing
as soon as they originate."’du śes ni smig rgyu lta bu’o źes bya ba la yul na mtshan
mar ’dzin pa ni ’du śes te, yul ni gzugs daṅ sgra la sogs pa’o; mtshan ma ni dkar po daṅ
dmar po la sogs pa’o; ’dzin pa ni de ni dkar po ñid yin gyi dmar po ma yin no, źes gcod
pa ste. ’du śes kyi phuṅ po ni smig rgyu daṅ ’dra ste, ci’i phyir źe na? bdag med ciṅ mnog
chuṅ ba’i phyir ro. ’di lta ste: chu ’dod pa’i skyes bu la la źig dpyid kyi dus na ñi ma’i
’od kyis gduṅs te, smig rgyu ba sna tshogs chu rlabs lta bu mig gis mthoṅ ba daṅ: de dag
la chu yin, sñam nas btuṅ bar bya ba’i phyir druṅ du brgyags te btags na chu ma yin par mthoṅ
nas: kye ma’o, ’di go smyig rgyu ba ste, bdag med pa gsog gsob ṅo bo ñid med pa źes sems
pa, de bźin du log pa sna tshogs kyi rnam par rtog pa maṅ po’i ’du śes kyi phuṅ po la
ye śes kyi mig gis bltas te – "... Perception is grasping the distinguishing marks of objects
(viṣaye nimittodgrahaṇaṃ saṃjñā), objects are form, sound, etc., distinguishing marks
(nimitta) are white and red and so on, grasping is deciding: ‘This is white, not red’. The
part of personality perception is like a mirage – why? It is without self and trifling. Thirsty
people tormented by the sunlight in summertime see mirages as billows of water with
their eyes, and thinking it is water they run to drink. Having discovered it is not, they
think: ‘Oh, this is a mirage, without self, worthless and vain, without essence.’ Thus, with
the eyes of wisdom (jñānacakṣur) they also see perception, full of thought-constructions
(vikalpa) concerned with misunderstandings."yod pa daṅ med pa la sogs par yaṅ dag par brtags
na bdag med pa daṅ dṅos po med par mthoṅ ste, de bas na ’du śes kyaṅ smig rgyu ba bźin
du bdag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pas na gaṅ zag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pa’i bar du’o.’du byed rnams
ni chu śiṅ lta bu’o źes bya ba la las dge ba daṅ mi dge ba daṅ luṅ du ma bstan pa rnams
sna tshogs byed pa ni ’du byed de, de yaṅ ’du byed kyi tshogs rnam pa maṅ po rnams so. ’du
byed kyi phuṅ po rnams ni chu śiṅ daṅ ’dra ste, ci’i phyir źe na? sñiṅ po med pa’i phyir
ro. ’di lta ste: śiṅ gi sñiṅ po sra ba ’dod pa’i skyes bu la la źig gis chu śiṅ bcad de ’dab
ma nas mthar gyis rnam par bśus nas de la mig gis bltas te sñiṅ po yod dam źes brtags
na, sñiṅ po yod par ma mthoṅ nas: kye ma’o, ’di go chu śiṅ gi sñiṅ po ste, stoṅ pa dṅos po
daṅ raṅ bźin med pa’o, źes sems pa, de bźin du dge ba daṅ mi dge ba daṅ luṅ du mi bstan pa
la sogs pa ’du byed kyi phuṅ po rnam pa sna tshogs pa la dam pa daṅ sñiṅ po yod du re ste,
śes rab kyi mig gis kun tu bltas nas yod pa daṅ med pa daṅ, gcig daṅ du ma daṅ, bdag daṅ
pha rol daṅ gñis ka’i sbyor bas yaṅ dag par brtags na sems tsam daṅ ma skyes pa daṅ yod
pa daṅ med pa las ’das pa sñiṅ po med pa chu śiṅ bźin du bdag gi raṅ bźin daṅ bral ba mthoṅ
ṅo – "... Formative factors create the different kinds of good, bad and neutral, the multitudes
of formative factors are many. The part of personality of formative factors is like
the plantain tree. Why? It is without a core (asāra). People who want a hard (dṛḍhasāra)
tree and cut down a plantain tree, stripping the bark off it from top to bottom, see that
there is no core (sāra) when examining it in this respect: ‘Oh, this has the core of a plantain
tree (kadalīsāra), empty, no substance, no essence.’ Thus also the part of personality
of different formative factors, concerned with good, bad, neutral, etc.: reflecting on
the existence of a principle or a core (sāra), one sees, having viewed it with the eyes of
insight (prajñācakṣur), that it is only thought (cittamātra), unborn (anutpanna), beyond
being and non-being (bhavābhavasamatikrānta), without a core (asāra) just like the plantain
tree, and without the essence of a self (ātmasvabhāvarahita), having thus reflected with
effort concerned with the duality of existence and non-existence, one and many, self and
others."rnam par śes pa ni sgyu ma lta bu źes bya ba la gzugs la sogs pa’i yul rnams śes
pa ni rnam par śes pa ste, de’aṅ mig la sogs pa’i rnam par śes pa brgyad do. rnam par śes
pa’i phuṅ po ni sgyu ma daṅ ’dra ste; ci’i phyir źe na? mi brtan pa’i phyir ro. ’di lta ste:
skyes bu sgrin po źig gis sgyu ma’i cha lugs kyi bzo bos lha daṅ, mi daṅ gnod sbyin daṅ,
dud ’gro’i gzugs sna tshogs kyi sgyu ma rnams sprul pa de dag la mig gis kyaṅ kun du lta
źiṅ, raṅ bźin daṅ rgyun du gnas par re nas brtags na, raṅ bźin med ciṅ de ma thag tu ’jig
pa yin par mthoṅ nas: kye ma, ’di go sgyu ma ste, stoṅ pa raṅ bźin med pa’o, źes sems pa,
de bźin du las kyi bag chags sna tshogs kyis bsgyur ba’i rnam par śes pa’i phuṅ po la śes
rab kyi mig gis raṅ bźin daṅ rgyun du gnas par re nas, gcig daṅ du ma’i ṅo bos brtags na,
sgyu ma bźin du stoṅ pa ṅo bo ñid med pa skad cig ma re re la ’jig par mthoṅ ṅo – "... Knowing
the objects, form, etc., is consciousness (rūpādiviṣaye jñānaṃ vijñānam), it is the
eight consciousnesses pertaining to the eye, etc., (cakṣurādivijñānāny aṣṭavijñānāni). The
part of personality of consciousness is like a magical creation (vijñānaskandho māyopamaḥ).
Why? It is not substantial (adṛḍhatvāt). A cunning man may create various illusory forms
of gods, men, demons and animals with the art of magic of illusions. But though they are
seen with the eyes, if one examines them hoping they have own being (svabhāva) and continued
existence (prabandhasthiti), you see that they have no own being (niḥsvabhāva), they perish
at once: ‘Oh, this is only an illusion (māyā), empty (śūnya), without own being (niḥsvabhāva),’
one thinks. In the same way, if one examines with the eye of insight, with a view
to the individual and general own-being, the part of personality of consciousness (vijñānaskandha),
which is created by the different habits of action (karmavāsanā), hoping it
has own being and continued existence, one sees that it perishes each moment (kṣaṇa) like
an illusion (māyopama), empty (śūnya) and without own being (niḥsvabhāva)."phuṅ po rnams ni
rmi lam lta bu ste źes bya ba la goṅ du bśad pa’i phuṅ po de dag ñid ni yaṅ rmi lam daṅ
’dra ste, ci’i phyir źe na? don med pa dag kyaṅ spyod yul du ’gyur źiṅ yid du ’oṅ ba daṅ yid
du mi ’oṅ ba kun du loṅs spyod par byed pa’i phyir ro. ’di ltar rnam par śes pa rnams yul
la ’jug par mi nus te, gñid kyis log pas na rtog pa sna tshogs kyi rgyu ba ’byuṅ ba ni
rmi lam mo. dper na rmi lam bdag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pa nas gaṅ zag gi bar gyi raṅ bźin ma
yin te, dṅos po med kyaṅ dga’ ba daṅ mi dga’ bar ’gyur ba’i yul mthoṅ ba’i tshe dga’ ba daṅ
mi dga’ ba’i sems rnam pa sna tshogs skye bar ’gyur ro. de bźin du phuṅ po rnams kyaṅ bdag
gi raṅ bźin ma yin pas na gaṅ zag gi bar gyi raṅ bźin ma yin te, dṅos po med mod kyi las
dge ba daṅ mi dge ba rnam pa sna tshogs kyi rgyus mtho ris daṅ ṅan soṅ gi bde ba daṅ sdug
bsṅal rnams skye bar ’gyur ro – "... The parts of personality mentioned above are like a
dream (svapna). Why? Even though it is without real meaning (or objective counterpart, anartha),
it becomes a sphere of objects (viṣaya) causing all kinds of pleasant and unpleasant
experience. Consciousness (vijñāna) is not able to enter the [outer] sphere of objects
(viṣaya), dream is the appearance of activity of different kinds of thought-constructions
(vividhakalpanāpracāra) because of sleep (suptatvāt). Dream has no own being as a self (ātmasvabhāva),
as it has no own being as a person (pudgalasvabhāva), but even though it is inexistent
(abhāva), it creates different kinds of happy and unhappy thoughts (citta) when
it sees the happy or unhappy spheres (viṣaya). In the same way the parts of personality (skandha)
have no own being as a self (ātmasvabhāva), as they have no own being as a person
(pudgalasvabhāva), but even though they are inexistent (abhāva), one is born in the states
of happiness and suffering of heaven (svarga) and hell (apāya) by the causes of the different
good and bad actions (vividhakuśalākuśalakarmahetubhiḥ)."

phuṅ po rnams ni brag ca lta bu ste źes bya ba ni phuṅ po rnams ni brag ca daṅ ’dra ste, ci’i
phyir źe na? dṅos po med kyaṅ tha sñad daṅ smra ba sna tshogs byed pa’i phyir ro. dper na
sgra la brag ca’i sgra brñan bdag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pas na gaṅ zag gi bar gyi raṅ bźin
yaṅ ma yin te, dṅos po med ciṅ don med kyaṅ sgra rnam pa sna tshogs ’byuṅ ba. de bźin du chos
thams cad bdag med de, raṅ bźin gyis źi ba yin mod kyi, ’on kyaṅ sgra brñan daṅ ’dra ba’i
miṅ daṅ tshig daṅ tha sñad du brjod pa maṅ po yaṅ yod do – "... The parts of personality
are like an echo (pratiśrutkā). Why? Even though it is immaterial (avastuka) it causes
different kinds of expressions (vyavahāra) and speech. The resounding (pratiśabda) in the
echo has no own being as a self (ātmasvabhāva), as it has no own being as a person (pudgalasvabhāva),
but even though it is immaterial (avastuka) and meaningless (anartha), different
kinds of sound (śabda) appear. In the same way, though all moments of existence are without
a self (anātma) and essentially peaceful (svabhāvena śāntāḥ), they have all kinds of
names, words and expressions in utterances which are like the resounding [echo] (pratiśabda)."

phuṅ po rnams ni mig yor lta bu ste źes bya ba la śog śog gam dar ram ras la ri mo sna tshogs
bris nas brgyaṅs te, phub la de’i naṅ du mtshan mo’i me mar bus na gzugs rnam pa sna tshogs
snaṅ ba ni mig yor źes bya’o. yaṅ na snaṅ brñan źes bya ste, khaṅ pa’i naṅ gi ñi zer ’od
la brten nas gzugs gcig daṅ gñis la sogs par snaṅ ba’o. yaṅ na gźan gnas pa las gźan du
snaṅ ba ni mig yor te, dper na sdoṅ po las mi lta bur ’khrul pa’o. phuṅ po rnams ni mig yor
daṅ ’dra ste, ci’i phyir źe na? don med kyaṅ mig yor gyi dus na gzugs rnam pa sna tshogs
snaṅ ba, de bźin du don med par yaṅ khams gsum gyi sems daṅ sems las byuṅ ba rnam pa sna
tshogs skye źiṅ ’byuṅ ṅo – "... A shadow figure is the following: If one draws some figures
on a piece of cotton, silk or paper and stretches it out, and then places a lamp behind
it in the night, different kinds of forms (rūpa) appear. Or, as a reflection, dependent on
the light in a ray of sun in a house, one, two or many forms (rūpa) appear. Or, it is when
something appears as something else in another place, as when one mistakes a post for a
man. The parts of personality are like a shadow picture. Why? Though without real meaning
(or objective counterpart, anartha), different kinds of forms appear at the time the shadow-picture
[is produced], in the same way, though without real meaning (or objective counterpart,
anartha), the thoughts and mental events (cittacaitta) of the threefold world (traidhātuka)
are born."

phuṅ po rnams ni gzugs brñan lta bu ste źes bya ba la phuṅ po rnams ni gzugs brñan daṅ ’dra
ste, ci’i phyir źe na? don med kyaṅ yaṅ dag par ’dzin pa rnams kyi tiṅ ṅe ’dzin gyi spyod
yul du ’gyur ba’i phyir ro. dper na chu’i zla ba daṅ me loṅ dag pa’i naṅ du bźin gyi gzugs
brñan du snaṅ ba bdag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pa nas gaṅ zag gi bar gyi raṅ bźin ma yin te, dṅos
po med du zin yaṅ bltar snaṅ ba tsam yaṅ yod pa, de bźin du tiṅ ṅe ’dzin la sogs pa’i raṅ
bźin daṅ rnal ’byor ba’i phuṅ po rnams kyaṅ bdag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pas na gaṅ zag gi bar
gyi raṅ bźin ma yin te, dṅos po med ciṅ raṅ bźin mi dmigs mod kyi, ’on kyaṅ rgya mtsho
daṅ ’dra ba’i sems mñam par gnas pa las gzugs brñan snaṅ ba bźin rnam par thar pa daṅ, gzugs
daṅ, sprul pa la sogs pa rnam pa sna tshogs ’byuṅ źiṅ snaṅ bar yaṅ byed do – "... The parts
of personality are like a reflected image (pratibimba). Why? Even though they are without
real meaning [or objective counterpart,] they are a field of concentrations (samādhigocara)
for those who practise. As the moon reflected in the water (udakacandra) and the reflected
image of the face in a pure mirror have no own being as a self (ātmasvabhāva), they
have no own being as a person (pudgalasvbhāva), but even though they are not a real thing
(avastuka), they are still reflections to be seen; in the same way with the own being of
concentration, etc. (samādhyādisvabhāva), the parts of religious effort (yogaskandha) have
no own being as a self (ātmasvabhāva), as they have no own being as a person (pudgalasvbhāva),
but even though they are not real things (avastuka) and their own being is not apprehended
(nopalabhyate), liberation (vimokṣa), form (rūpa) and magical appearances (nirmita)
of different kinds come into being and appear like reflected images (pratibimba) from thought
(citta) ever the same (samastha) like the sea (samudra)."

phuṅ po rnams ni sprul pa lta bu ste źes bya ba la phuṅ po rnams ni sprul pa daṅ ’dra ste, ci’i
phyir źe na? don med kyaṅ byaṅ chub sems dpa’ rnams bsam pa phyin ci ma log par sems can
thams cad kyi bya ba bsgrub pa’i phyir skye ba len par snaṅ bas so. dper na lha daṅ mi
la sogs pa’i sprul pa sna tshogs bdag gi raṅ bźin ma yin pa nas gaṅ zag gi bar gyi raṅ bźin
ma yin te, dṅos po med mod kyi, ’on kyaṅ gzugs daṅ dbyibs rnam pa sna tshogs snaṅ ba, de
bźin du sems can gyi don du byaṅ chub sems dpa’ ’khor bar ’jug pa yaṅ bdag gi raṅ bźin ma
yin pa nas gaṅ zag gi bar gyi raṅ bźin ma yin te, dṅos po med mod kyi, ’on kyaṅ skye ba rnam
pa sna tshogs ’byuṅ źiṅ skye bar snaṅ ṅo – "... The parts of personality are like a magical
creation (nirmita). Why? Even though [the magical creation] is no objective entity (anartha),
the bodhisattvas appear [by means of it] seeking birth with good intentions (aviparītāśaya)
to complete what all beings have to do. Although the magical apparitions of gods
and men have no own being as selves (ātmasvabhāva), etc., and no own being as persons (pudgalasvabhāva),
and accordingly are [really] inexistent (abhāva), they appear with colour
and form. In the same way the bodhisattvas enter existence (saṃsāra) for the sake of beings,
though they have no own being as selves (ātmasvabhāva), etc., and no own being as persons
(pudgalasvabhāva), and accordingly are [really] inexistent (abhāva), but they appear
as being born in different states of existence.gaṅ ’di la mkhas pa, de ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i
phuṅ po la mkhas pa źes bya’o źes bya ba la goṅ du phuṅ po dpe bstan pa’i tshul du phuṅ
po’i mtshan ñid la mkhas pa’i byaṅ chub sems dpa’ de ni phuṅ po la mkhas pa yin no źes
bya ba’i don to.

phuṅ po źes bya ba, de ni ’jig rten te źes bya ba la phuṅ po źes bya ba ni ’jig rten la bya
ste, ’jig rten gyi mtshan ñid gaṅ kyaṅ yin źe na? de’i phyir ’jig rten kyaṅ ’jig pa’i mtshan
ñid do źes smras te, ’jig rten gyi mtshan ñid ni skad cig ma re re la ’jig pa’i mtshan
ñid do.Cf. Mvy 3061: lujyata iti lokaḥ; Kośa 518-19: lujyata iti lokaḥ (read lujyata for lakṣyata
in the text of Kośa, tib. ’jig); Kośavyākhyā 235-10, and PTSD s. v. lujjati, lujjana.
Cf. also Aṣṭa p. 53720-53814; Mppś vol. V, p. IX.don de ñid gsal bar bstan pa’i phyir
’jig rten gyi raṅ bźin gaṅ yin pa, de raṅ bźin gyis mi rtag pa’o źes bya ba smos te, raṅ bźin
źes bya ba daṅ mtshan ñid ces bya ba ni don gcig go.de la med pa’i don ni mi rtag pa’i
don te, kun brtags kyi mtshan ñid ri boṅ gi rva bźin dus thams cad du med pas kun brtags
raṅ bźin med pa gaṅ yin pa, de ni mi rtag pa’o źes bya’o. raṅ bźin gyis sdug bsṅal ba’o źes
bya ba la yaṅ dag pa ma yin par kun rtog pa’i don ni raṅ bźin gyis sdug bsṅal ba’i don to.
de’aṅ gźan gyi dbaṅ gi mtshan ñid do. de bas na gźan gyi dbaṅ gis ji ltar ji ltar gzuṅ
ba daṅ ’dzin par kun rtog par byed pa, de tsam du sdug bsṅal ba’i raṅ bźin du ’gyur te, sdug
bsṅal rnam pa sna tshogs ’byuṅ ba’i rgyur ’gyur ro. raṅ bźin gyis stoṅ pa, raṅ bźin gyis
bdag med pa’o źes bya ba la, yoṅs su rtog pa tsam ñid yod pa’i don ni bdag med pa’i don
te, des na sems tsam yod kyi dṅos po gźan med par ston to. des bas na yoṅs su rtog gźan gyi
dbaṅ tsam ni yod kyaṅ, chos su brtags pa’i dṅos po ni med pas na raṅ bźin gyis stoṅ pa źes
bya’o. gaṅ zag tu brtags pa’i dṅos po med pas na raṅ bźin gyis bdag med pa’o źes bya’o.
raṅ bźin gyis źi ba ste źes bya ba la gaṅ zag daṅ chos su rnam par rtog pa ñe bar źi ba’i
don tam, de dag spaṅs pa’i don ni raṅ bźin gyis źi ba źes bya ste, de yaṅ dṅos su na yoṅs
su grub pa’i mtshan ñid don dam pa’i chos kyi dbyiṅs rnam par dag pa’o. de la phyin ci log
tu snaṅ ba’i sems ni gñen pos źi bar byas pa med kyi, raṅ bźin gyis skye ba med pa daṅ,
’byuṅ ba med par gnas pa’i phyir ro. de ltar mi rtag pa’i raṅ bźin gaṅ yin pa nas źi ba’i
bar gyi raṅ bźin gaṅ yin pa, ’jig rten gyi raṅ bźin yaṅ de yin te, de dag gi raṅ bźin tha
dad pa med par śes na byaṅ chub sems dpa’i phuṅ po la mkhas pa źes bya’o – "The meaning of
impermanent is the meaning of non-existent (asadartho ’nityārthaḥ): the imagined character
(parikalpitalakṣaṇa) is entirely (sarvatra) non-existent (asad) like a hare’s horn (śaśaviṣāṇa)
and thus imagined (parikalpita), and without own being (niḥsvabhāva), this is [the
meaning of] ‘impermanent’ (tad anityam iti). The sūtra says ’essentially suffering’: the
meaning of imagining the inexistent is the meaning of ‘essentially suffering’ (svabhāvena
duḥkha ity abhūtaparikalpārthaḥ svabhāvena duḥkhārthaḥ), and that is the dependent character
(paratantralakṣaṇam). Thus, to the extent the dependent imagines object and subject, to
that extent it appears as having the essence of suffering (tasmāt paratantro yathā yathā
grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ parikalpayati tāvad duḥkhasvabhāvo bhavati), that is, it becomes the cause
of various [kinds of] suffering (nānāduḥkhahetur bhavati). The sūtra says ’essentially empty,
essentially selfless’: the meaning of ’nothing but imagination’ is the meaning of ’selfless’,
thus it teaches ’nothing but thought’, no other being (svabhāvena śūnyaḥ svabhāvenānātmeti
parikalpamātrasyaiva bhāvārtho ’nātmārthas, tena cittamātraṃ nānyabhāvaṃ deśayati).
Thus, though imagination, as dependent, exists, a thing constructed as a moment of existence
do not exist: hence the sūtra says ’essentially empty’; a thing constructed as a person
does not exist: hence the sūtra says ’essentially selfless’ (tasmāt parikalpaḥ paratantro
’sti, dharme kalpito bhāvas tu nāsti, svabhāvena śūnya iti, pudgale kalpito bhāvo nāsti,
svabhāvenānātmeti). The sūtra says ’essentially in peace’, meaning appeasement of thought-constructions
concerning persons and moments of existence, or, ’essentially in peace’
means giving them up (svabhāvena śānta iti pudgaladharmavikalpopaśamārtho vā teṣāṃ prahāṇārtho
vā svabhāvena śānta iti); and further, it really means the absolute characteristic,
the highest meaning, the pure sphere of all moments of existence (tat punar vastutaḥ pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ
paramārtho viśuddhadharmadhātuḥ). There thought appearing as false is not
appeased by an antidote, as it is essentially unoriginated, staying unborn (tatra na viparītāvabhāsaṃ
cittaṃ pratipakṣeṇa śamitam, svabhāvenānutpādam ajātam avasthitam); and thus the
essence of impermanence and so on, up to the essence of peace, is also the essence of the
world (evaṃ yo ’nityasvabhāvo yāvac chāntasvabhāvaḥ so ’pi lokasvabhavaḥ). Knowledge of
the undivided essence of these things is the bodhisattva’s skill with the parts of personality
(teṣām abhinnasvabhāvajñānaṃ bodhisattvasya skandhakauśalyam).Cf. Msa. p. 1493-12:kaḥ
punar anityārtho yāvac chāntārthaḥ ity āha /asadartho vikalpārthaḥ parikalpārtha eva ca/vikalpopaśamārthaś
ca dhīmatāṃ tac catuṣṭayaṃ//bodhisatvānām asadartho ’nityārthaḥ / yan nityaṃ
nāsti tad anityaṃ teṣāṃ yat parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ / abhūtavikalpārtho duḥkhārtho yat paratantralakṣaṇaṃ
/ parikalpamātrārtho ’nātmārthaḥ / evaśabdenāvadhāraṇaṃ / parikalpita ātmā
nāsti parikalpamātraṃ tv astīti parikalpitalakṣaṇasyābhāvārtho ’nātmārtha ity uktaṃ bhavati
/ vikalpopaśamārthaḥ śāntārthaḥ pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ / kṣaṇabhaṅgārtho ’py anityārtho
veditavyaḥ paratantralakṣaṇasya /Cf. also Sūtrālaṃkāravṛttibhāṣya tsi fol. 132a3ff
ji ltar na mi rtag pa’i don źes bya ba la sogs pa la .... which commentary on Msa also
refers to Akṣ on the topic (cf. introduction, quotations o’, p’, q’ and r’ to Akṣ in Sūtrālaṃkāravṛttibhāṣya).
The content of Sūtrālaṃkāravṛttibhāṣya is similar to ṭ, but cannot be
regarded as a quotation.

phuṅ po la mkhas pa bstan pa’i ’og tu khams la mkhas pa bstan pas na ji ltar bstan pa de bźin
du bśad par ’dod nas de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’i khams la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na źes dris so.
de la khams kyi don ni mtshan ñid ’dzin pa’i don to; yaṅ na rgyu’i don te, khams daṅ sa bon
daṅ rigs ni rgyu’i miṅ gi rnam graṅs te, gaṅ la dmigs nas de bźin gśegs pa’i stobs daṅ
mi ’jigs pa la sogs pa ’byuṅ ba’i rgyu ni khams źes bya la; de rtogs pa’i ye śes ni khams
la mkhas pa źes bya ba’i phyir ro – "The meaning of sphere is the meaning of holding essential
characteristics (tatra dhātvartho lakṣaṇadhāraṇārthaḥ); or, it has the meaning of cause;
sphere, seed and type are synonyms of the word cause (atha vā hetvarthaḥ, dhātur bījaṃ
gotraṃ hetuparyāyāḥ), depending on which cause the powers and intrepidities of the tathāgata
arise (yaṃ hetum ālambya tathāgatabalavaiśāradyādyutpāda iti dhātuḥ). The knowledge which
consists in the understanding of that is skill with the spheres (tadadhigamajñānaṃ dhātukauśalyam
iti)." Cf. Śbh p. 38514-16.

de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’i khams la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na? gaṅ chos kyi dbyiṅs la ’jug pa’i ye
śes so źes bya ba smos te, chos ni ñan thos daṅ raṅ saṅs rgyas daṅ saṅs rgyas kyi chos stobs
daṅ mi ’jigs pa la sogs pa’o. chos de dag skyed pa’i rgyu ni chos kyi dbyiṅs źes bya ste,
don dam pa stoṅ pa’i mtshan ñid do. chos kyi dbyiṅs de rtogs pa’i ye śes ni chos kyi dbyiṅs
la ’jug pa’i ye śes źes bya ste, chos kyi dbyiṅs kyaṅ rnam par mi rtog pa’i ye śes kyis
rtogs pas na ye śes kyi sgra ni ’dir rnam par mi rtog pa’i ye śes ñid la bya’o. de ni ’di
skad du bstan pa yin te, mig la sogs pa khams so so’i mtshan ñid dmigs pa daṅ rten lta
bus khoṅ du chud pa ni khams la mkhas par mi ’gyur gyi, gaṅ chos rnams kyi chos kyi dbyiṅs
don dam pa’i mtshan ñid de rnam par mi rtog pa’i ye śes kyis rtogs na khams la mkhas pa yin
no źes ston to.

chos kyi dbyiṅs gaṅ yin pa daṅ ji ltar na chos kyi dbyiṅs la ’jug par ’gyur ba bstan pa’i phyir
chos kyi dbyiṅs sa’i khams yin mod kyi, chos kyi dbyiṅs sra ba’i mtshan ñid ni ma yin
no źes bya ba smos te, don dam par sa’i khams kyaṅ ṅo bo ñid kyis stoṅ pas chos kyi dbyiṅs
daṅ tha mi dad pa’i phyir chos kyi dbyiṅs sa’i khams yin no; gal te chos kyi dbyiṅs sa’i
khams yin na, sa’i khams sra ba’i mtshan ñid yin pa bźin du chos kyi dbyiṅs kyaṅ sra ba’i
mtshan ñid yin nam? sñam pa la chos kyi dbyiṅs sra ba’i mtshan ñid ni ma yin no źes bya ba
smos te, sa’i khams ni sa’i raṅ bźin te, de’i raṅ bźin ni raṅ bźin gyis stoṅ pa dben pa yin
pas sra ba ni byis pa so so’i skye bo rnams kyis phyin ci log tu rtogs pa ste, de’i mtshan
ñid ma yin pas na chos kyi dbyiṅs sra ba’i mtshan ñid ni ma yin no źes gsuṅs so. de bźin
du chu’i khams la sogs pa la yaṅ ci rigs par sbyar bar bya’o.The contents of this section,
and the next, are related to the idea of kṛtsnāyatana and the exercise of meditation to
see the whole of reality in the particular elements. Cf. Daśa § 42: sarvadhātūn pṛthivīdhātāv
adhimucya sarvam api pṛthivīdhātur evaikadhātur bhavati, etc., and further references
in Edg. s. v.

chos kyi dbyiṅs gzugs kyi khams yin mod kyi, chos kyi dbyiṅs mig gi rnam par śes pas rnam par
rig par bya ba’i mtshan ñid ni ma yin no źes bya ba daṅ ’og nas chos kyi dbyiṅs gzugs kyi
khams yin mod kyi, gzugs su rnam par rig pa’i mtshan ñid ma yin no źes bya ba gñis la goṅ
mas ni mig gi yul gyi bya ba mi byed pa ston te, ’og mas ni gzugs kyi mtshan ñid mi ’dzin
pa bstan te, de bźin du sgra la sogs par yaṅ ci rigs par sbyar ro.V. the preceding note.

ci’i phyir de mtshuṅs śe na źes bya ba ni bdag gi khams nas chos thams cad kyi khams kyi bar
rnam pa sna tshogs su gnas na ci’i phyir de dag mtshuṅs śe na źes bya ba’i tha tshig go.

stoṅ pa ñid du mtshuṅs pas na de ni mtshuṅs pa’o źes bya ba la gaṅ zag gi dṅos po daṅ chos kyi
dṅos po raṅ bźin med pa ni stoṅ pa ñid de, ji ltar bdag gi khams la gaṅ zag gi dṅos po
med pa daṅ chos kyi dṅos po med pas stoṅ pa yin pa, de bźin du nam mkha’i khams daṅ chos kyi
khams de dag kyaṅ gaṅ zag gi dṅos po med pa daṅ chos kyi dṅos po med de stoṅ pa yin par
’dra bas na chos de dag mtshuṅs pa źes bya’o.mtshan ma med par mtshuṅs pa źes bya ba la de
ltar gaṅ zag daṅ chos kyi dṅos po med pas na sa daṅ, chu daṅ, me daṅ, rluṅ daṅ, zla ba daṅ,
ñi ma daṅ, ri daṅ, rgya mtsho daṅ, chu kluṅ daṅ, mtsho daṅ, dgon pa daṅ, phyogs daṅ, yul
la sogs pa’i dṅos po mtshan ma so sor chad pa’i dṅos po rnams yod pa ma yin pas na mtshan
ma med pa źes bya’o.de ltar na mtshan ma med pas na khams gsum thams cad khams gsum gyi
rnam par mi snaṅ ba daṅ, mya ṅan las ’das pa yaṅ mya ṅan las ’das pa’i rnam par mi snaṅ ste,
de dag gñi ga la yaṅ cuṅ zad kyaṅ ’dod pa med pa ni smon pa med pa’o.las dge ba daṅ mi
dge bas ma bskyed ciṅ, las dge ba daṅ mi dge ba la spyod pa med pa ni mṅon par ’du mi byed
pa’o, ’das pa’i dus su ma skyes pa ni skye ba med pa’o, ma ’oṅs pa’i dus su skye bar ’gyur
ba med pa ni ’byuṅ ba med pa’o, da ltar gyi dus na gaṅ zag daṅ chos kyi dṅos por yod pa
ma yin pa ni dṅos po med pa’o.bdag gi khams nas chos thams cad kyi khams kyi bar dag smos
pa rnams don dam pa’i chos kyi dbyiṅs stoṅ pa ñid du ro gcig pa’i raṅ bźin te, mtshan ñid
so sor mi ’dra ba med pas na chos thams cad tha dad pa med par mtshuṅs pa źes bya’o.de dag
thams cad kyaṅ śes bya daṅ ñon moṅs pa’i sgrib pa daṅ bral ba raṅ bźin gyis ’od gsal źiṅ
dri ma med pa dag par ’dra bas na sgrib pa med par mtshuṅs pa źes bya’o.nam mkha’i khams
ni dmigs pa med pa, raṅ bźin med pa, thogs pa med pa, thams cad du khyab pa yin pa ltar, chos
de dag kyaṅ dmigs par bya ba daṅ byed pa daṅ bral ba, gzuṅ ba daṅ ’dzin pa’i raṅ bźin
daṅ bral ba, thogs pa med ciṅ thams cad du khyab pa yin pas nam mkha’i khams su mtshuṅs pa
źes bya’o.mya ṅan las ’das pa ni ñon moṅs pa thams cad spaṅs pa, phuṅ po rnams ñe bar źi
ba, tshe’i rgyun chad pa, dṅos po’i raṅ bźin thams cad las ’das pa, stoṅ pa ñid kyi raṅ bźin
yin pa, de bźin du chos thams cad kyaṅ de’i raṅ bźin yin pas na mya ṅan las ’das pa’i dbyiṅs
su mtshuṅs pas de dag mtshuṅs pa źes bya’o.

khams la mkhas par rgya cher bstan pa rnams bsdus te bśad pa’i phyir ’dus byas kyi khams la
’jug pa daṅ ’dus ma byas kyi khams la ’jug pa tshad med de źes bya ba la sogs pa smos te,
goṅ du bśad pa’i tshul gyis ’dus byas daṅ ’dus ma byas kyi chos zab ciṅ rgya che ba ’di tsam
mo źes dpag tu mi ruṅ źiṅ, tshad med pa de dag thams cad stoṅ pa ñid du ro gcig par chud
pa de la ’dus byas daṅ ’dus ma byas la ’jug pa źes bya’o.de bas na gaṅ bstan pa de la chos
kyi dbyiṅs kyi tshul gyi sgo nas ’jug pa, ’di ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i khams la mkhas pa
źes dṅos su gsuṅs te, gaṅ ’dus byas daṅ ’dus ma byas kyi chos bstan pa de dag thams cad kyi
chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi raṅ bźin du rtogs pa’i khams la mkhas pa’o źes bstan pa’o. sgo nas
’jug ces bya ba ni chos kyi dbyiṅs rtogs par bya ba’i sgo gzugs la sogs pa’i khams rnams la
bya ste, khams de dag gi raṅ bźin mi dmigs pa ñid chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi tshul rtogs par byed
pa’i sgor dgoṅs pa ste, tshul ni raṅ bźin la bya’o. yaṅ na ’dus byas kyi chos kyaṅ tshad
med pas de dag so so’i raṅ bźin rtogs par bya ba yaṅ tshad med pa la, ’dus ma byas kyi khams
kyaṅ tshad med de, de dag so so’i raṅ bźin rtogs par bya ba la yaṅ tshad med pas na ’dus
byas kyi khams la ’jug pa daṅ ’dus ma byas kyi khams la ’jug pa tshad med pa źes bya’o.
gaṅ bstan pa de la chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi tshul gyi sgo nas ’jug pa, ’di ni byaṅ chub sems
dpa’i khams la mkhas pa źes bya ba la gaṅ bstan pa ni ’dus byas kyi khams daṅ ’dus ma byas
kyi khams tshad med pa bstan pa’o, chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi tshul ni chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi raṅ bźin
te, dri ma med ciṅ thams cad la khyab pa’o, chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi tshul de ñid chos rnams
thams cad rtogs par bya ba’i thabs yin pas na chos kyi dbyiṅs kyi tshul gyi sgo źes bya
ste, sgo de nas chos thams cad stoṅ pa ñid du ro gcig par khoṅ du chud pa ni chos kyi dbyiṅs
kyi tshul gyi sgo nas ’jug pa ste, de ltar źugs na byaṅ chub sems dpa’i khams la mkhas
pa źes bya’o. Cf. Mvy 1720 for dharmadhātusthiti.

khams la mkhas pa’i ’og tu skye mched la mkhas pa bstan te, ji ltar bstan pa bźin du bśad par
’dod nas de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’i skye mched la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na źes bya ba dris so.
sems daṅ sems las byuṅ ba rnams skye źiṅ ’phel ba’i sgo ni skye mched de, skye mched la mkhas
pa ni skye mched la mkhas pa ste, mkhas pa’i sgra ni skye mched kyi raṅ bźin daṅ mtshan
ñid rtogs pa’o. skye mched gaṅ yin pa daṅ ’jig rten na skye mched la mkhas par ’gyur ba
bstan pa’i phyir gaṅ chos kyi skye mched la ’jug pa’i ye śes te źes smos te, skye mched ces
bya ba’i sgra bśad pa daṅ sbyar na skye ba’i gnas ’ba’ źig la mi bya’i, ’du ba’i gnas la
yaṅ bya ste; ’dir yaṅ chos thams cad chos kyi dbyiṅs su ro gcig par ’dus pas na chos kyi
dbyiṅs la chos kyi skye mched ces gsuṅs so. ’jug pa ni rtogs pa la bya ste, chos kyi dbyiṅs
rnam par dag pa ye śes kyis rtogs na skye mched la mkhas pa źes bya’o.

chos kyi skye mched ni mig gi skye mched yin mod kyi, chos kyi skye mched lta ba’i mtshan ñid
ni ma yin źes bya ba la sogs pa’aṅ, mig daṅ chos kyi dbyiṅs gñis stoṅ pa ñid kyi mtshan
ñid du tha mi dad pas na de skad ces bya ste, gźan ni gaṅ du khams bśad pa daṅ ’dra bar rig
par bya’o. yaṅ na mig gi skye mched kyi raṅ bźin stoṅ pa gaṅ yin pa, de ñid chos kyi dbyiṅs
yin te, chos kyi dbyiṅs źes bya ba yaṅ de las gźan med pas na chos kyi skye mched ni mig
gi skye mched yin mod kyi źes bya ba smos so.As an authority on the topic ṭ quotes the
Prajñāpāramitāhṛdayasūtra, fol. 120a3: de bas na śes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa las kyaṅ:
gzugs gaṅ yin pa de ni stoṅ pa’o, stoṅ pa gaṅ yin pa de ni gzugs te źes bya ba la sogs pa
gsuṅs so – "Form is emptiness, emtiness is form", Hṛdaya p. 35: yad rūpaṃ sā śūnyatā, yā
śūnyatā tad rūpam.

skye mched la mkhas pa’i rnam graṅs gźan yaṅ bstan par bźed nas gźan yaṅ skye mched la mkhas
pa ni: mig gi skye mched ni bdag daṅ bdag gis stoṅ ṅo źes bya ba smos te, mig gi skye mched
la sogs pa de dag ñid kyaṅ bdag ma yin la, bdag ces bya ba dbaṅ byed pa gźan gyis yaṅ ma
yin pas bdag gis stoṅ pa bya’o. yaṅ na, gaṅ na med pa de la des stoṅ ste, laṅ kar gśegs
pa las kyaṅ: ri dvags dgra’i mo’i khaṅ bzaṅs ’di phag daṅ lug la sogs pa med pas stoṅ ṅo,
źes gsuṅs te – "... The fields of the eye, etc., themselves are not the self (ātman), and
they are empty of anything belonging to a self (ātmīya) since they do not belong to some other
dominating power being a self (na cātmeti parādhipatyasya). Or, ’That which is not in
a place, of that it is empty’, the Laṅkavatāra says, ’as, for example, there are no pigs
or sheep (Skt. version reads ’elephants, cows or sheep’) in the mansion of Mṛgāramātar’, in
this way there is no self or anything belonging to a self in the field of eye, thus it is
empty."The quotation from Laṅkā p. 7510-12 is: yad yatra nāsti tat tena śūnyam ity ucyate,
tad yathā mahāmate mṛgāramātuḥ prāsāde hastigavaiḍakādyā na santi.’dir yaṅ mig gi skye
mched la bdag daṅ bdag gi med pas na stoṅ pa źes bya ste de bźin du rna ba la sogs pa’i skye
mched la yaṅ sbyar ro.

mig gi skye mched la sogs pa bdag daṅ bdag gis stoṅ par ji ltar khoṅ du chud sñam pa la, ’phags
pa blo gros mi zad pas rigs pas brtags na mig gi skye mched la bdag daṅ bdag gis stoṅ
par yaṅ ma zad kyi, bcom ldan ’das kyis kyaṅ thugs su chud nas gsuṅs pa bstan pa’i phyir bcom
ldan ’das kyis ji skad du: mig ni bdag daṅ bdag gis stoṅ ste, ’di ni de’i raṅ bźin no
źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅs so; ’di ni źes bya ba’i sgra bdag daṅ bdag gis źes bya ba’i tshig
daṅ sbyar te, bdag daṅ bdag gis stoṅ pa ’di ni mig gi skye mched de’i raṅ bźin no źes
bya ba tha tshig go.Saṃyutta IV p. 54: cakkhuṃ kho ānanda suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā...,
the expression is found in Pāli ibid. p. 296-7; Majjhima I p. 279, II p. 263; Paṭisaṃbhidāmagga
I p. 109, II p. 36; Cullaniddesa p. 279; Kathāvatthu p. 67, p. 579; Mahāniddesa p.
222, p. 439.Pañcaviṃśati p. 25820 has cakṣuḥ kulaputra śūnyam ātmanā cātmīyena ca, evaṃ
śrotraṃCf. also the expression in Pras. p. 26212: ātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ tat tasya svabhāva iti.

’di ltar gaṅ skye mched rnams ’bri bar mi byed ciṅ źes bya ba la sogs pa ni goṅ du bśad pa ltar
na mig gi skye mched la sogs pa bdag daṅ bdag gis stoṅ ste, raṅ bźin med pa’i phyir mig
gi skye mched la sogs pa’i sgo nas sems daṅ sems las byuṅ ba rnams mi skye bar dgag ciṅ
dbyer med ces bya ba’i don to; mi dge ba’i chos kyaṅ mi sogs, dge ba’i chos kyaṅ bri ba med
pa źes bya ba ni skye mched raṅ bźin gyis stoṅ pas skye mched kyi sgo nas ’dod chags daṅ
źe sdaṅ la sogs pa mi dge ba’i chos blaṅ bar mi bya la, mi dge ba’i chos rnams ’phel bar
mi byed ces te, dge ba’i chos rnams kyaṅ ’dor bar byed pa ma yin pas na dge ba’i chos kyaṅ
bri bar mi byed pa źes bya’o, de ltar mi dge ba’i chos mi sogs la, dge ba’i chos kyaṅ bri
bar mi byed na, spoṅ ba daṅ spel bar ’gyur bas gñis su ’du śes par mi ’gyur sñam la dge ba
daṅ mi dge ba la ’du śes gñis su mi ’gyur ba, ’di ni źes bya ba la sogs pa smos te, las
daṅ rnam par smin pa chud mi gson pas mi dge ba mi sogs śiṅ dge ba’i chos kyaṅ bri bar mi
byed mod kyi, don dam par dge ba daṅ mi dge ba gñi ga raṅ bźin med par rtogs pas ’di ni dge
ba ’di ni mi dge ba źes ’du śes gñis su mi ’gyur ba ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i skye mched la
mkhas pa źes bya’o.

yaṅ skye mched kyi rnam pa gźan bstan par ’dod nas gźan yaṅ skye mched la mkhas pa ni: mig gi
skye mched kyi ’dod chags kyi gnas daṅ rten ni gzugs kyi skye mched de; gaṅ mig gzugs la
’dod chags daṅ bral bar mthoṅ la, ’dod chags daṅ bral ba’i chos kyaṅ mṅon sum du mi byed
pa, ’di ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i skye mched la mkhas pa źes bya’o źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅs
so. gzugs kha dog mdzes pa dbyibs daṅ ldan pa mthoṅ nas ’dod chags skye bas na mig gi skye
mched kyi ’dod chags kyi gnas daṅ rten ni gzugs kyi skye mched do, mig gis gzugs mthoṅ
nas gzugs la ’dod chags la sogs pa skye bar ’dod chags kyi rgyu naṅ gi dṅos po daṅ phyi’i
dṅos po rnams ṅo bo ñid kyis med pas gzugs la ’dod chags daṅ bral du zin kyaṅ, ’dod chags
daṅ bral ba’i chos źi ba phyogs gcig pa yaṅ mṅon du mi len la gzugs la sogs pa ’khor ba’i
chos kyaṅ mi spoṅ ba ’di ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i skye mched la mkhas pa’o źes bya ba’i don
te, sgra la sogs pa la yaṅ ci rigs par sbyar ro.

skye mched kyi don rgyas par bśad pa bsdus te bstan pa’i phyir ’phags pa’i skye mched daṅ ’phags
pa ma yin pa’i skye mched do źes bya ba smos te, mdor na skye mched ni rnam pa gñis te,
’phags pa’i skye mched daṅ ’phags pa ma yin pa’i skye mched do. de la ñon moṅs pa rnams
las riṅ du soṅ źiṅ ñon moṅs pa spaṅs pa ni ’phags pa ste, de rnams skye źiṅ ’byuṅ ba’i sgo
la ’phags pa’i skye mched ces bya’o. de bas na mdo las kyaṅ: ’phags pa gaṅ źe na? gaṅ ’dod
chags ma lus par spaṅs pa daṅ, źe sdaṅ ma lus par spaṅs pa daṅ, gti mug ma lus par spaṅs
pa’o, źes gsuṅs so. gaṅ ñon moṅs pa rnams ma spaṅs pa ni ’phags pa ma yin pa ste, de dag
skye źiṅ ’byuṅ ba’i sgo ni ’phags pa ma yin pa’i skye mched ces bya’o. de bas na mdo las:
so so’i skye bo gaṅ źe na? gaṅ ’phags pa’i chos rnams ma thob pa ste: ñe bar bsams pas sems
pa daṅ, ñes par bya ba’i las byed pa daṅ, ñes par smra ba brjod pa’o, źes gsuṅs so.de la
’phags pa rnams skye źiṅ ’byuṅ ba’i sgo gaṅ yin pa bstan pa’i phyir ’phags pa’i skye mched
ni gaṅ lam yaṅ dag par bsgrub pa’o źes bya ba smos te, dge ba’i bśes gñen la brten nas
dam pa’i chos ñan pa daṅ, mñan pa rnams gtan la ’bebs śiṅ sems pa daṅ, bsams pa rnams źi gnas
lhag mthoṅ gi sgo nas brten te; daṅ po dran pa ñe bar gźag pa bźi sgom pa daṅ, de nas
dro bar gyur pa’i dus na yaṅ dag pa’i spoṅ ba bźi sgom pa daṅ, de nas spyi bo’i tshe rdzu
’phrul gyi rkaṅ pa bźi sgom pa daṅ, de nas bzod pa’i dus na dbaṅ po lṅa sgom pa daṅ, de nas
’jig rten pa’i chos kyi mchog gi dus na stobs lṅa sgom pa daṅ; de nas mthoṅ ba’i lam la
byaṅ chub kyi yan lag bdun sgom pa daṅ, de nas bsgom pa’i lam na ’phags pa’i lam yan lag brgyad
pa sgom pa ni lam sgrub pa źes bya ste, lam bsgrub pa las ’phags pa rnams skye źiṅ ’byuṅ
bas na lam bsgrub pa ni ’phags pa’i skye mched do.’phags pa ma yin pa skye źiṅ ’byuṅ
ba’i sgo bstan pa’i phyir ’phags pa ma yin pa’i skye mched ni gaṅ lam daṅ mi mthun pa’o źes
gsuṅs te, dge ba’i bśes gñen las dam pa’i chos ñan pa daṅ, bsam pa’am, sgom pa la mi ’jug
pa ni lam daṅ mi mthun pa źes bya’am; yaṅ na źi gnas daṅ lhag mthoṅ phyin ci log tu sgom
pa rnams ni ’phags par ’gyur ba med pas na ’phags pa ma yin pa’i skye mched ces bya’o.yaṅ
na, sems can rnam pa bcu ni lam daṅ mi mthun pa ste, bcu gaṅ źe na?1) rab tu ’bar ba’i sems
can daṅ, 2) dgra’i dbaṅ du soṅ ba’i sems can daṅ, 3) sdug bsṅal gyis gzir ba’i sems can
daṅ, 4) mun pas sgrib pa’i sems can daṅ, 5) lam ṅan par źugs pa’i sems can daṅ, 6) ’chiṅ
ba chen po daṅ ldan pa’i sems can daṅ, 7) zas mchog dug daṅ ’dres pa la źen pa’i sems can
daṅ, 8) lam rab tu stor ba’i sems can daṅ, 9) lam log par źugs pa’i sems can daṅ, 10) ñam
chuṅ ba’i sems can no. de la 1) rab tu ’bar ba’i sems can ni gaṅ ’dod pa’i bde ba la chags
pa rnams so; 2) dgra’i dbaṅ du soṅ ba’i sems can ni dge ba la źugs pa bdud kyis bar chad
byas nas dge ba btaṅ ba rnams so; 3) sdug bsṅal gyis gzir ba’i sems can ni gaṅ sems can dmyal
ba rnams so; 4) mun pas sgrib pa ni rṅon pa la sogs pa log par spyod pa la śin tu źugs
pa rnams te, las kyi rnam par smin pa la myos pa’i phyir ro; 5) lam ṅan par źugs pa’i sems
can ni yoṅs su mya ṅan las mi ’da’ ba’i chos can rnams te, ’khor ba’i lam rgyun mi ’chad
pa’i phyir ro; 6) ’chiṅ ba chen po daṅ ldan pa’i sems can ni lta ba sna tshogs kyi bciṅ ba
dam pos bciṅs pa’i mu stegs can thar pa’i lam log par źugs pa rnams so; 7) zas mchog dug
daṅ ’dres pa la źen pa’i sems can ni sñoms par ’jug pa’i bde ba la chags te, ji ltar kha
zas źim po dug daṅ ’dres pa ’phral du bde ba yaṅ ’chi ba’i rgyur ’gyur ba, de bźin du tiṅ
ṅe ’dzin gyi ro la chags pa yaṅ phyis de las ñams par ’gyur ba’i phyir ro; 8) lam stor ba’i
sems can ni mṅon pa’i ṅa rgyal can rnams te, thar pa’i lam nor ba’i phyir ro; 9) lam log
par źugs pa’i sems can ni ma ṅes pa’i rigs can rnams theg pa chuṅ ṅu’i lam du źugs pa’o;
10) ñam chuṅ ba’i sems can tshogs gñis rdzogs par mi btub pa’i byaṅ chub sems dpa’ rnams te.This
paragraph is quoted from Msa XVII 29-30, p. 1243-15:pradīptān śatruvaśagān duḥkhākrāntāṃs
tamovṛtān /durgamārgasamārūḍān mahābandhanasaṃyutān //29//mahāśanaviṣākrāntalolān mārgapranaṣṭakān
/utpathaprasthitān satvān durbalān karuṇāyate //30//tatra (1) pradīptāḥ kāmarāgeṇa
kāmasukhabhaktāḥ / (2) śatruvaśagā mārakṛtāntarāyāḥ kuśale ’prayuktāḥ / (3) duḥkhākrāntāḥ
duḥkhābhūtā narakādiṣu / (4) tamovṛtā aurabhrikādayo duścaritaikāntikāḥ karmavipākasaṃmūḍhatvāt
/ (5) durgamārgasamārūḍhā aparinirvāṇadharmāṇaḥ saṃsāravartmātyantānupacchedāt
/ (6) mahābandhanasaṃyutā anyatīrthyāḥ mokṣasaṃprasthitā nānākudṛṣṭigāḍhabandhanabaddhatvāt
/ (7) mahāśanaviṣākrāntalolāḥ samāpattisukhasaktāḥ / teṣāṃ hi tat kliṣṭaṃ samāpattisukham
/ yathā mṛṣṭam aśanaṃ viṣākrāntaṃ / tataḥ pracyāvanāt / (8) mārgapraṇaṣṭakā abhimānikā
mokṣamārgabhrāntatvāt / (9) utpathaprasthitā hīnayānaprayuktā aniyatā / (10) durbalā aparipūrṇasaṃbhārā
bodhisatvāḥ / [ity ete daśavidhāḥ satvā bodhisatvakaruṇāyā ālambanaṃ] /de
ni lam daṅ mi mthun pa źes bya’o. lam daṅ mi mthun pas na de dag la ’phral du ’phags par
’gyur ba med pa’i phyir, ’phags pa ma yin pa’i skye mched do.

de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’ lam la gnas nas źes bya ba ni goṅ du bśad pa’i lam de la gnas pa’o.
lam daṅ mi mthun pa la spyod pa’i sems can rnams la sñiṅ rje chen po bskyed ciṅ źes bya
ba la, lam daṅ mi mthun pa la gnas pa’i sems can bcu ba rnams te, sems can de dag la sñiṅ
rje chen po bskyed pa’o. lam gyi skye mched kyaṅ mi ’dor ba źes bya ba ni lam gyi skye mched
las ñams par yaṅ mi ’gyur źes bya ba’i tha tshig ste, de ltar śes pa de ni byaṅ chub sems
dpa’i skye mched la mkhas pa źes bya’o.

skye mched la mkhas pa bśad pa’i ’og tu bden pa la mkhas pa bstan te, ji ltar bstan pa bźin
du bśad par ’dod nas de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa la mkhas pa gaṅ źe na, de la źes bya
ba’i don ni sṅar bśad pa bźin no. gaṅ de bźin gśegs pas gsuṅs śiṅ bśad pa rnams ni phyin
ci ma log pa, ma nor ba de kho na ñid mi slu ba yin pas na bden pa źes bya’o, bden pa de
la mkhas pa bden pa la mkhas pa ste, bden pa’i raṅ bźin daṅ mtshan ñid phyin ci ma log par
rtogs pa’o.Cf. Bbh. p. 29217ff: punar anekavidham avitathārthena tāvad ekam eva satyaṃ.
na dvitīyam asti. dvividham satyam. saṃvṛtisatyaṃ parmārthasatyaṃ ca. trividhaṃ satyaṃ. lakṣaṇasatyaṃ
vāksatyaṃ kriyāsatyaṃ ca. caturvidhaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ yāvan mārgasatyaṃ.

’jug pa bźi ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa la mkhas pa yin te źes bya ba la rtogs pa bźi’am,
śes pa bźi ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa la mkhas pa źes bya ba ste, ’phags pa’i bden
pa bźi rtogs pa la bya bar dgoṅs so. bstan pa daṅ bśad pa’i tshul du khoṅ du chud par bya
ba’i phyir ’jug pa bźi gaṅ źe na źes bya ba la sogs pa smos te, rtogs pa bźi gaṅ źe na źes
bya ba’i tha tshig go, gaṅ ’di sdug bsṅal śes pa daṅ źes bya ba la sogs pas ni bstan pa’i
tshul bśad do.

Interpretations of the Four Truths are presented in ṭ.: de la sdug bsṅal śes pa źes bya ba ni
źes bya ba la sogs pas bśad pa’i tshul bstan to. ci’i phyir ’phags pa’i bden pa bźi bśad
ce na? kun nas ñon moṅs pa daṅ rnam par byaṅ ba’i phyogs kyi ’bras bu daṅ rgyu mdor phyin
ci ma log par bstan pa’i phyir ’phags pa’i bden pa bźi bśad do. de la kun nas ñon moṅs pa’i
’bras bu mdor phyin ci ma log par bstan pa ni sdug bsṅal gyi bden pa’o; kun nas ñon moṅs
pa’i phyogs kyi rgyu mdor phyin ci ma log par bstan pa ni kun ’byuṅ ba’i bden pa’o; rnam
par byaṅ ba’i phyogs kyi ’bras bu mdor phyin ci ma log par bstan pa ni ’gog pa’i bden pa’o,
rnam par byaṅ ba’i phyogs kyi rgyu mdor phyin ci ma log par bstan pa ni lam gyi bden pa’o.
yaṅ na nad daṅ, nad kyi gźi daṅ, nad med pa daṅ, sman lta bur bstan pa’i phyir bden pa
bźi ñid du bśad de, mi maṅ mi ñuṅ źes bya ba sbyar ro. de la nad lta bu ni sdug bsṅal gyi
bden pa’o, nad kyi gźi lta bu ni kun ’byuṅ gyi bden pa’o, nad med pa lta bu ni ’gog pa’i
bden pa’o, sman lta bu ni lam gyi bden pa’o. yaṅ na me daṅ, śiṅ daṅ, me źi ba daṅ, me ’gog
pa’i rgyu lta bu yin pas ’phags pa’i bden pa bstan te, me lta bu ni sdug bsṅal gyi bden pa
ste, me’i gduṅ ba daṅ ’dra bar sdug bsṅal gyi gduṅ ba daṅ ldan pa’i phyir ro, śiṅ lta bu
ni kun ’byuṅ ba’i bden pa ste, śiṅ me skye ba’i rgyu byed pa bźin du kun ’byuṅ ba yaṅ sdug
bsṅal skyed pa’i rgyu byed pa’i phyir ro, me źi ba lta bu ni ’gog pa’i bden pa ste, me’i
gduṅ ba źi ba daṅ ’dra bar sdug bsṅal gyi gduṅ ba źi ba’i phyir ro, me źi ba’i rgyu lta bu
ni lam gyi bden pa ste, ’gog pa thob pa’i rgyur gyur pa’i phyir ro. yaṅ na bu lon daṅ, dbul
ba daṅ, bu lon sbyaṅs pa daṅ, gter lta bu yin pas bden pa bźi’o, bu lon lta bu ni sdug
bsṅal gyi bden pa ste, rtag tu yid mi bde ba’i gduṅ ba daṅ ldan pas so, dbul ba lta bu ni
kun ’byuṅ ba’i bden pa ste, dbul ba’i rgyus bu lon chags pa daṅ ’dra bar kun ’byuṅ ba’i rgyus
sdug bsṅal skyed pa’i phyir ro, bu lon sbyaṅs pa lta bu ni ’gog pa’i bden pa ste, bu
lon sbyaṅs na bu lon gyi mi bde ba med pa bźin du sdug bsṅal rnams med pa’i phyir ro, gter
lta bu ni lam gyi bden pa ste, gter bu lon sbyoṅ ba’i rgyur gyur pa daṅ ’dra bar lam ni ’gog
pa ’thob pa’i rgyur gyur pa’i phyir ro. sdug bsṅal śes pa gaṅ yin pa bstan pa’i phyir
de la sdug bsṅal śes pa źes bya ba ni gaṅ phuṅ po rnams mi skye bar śes pa’o źes bya ba gsuṅs
te, spuṅs śiṅ tshogs su gyur pa’i phyir phuṅ po ste, de’aṅ gzugs daṅ, tshor ba daṅ, ’du
śes daṅ, ’du byed daṅ, rnam par śes pa’i phuṅ pa’o, phuṅ po de dag sgyu ma daṅ gzugs brñan
tsam du snaṅ mod kyi, ṅo bo ñid kyi skye ba med pas na mi skye ba’o, ’di ltar phuṅ po lṅa
rnams las ’phags pa’i ñan thos dag sdug bsṅal ba daṅ mi rtag pa la sogs par rtogs pa ni
ma yin gyi, thog ma nas ṅo bo ñid kyis ma skyes par śes pa ni sdug bsṅal śes pa’o; kun ’byuṅ
ba śes pa bstan pa’i phyir gaṅ sred pa legs par ’joms pa’i śes pa’o źes bya ba smos te,
de la sred pa gaṅ źe na? gaṅ mdo las bcom ldan ’das kyis: yaṅ srid pa ’byuṅ bar byed pa
daṅ, dga’ ba’i ’dod chags daṅ ldan pa daṅ, de dag de dag la mṅon par dga’ ba’i sred pa’o źes
gsuṅs pa’o; de la sred pa ni sgo gsum gyis źugs pa yin te, yaṅ ’byuṅ ba’i srid pa ’dod
pa daṅ, yul ’dod pa’o, de la yaṅ ’byuṅ ba’i srid pa ’dod pa ’di yaṅ srid pa ’dod pa ’byuṅ
ba byed pa yin no, yul ’dod pa ni rnam pa gñis te, yul thob pa rnams la yid bde źiṅ lhag par
chags pa daṅ ldan pa daṅ, yul ma thob pa rnams la kun tu sbyor bar ’dod pa daṅ ldan pa’o,
de la yul thob pa rnams la yid bde źiṅ lhag par chags pa daṅ ldan pa gaṅ yin pa de ni dga’
ba’i ’dod chags daṅ ldan pa źes bya’o, yul ma thob pa rnams la kun tu sbyor bar ’dod pa
daṅ ldan pa gaṅ yin pa de ni de dag la mṅon par dga’ ba źes bya’o; legs pa ’joms pa’i śes
pa ni srid pa de dag ma lus par spaṅ ba’i thabs śes pa ste, ’joms pa źes bya ba ni spoṅ
ba’i don to; ñan thos dag ltar kun ’byuṅ ba’i bden pa la rgyu daṅ rkyen la sogs par rtogs
pa ni ma yin gyi, sdug bsṅal gyi phuṅ po ’byuṅ ba’i rgyu ’dod chags kyi raṅ bźin sred pa źes
bya ba rab tu spaṅ ba’i thabs śes pa ni kun ’byuṅ ba śes pa źes bya’o. ’gog pa śes pa bstan
pa’i phyir ’gog pa śes pa źes bya ba ni ma rig pa daṅ bag la ñal rnams mi ’byuṅ ba’o
źes gsuṅs te, de yaṅ ma rig pa mi ’byuṅ ba daṅ, bag la ñal rnams mi ’byuṅ ba’o źes bya bar
sbyar ro; de la ma rig pa ni de kho na la kun tu gti mug pa ste, ma rig pa ma lus par spaṅs
nas phyis de’i rgyud la mi skye bar ’gyur ba ni ma rig pa mi ’byuṅ ba’o; bag la ñal gyi
sgras ’dod chags la sogs pa ñon moṅs pa gźan gyi bag la ñal la bya ste, de dag ma lus par
spaṅs nas phyis de’i rgyud la mi skye ba ni bag la ñal rnams mi ’byuṅ ba’o; bag la ñal smos
pas ma rig pa yaṅ smras pa yin mod kyi, ma rig pa ni ñon moṅs pa thams cad ’byuṅ ba’i rgyu
ste, gtso bo yin par bstan pa’i phyir miṅ gis bkar te smos te; yaṅ na ma rig pa bag la
ñal bas na ma rig pas bag la ñal te, ma rig pa la sogs pa’i bag la ñal rnams thog ma nas
ma skyes pas mtha’ ’gag pa yaṅ med pa ni ma rig pa daṅ bag la ñal rnams mi ’byuṅ ba źes bya’o;
’gog pa’i bden pa la ’phags pa ñan thos dag ltar źi ba daṅ gya nom pa la sogs pa rtog
pa ni ma yin gyi, ma rig pa la sogs pa bag la ñal rnams thog ma nas ma skyes pas mtha’ ’gag
pa yaṅ med par śes pa ni ’gog pa źes bya’o. lam śes pa bstan pa’i phyir lam śes pa źes
bya ba ni mñam pa ñid du gyur pa’i chos thams cad la sgro mi ’dogs pa ste źes bya ba smos
te, lam gyi bden pa la yaṅ ’phags pa ñan thos pa dag ltar ñon moṅs pa’i phyogs spoṅ ba daṅ
rnam par byaṅ ba’i phyogs sgrub par rtogs pa ni ma yin gyi, ñon moṅs pa daṅ rnam par byaṅ
ba’i phyogs gñi ga yaṅ mñam pa ñid du rtogs pas de ñid la sgro ’dogs pa med pa ni lam śes
pa źes bya’o; yaṅ na chos thams cad ni nam mkha’ daṅ ’dra bar ro gcig pas mñam pa ñid du
gyur pa’o, mñam pa ñid du gyur pa’i chos de dag las spaṅ ba daṅ, blaṅ ba daṅ, rtag pa daṅ,
mi rtag pa daṅ, yod pa daṅ, med pa daṅ, skye ba daṅ, mi skye ba la sogs par sgro mi ’dogs
pa ni lam śes pa’o. de ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa śes pa’o źes bya ba la bden pa bźi
po goṅ du bśad pa lta bu’i tshul du śes pa ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa śes pa źes bya’o.

byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa śes pa de dag kyaṅ śes rab daṅ thabs kyis yoṅs su zin pa yin par
bstan pa’i phyir de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’ ’phags pa’i bden pa bźi po de dag la de lta bur
śes rab daṅ ye śes kyis rab tu śes kyaṅ źes bya ba la sogs pa smos te, ’phags par ’gyur
ba’i bden pa yin pas na ’phags pa’i bden pa’am, ’phags pa rnams kyis bden pa de dag de kho
na lta bu yin par bden pa’i sgo nas yaṅ dag pa ji lta ba bźin mkhyen ciṅ gzigs kyi, byis
pa rnams kyis yaṅ dag pa ji lta ba bźin du mi śes mi mthoṅ bas na, de’i phyir ’phags pa bden
pa rnams źes bya’o. yaṅ na ’phags pa saṅs rgyas daṅ saṅs rgyas kyi ñan thos rnams kyis
bśad pa’i bden pa yin pas na ’phags pa’i bden pa ste, ’phags pa ma yin pas bśad rnams kyaṅ
de bźin gśegs pa rnams kyi byin gyi rlabs kyis ’chad pa daṅ, bcom ldan ’das kyi bstan pa
’dzin pa daṅ, ’phags par ’gyur ba’i rgyu byed pas na ’phags pa’i bden pa źes bya’o. de lta
bur źes bya ba ni goṅ du bstan pa lta bur ro. raṅ gi mtshan ñid rtogs pa ni śes rab yin
la, spyi’i mtshan ñid rtogs pa ni ye śes so, yaṅ na skabs ’dir śes rab bśad pas śes rab ñid,
goṅ du bśad pa lta bu’i tshul du stoṅ par rtogs pa la ye śes źes bya ste, ’di ni śes rab
kyis zin pa bstan to. sems can la lta ba’i phyir mṅon sum du mi byed ciṅ sems can rnams
kyaṅ yoṅs su smin par byed de źes bya ba ni de ltar bden pa bźi rtogs kyaṅ sñiṅ rje chen pos
sems can gyi don gyi phyir ñan thos bźin du źi ba phyogs gcig pa’i mya ṅan las ’das pa
mṅon du mi byed ciṅ thabs rnam pa sna tshogs kyis sems can smin par yaṅ byed do, ’di ni thabs
kyis zin par bstan to. ’di ni byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa la mkhas pa’o źes bya ba la
thabs daṅ śes rab kyis yoṅs su zin pa goṅ du bśad pa lta bur bden pa bźi po śes pa ’di ni
byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa la mkhas pa’o – "... Understanding the individual characteristics
(svalakṣaṇa) is insight (prajñā), while understanding the general characteristics (sāmānyalakṣaṇa)
is knowledge (jñāna). In this case, however, the insight mentioned is just
insight, and knowledge is the understanding of emptiness (śūnyatādhigama) in the way explained
above; it is taught that this [viz. the bodhisattva’s way of behaviour] is included in
insight (prajñāparigṛhīta). He does not realize them – for the sake of living beings - but
matures living beings, the sūtra says; though understanding the four truths he does not
realize extinction (nirvāṇa) – exclusively (ekāntika) peaceful (śānta) – like the disciples
(śrāvaka), so that, with great compassion for the sake of living beings, he may mature
living beings with expedient means; it is taught that this [viz. the bodhisattva’s way of
behaviour] is included in expedient means (upāyaparigṛhīta). This is called the bodhisattva’s
skill with truths, it says, the knowledge of the four truths as described above is included
in insight and expedient means (prajñopāyaparigṛhīta)."

bden pa’i mtshan ñid gźan yaṅ bstan par bźed nas gźan yaṅ byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa rnam
pa gsum ste źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅs te, gźan yaṅ źes bya ba ni goṅ du bden pa bźi bśad
pa tsam du yaṅ ma zad kyi, bden pa rnam pa gsum yaṅ yod de źes bya bar dgoṅs pa’o. ’dir yaṅ
bstan pa daṅ bśad pa’i tshul du rig par bya ste, gaṅ ’di kun rdzob kyi bden pa daṅ źes
bya ba la sogs pa ni bstan pa’i tshul lo, de la kun rdzob kyi bden pa gaṅ źe na źes bya ba
la sogs pa ni bśad pa’i tshul lo. kun rdzob ñid bden pa yin pas kun rdzob kyi bden pa ste,
sgyu ma daṅ smyig rgyu tsam ji ltar snaṅ ba rnams de bźin du bya ba byed pa’i phyir ro.
don dam pa ñid bden pa yin pas don dam pa’i bden pa ste, mi slu ba’i bdag ñid du pyin ci ma
log pa’i phyir ro. mtshan ñid bden pa yin pas na mtshan ñid kyi bden pa yin pa ste, chos
thams cad ro gcig par ma nor ba’i phyir ro.ci’i phyir bden pa rnam pa gsum bśad ce na? sems
can rnam pa gsum gyi don du dgoṅs nas bden pa rnam pa gsum bśad de, sems can rnam pa gsum
ni yoṅs su ma smin pa’i sems can daṅ, yoṅs su smin pa’i sems can daṅ, chos ñid zab mo la
kun tu mgo rmoṅs pa’i sems can no. de la yoṅs su ma smin pa’i sems can gyi don kun rdzob
kyi bden pa bstan to; yoṅs su smin pa’i sems can gyi don du don dam pa’i bden pa bstan to;
chos ñid zab mo la kun tu mgo rmoṅs pa’i sems can gyi don du mtshan ñid kyi bden pa bstan
to – "Why are the truths explained as being of three kinds? Having in mind the good of three
kinds of beings (trividhasattvārthaṃ saṃdhāya) the truths are explained as being of three
kinds, and those three kinds of beings are (1) the beings who are not matured (aparipācita),
(2) those who are matured (paripācita), and (3) those who are deluded as to the deep
nature of the moments of existence (gaṃbhīradharmatā)......de bas na ’phags pa sa bcu’i
mdo las kyaṅ: sems can gźan gyi bsam pa ji lta ba bźin du tshim par byed pas kyaṅ kun rdzob
kyi bden pa rab tu śes so, bgrod pa gcig pu la yaṅ dag par gźol bas don dam pa’i bden pa
rab tu śes so, raṅ daṅ spyi’i mtshan ñid rtogs pas mtshan ñid kyi bden pa rab tu śes so
źes gsuṅs so – "Thus it is also said in the noble Daśabhūmikasūtra: ’He knows the concealed
truth to please other beings according to their intentions, he knows the highest truth to
attain the one principle, he knows the truth of essential characteristics to understand
individual and general characteristics’."The quotation is from Dbh. p. 4223-26: sa parasatvānāṃ
yathāśayasaṃtoṣaṇāt saṃvṛtisatyam prajānāti, ekanayasamavasaraṇāt paramārthasatyam prajānāti,
svasāmānyalakṣaṇānubodhāl lakṣaṇasatyam prajānāti. Dbh., in the sections 5c-d, also
deals with satyakauśalya.

de la kun rdzob kyi bden pa bśad par bźed nas ’jig rten gyi tha sñad daṅ, yi ge daṅ, sgra daṅ,
brdas bstan pa ji sñed pa źes gsuṅs te, ji sñed pa źes bya ba’i sgra thams cad daṅ sbyar
te, ’jig rten gyi tha sñad ji sñed pa daṅ, yi ges bstan pa ji sñed pa daṅ, sgras bstan pa
ji sñed pa daṅ, brdas bstan pa ji sñed pa źes bya bar sbyar ro. ji sñed kyi sgra ni ji tsam
yod pa’i don draṅs te, ’jig rten gyi tha sñad ji tsam yod pa źes bya ba’i tha tshig go.
de la ’jig rten gyi tha sñad ni bstan pa’o; lhag ma rnams ni bśad pa ste: yi ge a daṅ ka
la sogs pa gsuṅ rab kyi luṅ daṅ ’brel pa rnams so; sgra ni gsuṅ rab kyi luṅ daṅ ’brel pa
’du byed mi rtag ces bya ba la sogs pa’i tshig gi rkaṅ pa rnams so; brda ni don ston par nus
śiṅ khoṅ du chud par nus pa’i tshig gi rkaṅ pa rnams so. ji sñed ces bya ba’i tshig gi
luṅ ’ba’ źig gi ma yin gyi, ’jig rten gyi yig ge daṅ sgra la sogs pa ci tsam yod pa rnams
kyaṅ sdud de, de yaṅ yid kyi daṅ ṅag gi sgo nas ston pa rnam pa gñis so; de la yid kyis ston
pa ni ji ltar brgya byin la yid kyis chos mṅon par bśad pa daṅ, de dag gis kyaṅ raṅ gi
the tshom yid la btags pa daṅ, lan kyaṅ yid kyis tshigs su bcad pas glan no, mdo de daṅ de
dag las ’byuṅ ba lta bu’o; ṅag gis bstan pa ni tshig gi rig byed rnam pa sna tshogs ñan pa’i
gaṅ zag rnams kyi rna bar soṅ ba rnams so, de dag gis ni mdor na ’di skad du: gdul bar
bya ba’i sems can rnams kyi dbaṅ du ji tsam du tha sñad brjod pa thams cad kun rdzob kyi
bden pa yin no, źes bstan te, de ltar dkon mchog sprin gyi mdo las kyaṅ: rigs kyi bu, chos
bcu daṅ ldan na byaṅ chub sems dpa’ kun rdzob la mkhas pa rnams yin no, bcu gaṅ źe na? ’di
lta ste, gzug su’aṅ ’dogs la, don dam par na gzugs su’aṅ mi dmigs śiṅ mi chags so; de bźin
du tshor ba daṅ, ’du śes daṅ, ’du byed daṅ, rnam par śes par kyaṅ ’dogs la, don dam par
na rnam par śes par kyaṅ mi dmigs śiṅ mṅon par mi chags so źes bya ba nas saṅs rgyas kyi
chos rnams su’aṅ ’dogs la, don dam par na saṅs rgyas kyi chos su yaṅ mi dmigs śiṅ mṅon par
mi chags so; byaṅ chub tu’aṅ ’dogs la, byaṅ chub sems dpar yaṅ mi dmigs śiṅ de la mṅon par
mi chags so; rigs kyi bu, de lta bas na miṅ daṅ, ’dogs pa daṅ, tha sñad de ni kun rdzob
ces bya ste, kun rdzob kyi chos rnams la don dam pa med kyi, kun rdzob kyi chos med par yaṅ
don dam pa bstan par mi nus so źes gsuṅs so.125b4-126a2: de las bzog pa ni don dam pa ste,
de bstan par bźed nas don dam pa’i bden pa ni gaṅ la sems kyi rgyu ba yaṅ med pa ste, yi
ge lta ci smos źes bya ba gsuṅ so. don dam pa ni skye ba daṅ, mi skye ba daṅ, bsam du yod
pa daṅ, bsam du med pa daṅ, rtag pa daṅ, mi rtag pa daṅ, brjod du yod pa daṅ, brjod du med
pa daṅ, ’gog pa daṅ, mi ’gog pa daṅ, śes par ruṅ ba daṅ, śes par mi ruṅ ba daṅ, rtag pa
daṅ, mi rtag pa źes bya ba la sogs pa’i spros pa thams cad las ’das pa yin pas sems kyi rgyu
ba med pa źes bya ste, sems daṅ sems las byuṅ ba’i spyod yul las ’das te, don dam pa daṅ
de’i rig pa’i ye śes gñis su med pa’i phyir sems kyi yul du yaṅ mi ’gyur na yi ge lta ci
smos źes bya ba’i tha tshig go. de bas na dkon mchog sprin gyi mdo las kyaṅ: rigs kyi bu,
chos bcu daṅ ldan na byaṅ chub sems dpa’ don dam pa la mkhas pa rnams yin no, bcu gaṅ źe
na? ’di lta ste, mi skye ba’i chos ñid daṅ ldan pa rnams yin, mi ’gog pa’i chos ñid daṅ,
mi ’jig pa’i chos ñid daṅ, mi len mi ’dor ba’i chos ñid daṅ, tshig gi spyod yul las yaṅ dag
par ’das pa’i chos ñid daṅ, smrar med pa’i chos ñid daṅ, spros pa med pa’i chos ñid daṅ,
brjod du med pa’i chos ñid daṅ, źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅ so.The Sanskrit fragment in Pras.
p. 3742 reads jñānasya; cittasya is, however, confirmed by T1 p. 197b9 心行 xin xing, and
also by Satyadvayavibhaṅgavṛtti (cf. Masamichi Ichigo in Taishūkyō no sōgōteki kenkyū p.
107): gaṅ la sems rgyu ba yaṅ med na).

de la mtshan ñid kyi bden pa bśad par bźed nas mtshan ñid kyi bden pa gaṅ źe na źes khoṅ nas
dris pa daṅ mtshan ñid kyi bden pa ni: gaṅ ’di mtshan ñid thams cad mtshan ñid gcig pa ste
źes bya ba gsuṅs te, ’di ltar sa’i mtshan ñid sra ba daṅ, chu’i mtshan ñid gśer ba daṅ,
źes bya ba nas gzugs kyi mtshan ñid thogs pa daṅ bcas pa daṅ, tshor ba’i mtshan ñid myoṅ bar
byed pa źes bya ba la sogs pa thams cad ni mtshan ñid gcig pa ste, de bźin ñid kyi mtshan
ñid du ’dra ba’i phyir ro. mtshan ñid gcig po de’i mtshan ñid kyaṅ gaṅ źe na? de’i phyir
mtshan ñid gcig po yaṅ mtshan ñid med pa’o źes bya ba gsuṅs te, de bźin ñid de ni mtshan
ñid du bgraṅ ba thams cad las ’das pa ste, skye ba daṅ, ’gag pa daṅ, yod pa daṅ, med pa daṅ,
rtag pa daṅ, mi rtag pa la sogs pa gaṅ gi mtshan ñid kyaṅ ma yin pas na mtshan ñid med
pa’o. mtshan ñid med pa’i bden pa ’di yaṅ don dam pa’i bden pa ñid de, de la gźan ma yin
na ci’i phyir don dam pa’i bden pa źes bya ba daṅ mtshan ñid kyi bden pa źes bya ba gñis su
bśad? de ni bden te, de las gźan ma yin mod kyi, ’dis don dam pa mtshon par byed, khoṅ du
chud par byed pas na mtshan ñid kyi bden pa ste. de bas na mtshan ñid kyi bden pa ni don
dam pa la ’jug pa’i sgo lta bur gźag go. yaṅ na sems can rnam pa gsum gyi don gyi phyir bden
pa rnam pa gsum bśad de, ñes pa med do.byaṅ chub sems dpa’i bden pa rnam pa gsum yaṅ thabs
daṅ śes rab kyis yoṅs su zin pa yin te, de bstan pa’i phyir de la byaṅ chub sems dpa’
kun rdzob kyi bden pa bstan pas kyaṅ yoṅs su mi skyo ba źes bya ba la sogs pa gsuṅs te, sems
can gyi don du byaṅ chub sems dpa’ kun rdzob kyi bden pa tha sñad daṅ, yi ge daṅ, brda
la sogs pa gźan la bstan kyaṅ kun rdzob kyi bden pa la yid ’byuṅ źiṅ skyo ba med de, śes
rab kyis zin pas de dag sgyu ma daṅ, rmi lam daṅ, gzugs brñan lta bur dṅos po med par khoṅ
du chud pa’i phyir ro. don dam pa’i bden pa mṅon sum du byed par yaṅ mi ltuṅ źes bya ba ni
thabs kyis yoṅs su zin pas ji ltar ’phags pa ñan thos rnams źi ba phyogs gcig pa’i mya ṅan
las ’das pa la gnas pa lta bur de bźin ñid ’ba’ źig gi phyogs su yaṅ gnas par mi byed ces
bya ba’i don to.mtshan ñid kyi bden pa gcig tu rtogs kyaṅ sems can rnams yoṅs su smin par
